AIR-MCQ-03.s: A 27-year-old woman develops itchy wheals over the trunk within 20 minutes of taking a first dose of amoxicillin. The lesions are transient, each lasting less than 24 hours, and resolve completely without scarring. Which immunologic mechanism best explains this reaction?
AIR-MCQ-03.a: Type I — IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation
AIR-MCQ-03.p: ผื่นลมพิษย้ายที่ ตุ่มละไม่เกิน 24 ชม. + เกิดเร็ว = **type I**; ผื่นคงที่นานหลายวันหรือหลุดลอก = **type IV**

AIR-OLD-01.s: A 32-year-old man develops generalized itchy wheals within 30 minutes of taking an oral antibiotic. The lesions blanch on pressure and each individual wheal disappears within a few hours. Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is this?

AIR-MCQ-01.s: A 24-year-old woman develops generalized urticaria, lip swelling, hoarseness and wheezing 10 minutes after eating shrimp. PE: T 37.0 C, PR 124/min, RR 28/min, BP 82/50 mmHg, SpO2 93% room air, diffuse wheezing and angioedema of the lips. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
AIR-MCQ-01.a: Intramuscular adrenaline 0.3–0.5 mg (1:1,000) into the anterolateral thigh
AIR-MCQ-01.p: เห็น anaphylaxis ให้ **adrenaline IM ต้นขาด้านนอกทันที** — antihistamine/steroid เป็นแค่ตัวประกอบ ความล่าช้าของ adrenaline คือปัจจัยเดียวที่สัมพันธ์กับการเสียชีวิต

AIR-OLD-03.s: A 28-year-old woman develops itching, generalized flushing, wheezing and hypotension 15 minutes after eating at a restaurant. Which is the most appropriate first drug and route?

AIR-MCQ-02.s: A 19-year-old man is observed for 6 hours after a severe anaphylactic reaction to peanuts that responded to intramuscular adrenaline. He is now asymptomatic with normal vital signs and is ready for discharge. Which of the following is the most appropriate discharge plan?
AIR-MCQ-02.a: Prescribe an adrenaline auto-injector with training, a written action plan and allergist referral
AIR-MCQ-02.p: ออกจาก ER ต้องได้ **ปากกา adrenaline + action plan + นัด allergist** — ไม่ใช่ antihistamine กินทุกวัน

AIR-OLD-02.s: A patient who survived anaphylactic shock from a bee sting is being discharged. Which of the following is the most appropriate advice?
AIR-OLD-02.a: Carry an adrenaline auto-injector at all times and use it immediately when symptoms begin

AIR-MCQ-04.s: A 32-year-old woman has had daily itchy wheals for 8 months. Individual lesions last less than 24 hours and leave no bruising. She has no fever, arthralgia or weight loss, and no identifiable trigger. A standard dose of a second-generation antihistamine gives only partial relief. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
AIR-MCQ-04.a: Increase the second-generation antihistamine up to fourfold the standard dose
AIR-MCQ-04.p: ลมพิษเรื้อรังคุมไม่อยู่ ให้ **เพิ่มขนาด antihistamine ได้ถึง 4 เท่า** ก่อนคิดถึง steroid; ตุ่มอยู่เกิน 24 ชม. + ทิ้งรอยจ้ำ = urticarial vasculitis ต้อง biopsy

AIR-MCQ-05.s: A 58-year-old man with hypertension treated with enalapril for 2 years presents with painless swelling of the lips and tongue for 6 hours. There is no urticaria and no itching. He denies new foods or drugs. PE: T 37.0 C, PR 88/min, BP 150/90 mmHg, no wheeze, no rash, tongue swollen without airway compromise at present. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
AIR-MCQ-05.a: Stop enalapril permanently, monitor the airway closely and switch to a different antihypertensive class
AIR-MCQ-05.p: **บวมโดยไม่มีลมพิษ ไม่คัน = bradykinin** — นึกถึง ACEI และ hereditary angioedema ไว้ก่อน, ยาแก้แพ้กับสเตียรอยด์ไม่ช่วย

AIR-MCQ-07.s: A 46-year-old woman develops fever and a painful rash 3 weeks after starting phenytoin. PE: T 38.8 C, dusky targetoid macules coalescing over the trunk with epidermal detachment of about 12% of body surface area, positive Nikolsky sign, erosions of the lips, oral mucosa and conjunctivae. Which of the following is the most important immediate management?
AIR-MCQ-07.a: Stop phenytoin immediately and transfer for intensive supportive care with fluid, wound and eye care
AIR-MCQ-07.p: SJS/TEN: **หยุดยาต้นเหตุทันที = การรักษาที่สำคัญที่สุด** แล้วดูแลแบบแผลไฟไหม้ + ปรึกษาจักษุวันแรก

AIR-OLD-05.s: A patient taking allopurinol develops a widespread painful rash with erosions of the lips, oral mucosa and conjunctivae, with skin detachment of about 8% of body surface area. What is the diagnosis?

AIR-MCQ-08.s: A 40-year-old man develops fever and a diffuse maculopapular rash 5 weeks after starting allopurinol. PE: T 39.0 C, generalized morbilliform rash with facial edema and cervical lymphadenopathy. Lab: WBC 14,800/mm3 with eosinophils 18%, atypical lymphocytes present, AST/ALT 320/410 U/L, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL (baseline 1.0). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-MCQ-08.a: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
AIR-MCQ-08.p: ผื่นยา + **eosinophilia + ตับอักเสบ + หน้าบวม** ที่มาช้าเป็นสัปดาห์ = DRESS; ต้องหยุดยาและให้สเตียรอยด์ลดยาว ไม่ใช่ course สั้น

AIR-MCQ-06.s: A 55-year-old Thai man with gout and stage 3 chronic kidney disease is about to start urate-lowering therapy with allopurinol. Which of the following tests should be performed before starting the drug to reduce the risk of severe cutaneous adverse reaction?
AIR-MCQ-06.p: **Allopurinol → B\*58:01 · Carbamazepine → B\*15:02 · Abacavir → B\*57:01** ท่องสามคู่นี้ให้ขึ้นใจ

AIR-OLD-04.s: A patient develops Stevens-Johnson syndrome after receiving allopurinol. Testing for which allele would have identified the risk before prescribing?

AIR-MCQ-09.s: A 30-year-old woman needs treatment for acute pyelonephritis. Her record says 'penicillin allergy' because she had a non-pruritic maculopapular rash at age 5 while taking amoxicillin for pharyngitis, with no swelling, no breathing difficulty and no hospitalization. Which of the following statements is most accurate?
AIR-MCQ-09.a: A childhood benign maculopapular rash is a low-risk history, and she can receive a cephalosporin or be evaluated for penicillin de-labeling
AIR-MCQ-09.p: ป้าย 'แพ้ penicillin' ต้อง **ซักให้ได้ว่าอาการคืออะไร เมื่อไร** — ผื่นราบตอนเด็ก = low risk ให้ beta-lactam ต่อได้ แต่ SJS/TEN หรือ DRESS = ห้ามตลอดชีวิต

AIR-MCQ-10.s: A 62-year-old woman receiving packed red cells develops fever 39.0 C, chills, flank pain and dark red urine 15 minutes after the transfusion starts. BP 88/54 mmHg, PR 124/min. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate action?
AIR-MCQ-10.a: Stop the transfusion immediately, keep the intravenous line open with normal saline and send blood and the unit for investigation
AIR-MCQ-10.p: ให้เลือดแล้ว **ไข้ + ปวดหลัง + ปัสสาวะดำ = AHTR หยุดทันที**; ไข้อย่างเดียวไม่มีปัสสาวะผิดปกติ = FNHTR

AIR-OLD-07.s: A patient develops fever and chills 2 hours into a red cell transfusion. Urine colour is normal, blood pressure is stable and there is no flank pain. What is the most likely diagnosis and the measure to prevent recurrence?
AIR-OLD-07.a: Febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reaction; use leukocyte-reduced blood components in future transfusions

AIR-MCQ-11.s: A 28-year-old man with thalassemia develops itchy urticarial wheals over the chest 15 minutes into a packed red cell transfusion. He has no fever, no dyspnea, normal blood pressure and normal urine colour. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
AIR-MCQ-11.a: Pause the transfusion, give an antihistamine, and resume slowly if the wheals resolve and no other symptom appears
AIR-MCQ-11.p: ผื่นลมพิษล้วนระหว่างให้เลือด = allergic reaction — **ชนิดเดียวที่ให้เลือดต่อได้** หลังผื่นยุบ

AIR-OLD-06.s: Fifteen minutes after a packed red cell transfusion is started, a patient develops itchy urticarial wheals only, with no fever, no hypotension and normal urine colour. What is the most likely type of reaction?

AIR-OLD-08.s: A 25-year-old woman has anemia and jaundice. Blood smear shows spherocytes and polychromasia; direct Coombs test is positive. Which additional investigation should be sent to look for an underlying cause?

AIR-OLD-09.s: A newly diagnosed HIV-positive man has isolated thrombocytopenia (platelet 80,000/mm3) with normal hemoglobin and white cell count, and no bleeding. What is the most appropriate management?
AIR-OLD-09.a: Start antiretroviral therapy and monitor the platelet count

AIR-OLD-10.s: A young woman presents with easy bruising for 1 week. CBC shows isolated thrombocytopenia with giant platelets on smear; hemoglobin and white cells are normal. Besides a bone marrow study if indicated, which screening tests are most appropriate to look for secondary causes?
AIR-OLD-10.a: Antinuclear antibody, anti-HIV and anti-hepatitis C virus

AIR-MCQ-12.s: A 45-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus takes prednisolone 30 mg daily and azathioprine. She asks about vaccination before the rainy season. Which of the following is most appropriate?
AIR-MCQ-12.a: Give inactivated influenza vaccine now and defer live attenuated vaccines while she is immunosuppressed
AIR-MCQ-12.p: กดภูมิอยู่: **วัคซีนเชื้อตายให้ได้ทันที · วัคซีนเชื้อเป็นห้าม** — และควรวางแผนฉีดเชื้อเป็นให้เสร็จก่อนเริ่มยากดภูมิ 4 สัปดาห์

AIR-OLD-11.s: A patient on long-term prednisolone 30 mg daily for lupus nephritis asks about vaccination. Which vaccine is contraindicated?

AIR-OLD-16.s: A patient with SLE on prednisolone and immunosuppressants presents with 1 week of dry cough, fever and dyspnea with bilateral interstitial infiltrates and marked hypoxemia but an unremarkable lung examination. What should be done first?
AIR-OLD-16.a: Treat empirically for Pneumocystis pneumonia while investigating for infection

AIR-MCQ-13.s: A 24-year-old man has had four episodes of bacterial pneumonia and two episodes of bacterial sinusitis in the past 2 years, plus chronic diarrhea from giardiasis. He is HIV-negative. CBC shows normal white cell count and differential. Which of the following is the most appropriate next investigation?
AIR-MCQ-13.p: **ติดเชื้อ sinopulmonary ซ้ำ + giardia ในผู้ใหญ่ = สงสัย CVID → ส่ง IgG/IgA/IgM ก่อน**; Neisseria ซ้ำ = complement, ฝีหนองซ้ำ = phagocyte

AIR-MCQ-14.s: A 58-year-old man presents with a hot, swollen, exquisitely tender right knee for 2 days and fever 38.5 C. He has had three similar self-limited episodes in the past 2 years. He cannot bear weight. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial investigation?
AIR-MCQ-14.a: Arthrocentesis for synovial fluid cell count, crystal examination and Gram stain with culture
AIR-MCQ-14.p: ข้ออักเสบเฉียบพลันข้อเดียว = **เจาะข้อก่อน** เสมอ; uric acid ปกติไม่ตัดเก๊าท์ และ uric acid สูงก็ไม่ตัดข้อติดเชื้อ

AIR-OLD-26.s: A 45-year-old man presents with acute arthritis. Which of the following history items is most important to obtain?
AIR-OLD-26.a: Sexual history, alcohol intake, recent infection and family history of arthritis

AIR-MCQ-15.s: Synovial fluid from an acutely inflamed first metatarsophalangeal joint shows 28,000 WBC/mm3 with 85% neutrophils, and polarized light microscopy reveals needle-shaped crystals that are strongly negatively birefringent (yellow when parallel to the compensator axis). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-MCQ-15.p: **Needle + negative + เหลืองเมื่อขนาน = gout**; rhomboid + positive = CPPD — และเจอผลึกแล้วก็ยังต้องส่งเพาะเชื้อ

AIR-OLD-21.s: A 50-year-old man with acute pain of the first metatarsophalangeal joint has synovial fluid showing needle-shaped, strongly negatively birefringent crystals. What is the diagnosis?

AIR-MCQ-17.s: A 52-year-old man with an acute gout flare of the left ankle for 18 hours has stage 2 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 68 mL/min/1.73 m2), well-controlled hypertension and peptic ulcer disease treated 6 months ago. He takes no urate-lowering therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for this flare?
AIR-MCQ-17.a: Oral colchicine or a short course of oral prednisolone
AIR-MCQ-17.p: Flare เก๊าท์เลือกยาตาม**โรคร่วม**: PUD/CKD → colchicine ขนาดต่ำหรือสเตียรอยด์; **ห้ามเริ่ม allopurinol เดี่ยว ๆ ตอนอักเสบ แต่ก็ห้ามหยุดตัวที่กินอยู่**

AIR-OLD-22.s: Which drug is the most appropriate first-line treatment for an acute gout flare in a patient with peptic ulcer disease?

AIR-MCQ-18.s: A 49-year-old man has had four gout flares in the past year and a tophus over the right elbow. Serum urate is 9.2 mg/dL, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL. His last flare resolved 3 weeks ago. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
AIR-MCQ-18.a: Start allopurinol at a low dose with anti-inflammatory prophylaxis and titrate to a serum urate below 6 mg/dL
AIR-MCQ-18.p: ULT: **เริ่มต่ำ ค่อยเพิ่ม + colchicine กัน flare 3–6 เดือน + คุม urate < 6 (มี tophus < 5) แล้วกินตลอด**

AIR-OLD-30.s: Which of the following is an indication to start urate-lowering therapy?
AIR-OLD-30.a: Presence of tophi or two or more gout flares per year

AIR-MCQ-19.s: A 45-year-old man on the intensive phase of anti-tuberculous treatment develops an acutely painful, swollen right first metatarsophalangeal joint at week 6. Serum uric acid is 11 mg/dL. Which drug in his regimen is most responsible for this problem?
AIR-MCQ-19.p: ยาวัณโรคทำให้ **uric acid สูง = pyrazinamide** (ethambutol เสริมได้) — ถ้าไม่มีอาการ ไม่ต้องรักษาและไม่ต้องหยุดยา

AIR-OLD-23.s: A patient on anti-tuberculous therapy develops joint pain with a serum uric acid of 10 mg/dL. Which drug is responsible?

AIR-MCQ-26.s: A 46-year-old man has a serum uric acid of 8.4 mg/dL found on a health check-up. He has never had joint pain, tophi or kidney stones. Renal function is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
AIR-MCQ-26.a: Lifestyle advice and periodic follow-up without urate-lowering drug therapy
AIR-MCQ-26.p: **urate สูงแต่ไม่มีอาการ = ไม่ต้องให้ยา** — ไปแก้ยาและพฤติกรรมที่ทำให้สูงแทน

AIR-MCQ-27.s: A 68-year-old man with untreated gout for 15 years has firm, chalky white nodules over the olecranon and the helix of the ear, and deformed fingers. Radiograph of the hand shows well-defined 'punched-out' erosions with sclerotic margins and overhanging edges, with preserved joint space until late. Which of the following best explains these radiographic findings?
AIR-MCQ-27.a: Deposition of monosodium urate aggregates in and around bone that erode cortex while cartilage is relatively spared
AIR-MCQ-27.p: Tophaceous gout บนฟิล์ม = **punched-out erosion + overhanging edge + ช่องข้อยังกว้าง**; รักษาโดยคุม urate < 5 เพื่อละลาย tophus

AIR-OLD-29.s: Which radiographic finding is most characteristic of long-standing tophaceous gout?
AIR-OLD-29.a: Punched-out erosion with sclerotic margin and overhanging edge, with preserved joint space

AIR-MCQ-28.s: A 76-year-old woman on hydrochlorothiazide for hypertension has a 6-month history of pain and swelling of multiple small joints of both hands, including some distal interphalangeal joints, with firm nodules over the finger pads. RF and anti-CCP are negative. Aspiration of a nodular joint shows negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-MCQ-28.a: Polyarticular tophaceous gout mimicking rheumatoid arthritis
AIR-MCQ-28.p: หญิงสูงอายุกิน thiazide + ปุ่มที่นิ้วคล้าย RA/OA — **เจาะดูผลึกก่อนสรุป**; losartan เป็นยาลดความดันที่ช่วยลด urate

AIR-MCQ-29.s: A 60-year-old man with gout and stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 24 mL/min/1.73 m2) needs urate-lowering therapy. HLA-B*58:01 is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?
AIR-MCQ-29.a: Start allopurinol at 50 mg daily and titrate slowly with monitoring, aiming for urate below 6 mg/dL
AIR-MCQ-29.p: CKD: **allopurinol เริ่ม 50 mg เพิ่มช้า ๆ จนได้ urate < 6** — ไม่ใช่ห้ามใช้ และไม่ใช่ยิงขนาดมาตรฐานทันที

AIR-MCQ-16.s: A 74-year-old woman has acute pain and swelling of the right knee. Synovial fluid shows 18,000 WBC/mm3 and rhomboid-shaped crystals that are weakly positively birefringent. Plain radiograph shows linear calcification of the meniscal cartilage. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis and the associated metabolic condition to screen for?
AIR-MCQ-16.a: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease; screen for hyperparathyroidism, hemochromatosis and hypomagnesemia
AIR-MCQ-16.p: Pseudogout = **calcium PYROPHOSPHATE** + chondrocalcinosis; เป็นในคนอายุน้อยหรือหลายข้อให้หา **hyperparathyroidism / hemochromatosis / hypomagnesemia**

AIR-OLD-19.s: Synovial fluid from a painful knee contains rhomboid-shaped crystals that are weakly positively birefringent under polarized light. What is the diagnosis?

AIR-OLD-20.s: In the same patient with pseudogout of the knee, which additional synovial fluid profile is expected?
AIR-OLD-20.a: Inflammatory fluid with WBC 2,000-50,000/mm3, predominantly neutrophils, and reduced viscosity

AIR-OLD-31.s: A 70-year-old man on hemodialysis develops an acutely painful shoulder. Aspiration shows no crystals under polarized light but the fluid contains clumps that stain with alizarin red. What is the most likely diagnosis?

AIR-23-04B-Q1.s: A 62-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease on maintenance hemodialysis develops pain and swelling of both second and third proximal interphalangeal joints. Joint aspiration shows 6,500 WBC/µL, Gram stain is negative, and polarized microscopy shows bipyramidal, strongly positively birefringent crystals. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-23-04B-Q1.p: ผู้ป่วยฟอกไต + ผลึกพีระมิดคู่ positively birefringent ที่ PIP/MCP = calcium oxalate arthropathy รักษาตามอาการและพิจารณาเพิ่มความถี่การฟอกไต

AIR-MCQ-20.s: A 63-year-old man with diabetes has a hot swollen left knee and fever for 2 days. Synovial fluid shows 78,000 WBC/mm3 with 93% neutrophils, no crystals, and Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
AIR-MCQ-20.p: Septic arthritis = **ระบายหนอง + ยาฉีด** เสมอ; GPC cluster = S. aureus → cloxacillin, หนุ่มสาวเพศสัมพันธ์เสี่ยง = gonococcus → ceftriaxone

AIR-OLD-24.s: A patient with a hot swollen knee has synovial fluid Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci in clusters. What is the most appropriate antibiotic?

AIR-OLD-32.s: A 30-year-old sexually active man has migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis of the wrist and a few pustular skin lesions, then develops a hot swollen knee. What is the most likely organism?

AIR-OLD-25.s: A patient with septic arthritis on intravenous cloxacillin for 12 days is clinically well but the neutrophil count has fallen to 900/mm3. What is the most appropriate next step?
AIR-OLD-25.a: Recognize drug-induced neutropenia and switch to another effective antibiotic class with monitoring

AIR-MCQ-21.s: The same patient improves clinically on intravenous cloxacillin. On day 12 of therapy he is afebrile with a normal-looking knee, but routine CBC shows WBC 2,800/mm3 with absolute neutrophil count 900/mm3 (previously normal). There is no new fever or mucosal ulcer. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
AIR-MCQ-21.a: Recognize drug-induced neutropenia, change to an alternative antibiotic class and monitor the blood count
AIR-MCQ-21.p: Neutropenia สัปดาห์ที่ 2 ของ beta-lactam ขนาดสูง = **drug-induced** — เปลี่ยนกลุ่มยา ไม่ใช่หยุดยาทั้งหมดหรือเจาะไขกระดูก

AIR-MCQ-22.s: A 64-year-old woman with BMI 31 kg/m2 has bilateral knee pain worse with walking and improving with rest, with morning stiffness of 10 minutes and crepitus. There is no warmth or effusion. Radiographs show joint space narrowing and osteophytes. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line management?
AIR-MCQ-22.a: Structured exercise, quadriceps strengthening and weight reduction, with topical NSAID for pain
AIR-MCQ-22.p: OA = **ออกกำลังกาย + ลดน้ำหนัก + topical NSAID มาก่อนเสมอ**; ข้อฝืดเช้า < 30 นาทีและไม่มีการอักเสบทั่วร่างกาย

AIR-OLD-27.s: A 60-year-old woman has bilateral knee pain worse with walking, relieved by rest, with 10 minutes of morning stiffness and bony enlargement of the distal interphalangeal joints. ANA and rheumatoid factor are negative. Radiograph shows joint space narrowing with osteophytes. What is the diagnosis?

AIR-MCQ-23.s: A 55-year-old woman has painful hands. Which of the following findings best distinguishes rheumatoid arthritis from osteoarthritis?
AIR-MCQ-23.a: Symmetric swelling of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints with morning stiffness lasting more than 1 hour
AIR-MCQ-23.p: **MCP/PIP + ฝืดเช้า > 1 ชม. = RA · DIP เป็นปุ่มกระดูก + ฝืด < 30 นาที = OA**; RF ลบไม่ตัด RA ออก

AIR-MCQ-24.s: A 42-year-old woman who cares for her newborn grandchild has pain over the radial side of the right wrist. Pain is reproduced when she flexes the thumb into the palm and deviates the wrist to the ulnar side (Finkelstein test). There is no joint swelling and no morning stiffness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-MCQ-24.p: เจ็บ**เฉพาะจุด + ขยับ passive ได้เกือบเต็ม = periarticular (soft-tissue rheumatism)** ไม่ใช่โรคข้อ; Finkelstein บวก = de Quervain

AIR-MCQ-25.s: A 26-year-old man develops asymmetric pain and swelling of the right knee and left ankle 3 weeks after an episode of bloody diarrhea. He also has conjunctivitis and dysuria without urethral discharge. Synovial fluid shows 15,000 WBC/mm3, no crystals, and sterile culture. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-MCQ-25.p: ท้องเสีย/ติดเชื้อทางเพศสัมพันธ์ → 1–4 สัปดาห์ → **ข้ออักเสบไม่สมมาตรขาส่วนล่าง + ตาแดง + แสบขัด = reactive arthritis ข้อปลอดเชื้อ**

AIR-OLD-33.s: A patient with acute pericarditis has pleuritic chest pain relieved by leaning forward. Which drug combination is first-line?
AIR-OLD-33.a: Aspirin or an NSAID plus colchicine

AIR-MCQ-30.s: A 68-year-old woman sustains a wrist fracture after falling from standing height. She has taken prednisolone 7.5 mg daily for 3 years for rheumatoid arthritis. Bone mineral density T-score at the femoral neck is -2.7. Serum calcium, phosphate and creatinine are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
AIR-MCQ-30.a: Start an oral bisphosphonate with calcium and vitamin D, and review the need for continued corticosteroid
AIR-MCQ-30.p: หักจากล้มระดับพื้น = รักษา osteoporosis **ทันที**; ได้สเตียรอยด์ ≥ 2.5–7.5 mg นานกว่า 3 เดือน ต้องประเมินกระดูกทุกราย

AIR-OLD-14.s: Which of the following is the best initial screening test in a patient with suspected systemic lupus erythematosus?

AIR-OLD-48.s: Which antibody pattern is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?

AIR-MCQ-31.s: A 24-year-old woman has 3 months of fatigue, malar rash sparing the nasolabial folds, painless oral ulcers, and symmetric arthritis of the hands without erosion. Lab: WBC 3,100/mm3, lymphocyte 800/mm3, platelet 130,000/mm3, urinalysis protein 2+, RBC 15–20/HPF with red cell casts. Which of the following investigations best supports the diagnosis?
AIR-MCQ-31.a: Antinuclear antibody with anti-double-stranded DNA and complement C3/C4 levels
AIR-MCQ-31.p: **ANA = คัดกรอง (ลบแทบตัดออก) · anti-dsDNA + anti-Sm = ยืนยัน · C3/C4 ต่ำ = active** — และ RBC cast แปลว่าไตอักเสบจนกว่าจะพิสูจน์เป็นอื่น

AIR-MCQ-32.s: A 26-year-old woman with newly diagnosed SLE has urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.8 g/g, active urine sediment with red cell casts, and creatinine 1.3 mg/dL (was 0.8 mg/dL 4 months ago). Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
AIR-MCQ-32.a: Percutaneous renal biopsy to determine the class of lupus nephritis before immunosuppressive therapy
AIR-MCQ-32.p: SLE + โปรตีนรั่ว ≥ 0.5 g/วัน หรือ active sediment → **biopsy ก่อนเสมอ เพราะ class เป็นตัวเลือกยา**

AIR-OLD-49.s: A woman with SLE and lupus nephritis wishes to become pregnant. Which drug must be stopped and replaced before conception?

AIR-33-02B-Q1.s: A 24-year-old woman has a 2-month history of photosensitive malar rash, painless oral ulcers seen by the physician, and morning stiffness with swelling of both wrists and several MCP joints. Investigations: ANA 1:640 speckled, anti-dsDNA positive, C3 and C4 low, platelet 96,000/uL, urinalysis normal. She also has a fever of 38.5 C on the day she is seen; blood cultures are negative and there is no localizing source. Which of the following statements about applying the EULAR/ACR 2019 criteria to this patient is correct?
AIR-33-02B-Q1.a: The fever may be counted because no more likely explanation than SLE has been found, and only the highest-weighted criterion within each domain is counted
AIR-33-02B-Q1.p: เกณฑ์ 2019 = ANA ≥ 1:80 เป็นประตูเข้า + ≥ 1 อาการทางคลินิก + คะแนนรวม ≥ 10 โดยห้ามนับข้อที่โรคอื่นอธิบายได้ดีกว่า และนับข้อคะแนนสูงสุดข้อเดียวในแต่ละ domain

AIR-33-02B-Q2.s: A 32-year-old woman has scaly, coin-shaped plaques on the scalp and cheeks for the past year. The plaques have a depressed, atrophic centre with surrounding hyperpigmentation, and hair does not regrow within them. Peeling a scale reveals keratin spikes on its undersurface. Which of the following is the most appropriate description and implication of this lesion?
AIR-33-02B-Q2.a: Chronic discoid lupus erythematosus, an LE-specific lesion that scars permanently, so treatment should be started promptly to preserve hair follicles
AIR-33-02B-Q2.p: Carpet tack sign + follicular plugging + ตรงกลางฝ่อขอบคล้ำ = discoid lupus ซึ่งทำให้ผมร่วงถาวร ต้องรีบรักษา

AIR-33-02C-Q1.s: A 27-year-old woman with SLE on hydroxychloroquine alone presents with a 2-week history of easy bruising. She has no fever, no rash, and no new joint symptoms. Hb 12.4 g/dL, WBC 5,200/uL, platelet 18,000/uL, reticulocyte 1.2%, direct Coombs test negative, urinalysis normal, C3 low, anti-dsDNA rising. A blood smear confirms true thrombocytopenia without schistocytes. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
AIR-33-02C-Q1.p: เกล็ดเลือด < 25,000 หรือ AIHA ใน SLE = ให้ pulse methylprednisolone ไม่ใช่ steroid ขนาดต่ำ และให้ HCQ ต่อเสมอ

AIR-33-02C-Q2.s: A 30-year-old woman is about to start prednisolone 40 mg/day plus mycophenolate mofetil for class IV lupus nephritis. Which of the following pre-treatment and long-term measures is most appropriate?
AIR-33-02C-Q2.a: Screen with chest radiograph, stool examination for parasites and a dental examination, give Pneumocystis prophylaxis, and add calcium, vitamin D and fracture-risk assessment
AIR-33-02C-Q2.p: ก่อนกดภูมิคุ้มกัน: CXR + อุจจาระหาพยาธิ + ตรวจฟัน แล้วตามด้วย PJP prophylaxis วัคซีนเชื้อตาย และการดูแลกระดูกตั้งแต่ต้น

AIR-33-02D-Q1.s: A 27-year-old woman with SLE on prednisolone 10 mg/day presents with pleuritic chest pain and dyspnoea for 5 days. Chest radiograph shows small bilateral pleural effusions. Thoracentesis yields clear yellow fluid: protein 4.2 g/dL (serum 6.8), LDH 260 IU/L (serum 340), glucose 82 mg/dL, pH 7.41, WBC 2,800/mm3 with lymphocyte predominance, ADA 15 U/L, Gram stain and AFB smear negative, cytology negative, pleural fluid ANA positive with a fluid-to-serum ratio of 1.4 and low pleural C4. Which interpretation best fits this fluid?
AIR-33-02D-Q1.a: Lupus pleuritis — an exudate with near-normal pH and glucose, positive fluid ANA and low complement
AIR-33-02D-Q1.p: Exudate + pH และน้ำตาลเกือบปกติ + ANA ในน้ำเจาะบวก (ratio ≥ 1) + complement ต่ำ = lupus pleuritis

AIR-33-02D-Q2.s: A 34-year-old woman with a 6-year history of SLE develops a unilateral pleural effusion. Pleural fluid shows protein 5.1 g/dL (serum 7.0), LDH 890 IU/L (serum 300), glucose 22 mg/dL, pH 7.08, WBC 9,400/mm3 with 85% neutrophils. Which is the most appropriate next step?
AIR-33-02D-Q2.a: Send Gram stain and culture and arrange drainage, because very low glucose with pH below 7.2 points away from lupus pleuritis
AIR-33-02D-Q2.p: pH < 7.2 และน้ำตาลต่ำมากในผู้ป่วย SLE = ติดเชื้อจนกว่าจะพิสูจน์ได้ว่าไม่ใช่ ต้องเพาะเชื้อและระบาย ไม่ใช่เพิ่มยากดภูมิคุ้มกัน

AIR-MCQ-33.s: A 62-year-old man treated with hydralazine for 8 months develops fever, arthralgia and pleuritic chest pain. ANA is positive at 1:640 in a homogeneous pattern, anti-histone antibody is positive, anti-double-stranded DNA is negative, and C3/C4 are normal. Renal function and urinalysis are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
AIR-MCQ-33.a: Stop hydralazine; symptoms usually resolve over weeks, with NSAID or short-course corticosteroid if needed
AIR-MCQ-33.p: **Anti-histone บวก + anti-dsDNA ลบ + complement ปกติ + ไม่เข้าไตเข้าสมอง = drug-induced lupus → หยุดยา**

AIR-OLD-15.s: A 45-year-old woman on hydralazine for 1 year develops arthralgia, fever and pleuritic chest pain. ANA is positive, anti-double-stranded DNA is negative, anti-histone antibody is positive and complement levels are normal. What is the diagnosis?

AIR-MCQ-34.s: A 32-year-old woman has had three unexplained first-trimester miscarriages and one fetal death at 22 weeks. She also had an unprovoked deep vein thrombosis 2 years ago. Which of the following laboratory tests should be ordered to confirm the suspected diagnosis?
AIR-MCQ-34.a: Lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin antibody and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I, repeated at least 12 weeks apart
AIR-MCQ-34.p: แท้งซ้ำ + ลิ่มเลือด = **APS → ส่ง LA, anticardiolipin, anti-β2GPI และต้องยืนยันซ้ำที่ 12 สัปดาห์**

AIR-OLD-18.s: A woman with four unexplained pregnancy losses and a past unprovoked deep vein thrombosis is suspected of having antiphospholipid syndrome. Which antibody should be tested?
AIR-OLD-18.a: Anticardiolipin antibody (with lupus anticoagulant and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I)

AIR-MCQ-35.s: The same patient is now 6 weeks pregnant. Antiphospholipid antibodies were positive on two occasions 12 weeks apart. Which of the following is the most appropriate management during this pregnancy?
AIR-MCQ-35.a: Low-dose aspirin plus prophylactic low-molecular-weight heparin throughout pregnancy and postpartum
AIR-MCQ-35.p: Obstetric APS = **aspirin ขนาดต่ำ + heparin** (ห้าม warfarin ในไตรมาสแรก) และให้ต่อหลังคลอด 6 สัปดาห์

AIR-MCQ-36.s: A 30-year-old man with lupus nephritis on prednisolone 30 mg daily and mycophenolate presents with 1 week of dry cough, fever and progressive dyspnea. PE: T 38.6 C, RR 28/min, SpO2 88% on room air, clear breath sounds. CXR shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates. Lab: WBC 9,000/mm3 with lymphocyte 600/mm3, LDH 520 U/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
AIR-MCQ-36.a: Treat empirically for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and corticosteroid while confirming the diagnosis
AIR-MCQ-36.p: ผู้ป่วยกดภูมิ + ไข้ + ฝ้า interstitial + LDH สูง + ฟังปอดปกติ = **PCP จนกว่าจะพิสูจน์เป็นอื่น** — รักษาก่อน ยืนยันคู่กันไป

AIR-MCQ-37.s: A 38-year-old woman with SLE has taken hydroxychloroquine for 6 years. She is asymptomatic. Which of the following is the most appropriate monitoring plan for this drug?
AIR-MCQ-37.a: Baseline eye examination within the first year, then annual screening after 5 years using automated visual fields and optical coherence tomography
AIR-MCQ-37.p: Hydroxychloroquine = ยาหลักของ SLE ที่ต้อง **คัดกรองจอตาปีละครั้งหลังใช้ครบ 5 ปี** และคุมขนาดไม่เกิน 5 mg/kg/วัน

AIR-OLD-17.s: Which drug used in systemic lupus erythematosus requires periodic ophthalmologic screening because of the risk of irreversible maculopathy?

AIR-MCQ-48.s: A 34-year-old woman with SLE who has received prednisolone 30–60 mg daily for 2 years develops progressive right groin pain, worse on weight bearing, for 6 weeks. Range of motion of the hip is painful at the extremes but the joint is not hot or swollen. ESR 20 mm/hr. Plain radiograph of the hip is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next investigation?
AIR-MCQ-48.a: Magnetic resonance imaging of both hips
AIR-MCQ-48.p: ปวดสะโพกในคนกินสเตียรอยด์นาน + ฟิล์มปกติ = **ส่ง MRI สองข้างหา osteonecrosis** อย่ารอฟิล์มซ้ำ

AIR-OLD-44.s: A 34-year-old woman with SLE on long-term high-dose prednisolone develops progressive right groin pain on weight bearing. Hip radiograph is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

AIR-OLD-12.s: A woman with SLE has been on prednisolone for 3 years and now presents in pregnancy with fasting plasma glucose 138 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.2% at 8 weeks of gestation. How should her hyperglycemia be classified?
AIR-OLD-12.a: Pre-existing (overt) diabetes mellitus detected in pregnancy, likely glucocorticoid-induced

AIR-MCQ-38.s: A 45-year-old woman has 1 year of Raynaud phenomenon, thickening of the skin of the fingers extending to the forearms, and fine inspiratory crackles at both lung bases. ANA by immunofluorescence is reported negative at the screening dilution. Which of the following is the most appropriate next investigation?
AIR-MCQ-38.a: Anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70) and anticentromere antibody testing with high-resolution CT of the chest
AIR-MCQ-38.p: Scleroderma: **Scl-70 → ปอด (ILD) · centromere → ความดันปอดสูง · RNA pol III → renal crisis**; ANA ลบไม่ตัดโรคออกเมื่อคลินิกชัด

AIR-OLD-34.s: A patient with features of systemic sclerosis has a negative ANA on the standard screening assay. Which test should be sent next?

AIR-MCQ-39.s: A 49-year-old woman with diffuse systemic sclerosis for 8 months, recently given prednisolone 20 mg daily for arthralgia, presents with headache and blurred vision. BP 220/130 mmHg, creatinine 3.2 mg/dL (was 0.9 mg/dL), platelet 88,000/mm3, blood smear shows schistocytes, urinalysis shows mild proteinuria without casts. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
AIR-MCQ-39.a: Start a short-acting ACE inhibitor such as captopril and titrate rapidly
AIR-MCQ-39.p: SSc + ความดันพุ่ง + Cr ขึ้น + schistocyte = **scleroderma renal crisis → captopril ทันที และห้ามหยุดแม้ Cr จะขึ้น**

AIR-OLD-35.s: A patient with diffuse systemic sclerosis recently started on prednisolone develops blood pressure 210/120 mmHg, acute kidney injury and schistocytes on blood smear. Which drug should be started immediately?

AIR-MCQ-40.s: A 20-year-old woman reports that her fingers turn white then blue then red in cold air, symmetrically in both hands, for 4 years. There is no digital ulcer or pitting scar, peripheral pulses are normal, ANA is negative and nailfold capillaroscopy is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
AIR-MCQ-40.a: Reassurance with cold avoidance and smoking avoidance; drug therapy only if symptoms interfere with daily life
AIR-MCQ-40.p: Primary Raynaud: **อายุน้อย สองข้างเท่ากัน ไม่มีแผลปลายนิ้ว ANA ลบ capillaroscopy ปกติ → ไม่ต้องใช้ยา**

AIR-33-06B-Q1.s: A 45-year-old woman has Raynaud's phenomenon for 3 years, puffy fingers with sclerodactyly limited to the fingers (skin thickening does not extend proximal to the MCP joints), fingertip pitting scars, facial telangiectasia, abnormal nailfold capillaries and a positive anti-centromere antibody. Echocardiography shows pulmonary arterial hypertension and HRCT shows mild interstitial lung disease. What is her total 2013 ACR/EULAR score?
AIR-33-06B-Q1.p: puffy fingers + sclerodactyly นับ 4 ไม่ใช่ 6 · PAH + ILD นับ 2 ไม่ใช่ 4 · แอนติบอดีรวมสูงสุด 3 → เคสนี้ได้ 19 คะแนน

AIR-33-06B-Q2.s: A 52-year-old woman is referred with Raynaud's phenomenon, abnormal nailfold capillaries and a positive anti-U1RNP antibody at 1:320. She has puffy hands but no sclerodactyly, no telangiectasia, no digital ulcers or pitting scars, and normal PFT and echocardiography. Which statement is correct?
AIR-33-06B-Q2.a: She scores 7 points and is not classified as systemic sclerosis, because anti-U1RNP is not one of the three SSc-related antibodies that score
AIR-33-06B-Q2.p: anti-U1RNP ไม่ได้คะแนนในเกณฑ์ SSc 2013 — Raynaud + puffy fingers + nailfold ผิดปกติ ได้แค่ 7 ให้คิดถึง MCTD/UCTD แทน

AIR-MCQ-41.s: A 52-year-old woman has 3 months of progressive difficulty climbing stairs and combing her hair, without pain. PE: symmetric proximal muscle weakness grade 3/5, violaceous rash over the eyelids and scaly erythematous papules over the knuckles. Lab: creatine kinase 4,200 U/L, AST 180 U/L, ALT 120 U/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in addition to starting treatment?
AIR-MCQ-41.a: Age-appropriate malignancy screening, because dermatomyositis is strongly associated with occult cancer
AIR-MCQ-41.p: อ่อนแรงส่วนต้น + CK สูง + heliotrope/Gottron = dermatomyositis → **ต้องคัดกรองมะเร็ง**; AST/ALT ที่สูงอาจมาจากกล้ามเนื้อ ไม่ใช่ตับ

AIR-OLD-38.s: A 55-year-old woman has proximal muscle weakness, a violaceous periorbital rash and scaly papules over the knuckles. Apart from treating the myositis, what must not be missed?

AIR-OLD-37.s: A patient has proximal muscle weakness with AST 1,000 U/L but normal ALT, ALP and GGT. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

AIR-MCQ-42.s: A 58-year-old man with dyslipidemia on simvastatin 40 mg daily for 6 months complains of symmetric aching of the thigh and shoulder muscles for 3 weeks, without weakness or dark urine. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial investigation?
AIR-MCQ-42.p: ปวดกล้ามเนื้อ + กิน statin = **ส่ง CK ก่อน** และมองหายาที่ยับยั้ง CYP3A4 ร่วมด้วยเสมอ

AIR-OLD-36.s: A 58-year-old man on simvastatin complains of symmetric proximal muscle aching. Which investigation should be ordered first?

AIR-33-07-Q1.s: A 48-year-old woman has a 6-week history of heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules, painful papules on the palms and skin ulcers over the elbows, but her muscle strength is normal and CK is 120 U/L. She now has progressive dyspnoea; HRCT shows rapidly progressive interstitial changes and a small pneumomediastinum, and serum ferritin is markedly raised. Which myositis-specific antibody is most likely, and what does it imply?
AIR-33-07-Q1.a: Anti-MDA-5 — clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis with rapidly progressive ILD and high early mortality
AIR-33-07-Q1.p: ผื่น DM เต็มรูปแบบ + กล้ามเนื้อปกติ + ILD ลุกลามเร็ว + ferritin สูง = anti-MDA-5 ต้องรักษาเชิงรุกทันที

AIR-33-07B-Q1.s: A 54-year-old woman reports 2 years of gritty eyes and a dry mouth that forces her to sip water while eating. Schirmer test is 3 mm in 5 minutes bilaterally and unstimulated salivary flow is 0.05 mL/min. ANA is 1:320 fine speckled, anti-Ro52 is positive, anti-Ro60 and anti-La are negative, rheumatoid factor is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
AIR-33-07B-Q1.a: Perform a minor labial salivary gland biopsy, since her current score is below the classification threshold and a focus score would carry 3 points
AIR-33-07B-Q1.p: ในเกณฑ์ Sjögren 2017 มีเพียง focus score ≥ 1 และ anti-Ro60 ที่ให้ 3 คะแนน — anti-Ro52 เดี่ยว ๆ ไม่นับ

AIR-33-07B-Q2.s: A 58-year-old woman with primary Sjögren syndrome of 8 years returns with a firm, progressively enlarging left parotid swelling for 3 months, new palpable purpura on both legs, and cervical lymphadenopathy. Laboratory tests show C4 0.06 g/L (low), positive cryoglobulins and a monoclonal IgM kappa band. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-33-07B-Q2.a: Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) lymphoma arising in the parotid gland
AIR-33-07B-Q2.p: Sjögren + ต่อมน้ำลายโตข้างเดียวที่โตขึ้นเรื่อย ๆ + C4 ต่ำ + cryoglobulin + purpura = สงสัย MALT lymphoma ต้องตัดชิ้นเนื้อ

AIR-33-07C-Q1.s: A 30-year-old woman presents with polyarthritis for 3 weeks together with Raynaud phenomenon and sclerodactyly. ANA is positive at 1:160 speckled, anti-RNP is positive and anti-Sm is negative. Hand radiographs are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-33-07C-Q1.p: Raynaud + puffy hands/sclerodactyly + ข้ออักเสบ + anti-U1RNP = MCTD ไม่ใช่ overlap syndrome

AIR-33-07C-Q2.s: A 41-year-old woman has had Raynaud phenomenon, arthralgia and a positive ANA (1:160 speckled) for 3 years. She has never had a rash, oral ulcer, serositis, nephritis, cytopenia, sclerodactyly or muscle weakness; anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, anti-RNP, anti-Ro/La, anti-Scl-70 and anti-centromere are all negative, and complement levels are normal. Which of the following statements about her condition is most accurate?
AIR-33-07C-Q2.a: She has undifferentiated connective tissue disease; about 30% of such patients evolve into a defined disease over time, most often rheumatoid arthritis, so she needs periodic reassessment
AIR-33-07C-Q2.p: UCTD = มีอาการและแอนติบอดีแต่ไม่เข้าเกณฑ์โรคใด · ราว 30% กลายเป็นโรคชัดเจน (RA มากที่สุด) จึงต้องนัดติดตาม

AIR-33-07C-Q3.s: A 30-year-old woman presents with polyarthritis for 3 weeks together with Raynaud's phenomenon and sclerodactyly. ANA is positive at 1:160 with a speckled pattern, anti-RNP is positive and anti-Sm is negative. Hand radiographs are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-33-07C-Q3.p: มีอาการและแอนติบอดีของ CTD แต่ไม่เข้าเกณฑ์โรคใดเลย = UCTD · anti-RNP ไทเตอร์ไม่สูงพอและอาการไม่ครบ จึงยังไม่ใช่ MCTD

AIR-MCQ-43.s: A 72-year-old woman has 6 weeks of severe aching and morning stiffness of both shoulders and hips lasting 2 hours, with fatigue and low-grade fever. For 5 days she has had a new right temporal headache, scalp tenderness and pain in the jaw while chewing. ESR is 92 mm/hr. Vision is currently normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management?
AIR-MCQ-43.a: Start high-dose corticosteroid immediately and arrange temporal artery biopsy or vascular imaging without delaying treatment
AIR-MCQ-43.p: ผู้สูงอายุ + ปวดขมับ + **jaw claudication** + ESR สูง = GCA → **ให้สเตียรอยด์ทันที อย่ารอ biopsy**

AIR-OLD-39.s: A 72-year-old woman has new temporal headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication and ESR 95 mm/hr. Vision is normal. What should be done first?
AIR-OLD-39.a: Start high-dose corticosteroid immediately, then arrange temporal artery biopsy

AIR-OLD-46.s: A 68-year-old woman has 2 months of bilateral shoulder and hip girdle aching with prolonged morning stiffness, ESR 88 mm/hr, normal creatine kinase and no true weakness on testing. What is the most likely diagnosis and treatment?
AIR-OLD-46.a: Polymyalgia rheumatica; low-dose prednisolone 12.5-25 mg daily with a dramatic response expected

AIR-MCQ-44.s: A 56-year-old man has 2 months of chronic sinusitis with bloody nasal discharge, then develops hemoptysis and acute kidney injury. Lab: creatinine 3.8 mg/dL, urinalysis protein 2+, dysmorphic RBC with red cell casts. CXR shows bilateral nodular infiltrates, some with cavitation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-MCQ-44.p: **ไซนัสเรื้อรัง + ปอดเป็นโพรง + ไตอักเสบ = GPA (c-ANCA/PR3)** — pulmonary-renal syndrome ต้องรีบให้ยากดภูมิ

AIR-OLD-41.s: A 56-year-old man with chronic sinusitis and bloody nasal discharge develops hemoptysis, cavitating lung nodules and glomerulonephritis with red cell casts. Which antibody is most likely to be positive?

AIR-MCQ-45.s: A 19-year-old man develops palpable purpura over both lower legs and buttocks 1 week after an upper respiratory tract infection, together with colicky abdominal pain and pain in both ankles. Lab: platelet 320,000/mm3, normal coagulation, urinalysis shows RBC 20–30/HPF with protein 1+. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-MCQ-45.p: **Palpable purpura + เกล็ดเลือดปกติ = vasculitis**; ที่ขา/ก้น + ปวดท้อง + ปัสสาวะมีเลือด หลังเป็นหวัด = IgA vasculitis

AIR-OLD-40.s: A 19-year-old man has palpable purpura over both legs and buttocks, colicky abdominal pain, arthralgia and hematuria one week after an upper respiratory infection. Platelet count and coagulation tests are normal. What is the diagnosis?

AIR-MCQ-46.s: A 44-year-old woman has had symmetric swelling of the metacarpophalangeal and wrist joints with 90 minutes of morning stiffness for 10 weeks. RF and anti-CCP are positive, ESR 48 mm/hr, and radiographs show no erosion yet. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
AIR-MCQ-46.a: Start methotrexate with folic acid promptly, using a short course of corticosteroid as a bridge
AIR-MCQ-46.p: RA: **เริ่ม methotrexate สัปดาห์ละครั้ง + folic acid ให้เร็วที่สุด** ใช้สเตียรอยด์เป็นสะพาน และคัดกรอง TB/HBV ก่อน biologic

AIR-OLD-28.s: A 46-year-old woman has symmetric swelling of the MCP and PIP joints of both hands with morning stiffness of more than 30 minutes for 4 months. What is the most likely diagnosis?

AIR-OLD-42.s: Which conventional DMARD is the anchor drug for newly diagnosed rheumatoid arthritis, and how is it given?
AIR-OLD-42.a: Methotrexate, given once weekly with folic acid supplementation

AIR-MCQ-47.s: A 50-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate 15 mg weekly for 2 years presents with fever, cough and progressive dyspnea for 2 weeks. CXR shows diffuse interstitial infiltrates. Lab: WBC 3,200/mm3, platelet 98,000/mm3, AST/ALT 95/110 U/L, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management?
AIR-MCQ-47.a: Stop methotrexate, evaluate for both opportunistic infection and methotrexate pneumonitis, and give folinic acid if cytopenia is significant
AIR-MCQ-47.p: Methotrexate: ไข้ + ฝ้าปอด = **หยุดยา แล้วแยก pneumonitis กับการติดเชื้อฉวยโอกาสเสมอ**; ระวังคู่กับ TMP-SMX เพราะเสี่ยง pancytopenia

AIR-OLD-47.s: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate develops fever, dry cough and diffuse interstitial infiltrates with leukopenia. What should be done first?
AIR-OLD-47.a: Stop methotrexate and evaluate for both opportunistic infection and drug-induced pneumonitis

AIR-OLD-43.s: Before starting an anti-TNF biologic agent in rheumatoid arthritis, which screening is mandatory?
AIR-OLD-43.a: Latent tuberculosis (chest radiograph plus tuberculin skin test or IGRA) and hepatitis B and C serology

AIR-MCQ-49.s: A 27-year-old man has had low back pain for 18 months. The pain wakes him in the second half of the night, is associated with more than 45 minutes of morning stiffness, improves with exercise and worsens with rest. He had one episode of painful red eye with photophobia last year. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management after confirming sacroiliitis?
AIR-MCQ-49.a: Regular exercise and physiotherapy with a full-dose NSAID, escalating to a biologic if the response is inadequate
AIR-MCQ-49.p: Inflammatory back pain (ดีขึ้นเมื่อขยับ ตื่นกลางดึก ฝืดเช้านาน) + uveitis = axial SpA → **ออกกำลังกาย + NSAID เต็มขนาด; methotrexate ไม่ช่วยโรคแกนกลาง**

AIR-OLD-45.s: A 27-year-old man has chronic low back pain that improves with exercise, wakes him in the early morning, with morning stiffness of 1 hour and a past episode of acute anterior uveitis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

AIR-MCQ-50.s: A 28-year-old woman has 3 weeks of daily fever spiking to 39.5 C in the evening, a salmon-coloured evanescent rash appearing with the fever, sore throat, and arthralgia of the wrists and knees. Lab: WBC 19,000/mm3 with 88% neutrophils, ferritin 8,400 ng/mL, ESR 95 mm/hr, ANA and RF negative, blood cultures negative twice, echocardiography normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
AIR-MCQ-50.p: ไข้รายวัน + ผื่นแซลมอนตามไข้ + เจ็บคอ + **ferritin สูงมาก + ANA/RF ลบ = AOSD** แต่ต้องตัดติดเชื้อและมะเร็งออกก่อนเสมอ

AIR-OLD-50.s: A 28-year-old woman has daily evening fever for 3 weeks, an evanescent salmon-coloured rash, sore throat, arthralgia, neutrophilic leukocytosis and ferritin 8,000 ng/mL, with negative ANA, RF and blood cultures. What is the most likely diagnosis?

AIR-OLD-13.s: A 20-year-old man presents with fever, arthralgia, a maculopapular rash over the trunk and extremities, and swelling with warmth and limited movement of both knees, ankles and elbows. Hct 40%, WBC 3,500/mm3 (N 45%, L 50%, atypical lymphocyte 5%), platelet 45,000/mm3. What is the most likely diagnosis?

CARDIO-04-01-Q1.s: A 24-year-old man sustains a stab wound to the left chest. He is hypotensive with distended neck veins and muffled heart sounds. Bedside echocardiography shows only about 150 mL of pericardial fluid. In contrast, a 60-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer has 1,200 mL of pericardial fluid on echocardiography but is haemodynamically stable. Which factor best explains this difference?
CARDIO-04-01-Q1.a: The rate at which the fluid accumulated relative to the compliance of the pericardium
CARDIO-04-01-Q1.p: เลือดออกเร็ว 150 mL ทำให้ tamponade ได้ · น้ำสะสมช้า 1 ลิตรอาจยังสบายดี — อัตราสำคัญกว่าปริมาณ

C-OLD-14.s: A young man has chest pain and an ECG with widespread ST elevation. Troponin-I is markedly elevated but coronary angiography shows normal coronary arteries and echocardiography shows mildly reduced left ventricular function. What is the most likely diagnosis?

C-OLD-01.s: A 35-year-old man has sharp retrosternal chest pain for 2 days that is worse when lying flat and on deep inspiration, and is relieved by sitting up and leaning forward. What is the most likely diagnosis?

C-OLD-03.s: A patient with pleuritic chest pain relieved by sitting forward has an ECG showing widespread concave ST elevation with PR depression, and a scratchy triphasic sound at the left lower sternal border. What is the diagnosis?

C-OLD-04.s: An ECG shows ST elevation in all leads except aVR, where there is ST depression with PR elevation. What is the most likely diagnosis?

C-OLD-10.s: A patient with a pleural effusion has an ECG showing ST elevation in leads V1 to V4 with reciprocal ST depression inferiorly and elevated troponin. What is the most likely cause of the ECG change?

C-MCQ-01.s: A 38-year-old man presents with 3 days of sharp retrosternal chest pain that worsens when he lies flat and on deep inspiration, and is relieved by sitting up and leaning forward. He had an upper respiratory tract infection 10 days ago. Vital signs: BT 37.8 C, PR 96/min, BP 118/74 mmHg, RR 20/min. A scratchy triphasic sound is heard at the left lower sternal border, loudest at end-expiration while sitting forward. ECG shows widespread concave-upward ST elevation with PR-segment depression in II, III, aVF and V2-V6, with ST depression and PR elevation in aVR. Troponin-I is minimally elevated. Echocardiogram: normal LV systolic function, no pericardial effusion, no regional wall motion abnormality. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
C-MCQ-01.p: trop ขึ้นเล็กน้อย + ST elevation ทั่ว = myopericarditis ยังรักษาแบบ pericarditis แต่ **ห้ามออกกำลังกายหนัก** และต้องตาม EF; ถ้า EF ตก = myocarditis เด่น ต้อง admit

C-OLD-02.s: A 38-year-old man with acute pericarditis after a viral illness has no effusion and normal cardiac function. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
C-OLD-02.a: High-dose aspirin or an NSAID plus colchicine

CARDIO-04-05-Q1.s: A 44-year-old man from an area where tuberculosis is endemic has 6 weeks of low-grade fever, weight loss and progressive dyspnoea. Echocardiography shows a large circumferential pericardial effusion. Pericardiocentesis yields straw-coloured fluid with a lymphocyte-predominant exudate, protein ratio 0.7, adenosine deaminase 78 IU/L and a negative acid-fast smear; culture is pending. Which of the following best describes this case, and what is the appropriate management?
CARDIO-04-05-Q1.a: Probable tuberculous pericarditis — start 2HRZE/4-7HR with adjunctive prednisolone
CARDIO-04-05-Q1.p: Lymphocytic exudate + ADA สูงในพื้นที่วัณโรคชุก = probable TB pericarditis เริ่มยาได้เลย พร้อมสเตียรอยด์เสริมกันพังผืดรัด

CARDIO-04-05-Q2.s: A 66-year-old man had a large anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction 2 days ago; reperfusion was delayed. He now has pleuritic chest pain and a pericardial friction rub. Blood pressure is 128/76 mmHg and echocardiography shows a trivial pericardial effusion with no tamponade physiology. Which of the following is the most appropriate anti-inflammatory management?
CARDIO-04-05-Q2.p: Early post-MI pericarditis เลือก aspirin ขนาดสูง + colchicine — เลี่ยง NSAID ตัวอื่นและสเตียรอยด์ขนาดสูงเพราะรบกวนการสมานของกล้ามเนื้อหัวใจ

C-OLD-15.s: A dyspnoeic patient has a chest radiograph showing an enlarged globular 'water-bottle' cardiac silhouette with clear lung fields. What is the most appropriate next step?
C-OLD-15.a: Echocardiography, and pericardiocentesis if there is tamponade physiology

C-OLD-17.s: Which finding on pericardial fluid analysis most suggests a tuberculous rather than a malignant pericardial effusion?
C-OLD-17.a: Lymphocyte-predominant exudate with high adenosine deaminase

C-OLD-06.s: A patient has muffled heart sounds, hypotension and distended neck veins, then develops shock. What type of shock is this?

C-OLD-08.s: A patient with known pericardial effusion becomes hypotensive with BP 80/50 mmHg, pulse 120/min, and distended neck veins that do not collapse on inspiration. Which physical sign best supports tamponade physiology?
C-OLD-08.a: Pulsus paradoxus — an inspiratory fall in systolic pressure of more than 10 mmHg

C-OLD-09.s: In cardiac tamponade, echocardiography shows right atrial and right ventricular diastolic collapse. Which mechanism best explains the haemodynamic compromise?
C-OLD-09.a: Raised intrapericardial pressure impairs diastolic filling, with ventricular interdependence across the septum

C-MCQ-02.s: A 28-year-old woman with acute pericarditis returns with progressive dyspnea. Vital signs: PR 122/min, BP 84/62 mmHg, RR 26/min. Neck veins are distended to the angle of the jaw and do not collapse on inspiration. Heart sounds are distant. ECG now shows beat-to-beat variation of QRS amplitude (electrical alternans). Which of the following additional physical findings is most likely to be present?
C-MCQ-02.a: Inspiratory fall in systolic blood pressure of more than 10 mmHg
C-MCQ-02.p: Beck triad (hypotension + distended neck veins + muffled heart sounds) ครบทั้ง 3 พบจริงแค่ส่วนน้อย; **pulsus paradoxus + JVP ไม่ยุบตอนหายใจเข้า** sensitive กว่า. ข้อสอบชอบถามว่า shock ชนิดไหน → **obstructive shock**

C-OLD-05.s: An ECG shows beat-to-beat variation in the amplitude of the QRS complexes (electrical alternans) with sinus tachycardia and low voltage. What is the most likely diagnosis?

C-OLD-07.s: A hypotensive patient has an ECG with low voltage and electrical alternans, and echocardiography shows a large pericardial effusion with right atrial collapse. What is the most appropriate immediate management?

C-MCQ-03.s: A 40-year-old woman with breast cancer (T2N1M0) presents with dyspnea progressing over 3 days. She completed 6 cycles of cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin and fluorouracil 6 months ago. She has no pleuritic chest pain. Vital signs: BP 80/60 mmHg with a 14 mmHg inspiratory fall in systolic pressure, PR 120/min. Jugular venous pressure is elevated to 10 cm. Lungs are clear on auscultation. There is trace pitting edema of both legs. Chest radiograph shows cardiomegaly with a globular heart, no pleural effusion and no pulmonary infiltrate. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
C-MCQ-03.a: Pericardial tamponade from malignant pericardial effusion
C-MCQ-03.p: ถ้าโจทย์มี **JVP สูง + ปอด clear** ให้คิด obstructive (tamponade, PE, constrictive pericarditis) หรือ RV failure เสมอ; ถ้า **JVP สูง + ปอดมี crackle** ให้คิด LV failure

C-OLD-12.s: A 40-year-old woman with breast cancer treated with a CAF regimen 6 months ago presents with dyspnoea, BP 80/60 mmHg, JVP elevated 10 cm, clear lungs and cardiomegaly on chest radiograph. What is the most likely diagnosis?

C-OLD-16.s: Which physical finding is characteristic of constrictive pericarditis rather than cardiac tamponade?
C-OLD-16.a: Pericardial knock with Kussmaul sign and a prominent y descent

C-MCQ-05.s: A 55-year-old man with previously treated tuberculous pericarditis presents with 6 months of progressive abdominal distension and leg oedema. He denies orthopnoea. Vital signs: PR 92/min regular, BP 106/70 mmHg. JVP is elevated and rises further on inspiration. An early diastolic high-pitched sound is heard at the apex. The liver is enlarged, there is ascites and 3+ pitting oedema. Lungs are clear. Chest radiograph shows pericardial calcification and a normal-sized heart. Which of the following findings best supports the diagnosis of constrictive pericarditis rather than restrictive cardiomyopathy?
C-MCQ-05.a: Discordant respiratory variation of right and left ventricular systolic pressures on cardiac catheterisation
C-MCQ-05.p: Constriction รักษาหายขาดได้ด้วย **pericardiectomy** ขณะที่ restrictive cardiomyopathy รักษาที่โรคต้นเหตุ — การแยกจึงเปลี่ยนการรักษาโดยสิ้นเชิง; ในไทย **TB คือสาเหตุอันดับหนึ่งของ constrictive pericarditis**

CARDIO-04-10-Q1.s: A 58-year-old man has ascites, leg oedema and an elevated jugular venous pressure. Echocardiography shows normal ventricular size and an ejection fraction of 60%, with bi-atrial enlargement. Tissue Doppler shows a medial mitral annular e' of 12 cm/s and a lateral e' of 7 cm/s. Which of the following does this tissue Doppler pattern most support?
CARDIO-04-10-Q1.p: Medial e′ สูงกว่า lateral e′ (annulus reversus) ในคนที่มี JVP สูงและ EF ปกติ = constrictive pericarditis

C-MCQ-04.s: A 22-year-old previously healthy man presents with 5 days of fever, myalgia and diarrhoea, followed by 2 days of progressive dyspnoea and orthopnoea. Vital signs: BT 38.0 C, PR 118/min, BP 96/64 mmHg. There is an S3 gallop and bibasilar crepitations. ECG shows sinus tachycardia with diffuse low-amplitude T wave inversion and no ST elevation. Troponin-I is 4.8 ng/mL (normal <0.04). Echocardiogram shows globally reduced LV systolic function (LVEF 32%) with no segmental pattern. Coronary angiography shows normal coronary arteries. Which of the following is the most likely aetiology of his condition?
C-MCQ-04.p: Gold standard วินิจฉัย = endomyocardial biopsy (Dallas criteria) แต่ practice ใช้ **cardiac MRI (Lake Louise criteria)** แทน; การรักษาคือ supportive HF therapy + **ห้ามออกกำลังกาย 3-6 เดือน** และ **ห้ามให้ NSAID ขนาดสูง** เมื่อ EF ตก

C-OLD-11.s: What is the most common cause of myocarditis in previously healthy adults?

C-OLD-13.s: Which chemotherapeutic agent is most characteristically associated with dose-dependent cardiomyopathy?

CARDIO-04-12-Q1.s: A 63-year-old man with metastatic melanoma received his second dose of combined nivolumab and ipilimumab 3 weeks ago. He now has fatigue, ptosis and proximal muscle weakness. ECG shows new first-degree atrioventricular block, troponin T is markedly elevated and echocardiography shows an ejection fraction of 42%. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management?
CARDIO-04-12-Q1.a: Withhold the checkpoint inhibitors and start pulse-dose methylprednisolone
CARDIO-04-12-Q1.p: กล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรง + หนังตาตก + troponin สูง + AV block ใหม่ ในคนที่ได้ ICI = หยุดยาและให้สเตียรอยด์ขนาดพัลส์ทันที

CARDIO-10-01-Q1.s: A 24-year-old woman with severe iron-deficiency anaemia has a haemoglobin of 4.2 g/dL. Her blood pressure is 112/70 mmHg, heart rate 118/min, and she has a wide pulse pressure with warm extremities. Serum lactate is 3.8 mmol/L. Which component of oxygen delivery is primarily responsible for her tissue hypoxia?
CARDIO-10-01-Q1.a: Arterial oxygen content, because haemoglobin is the dominant term in CaO2
CARDIO-10-01-Q1.p: ฮีโมโกลบินคือตัวหลักของ CaO₂ — ซีดรุนแรงทำให้เนื้อเยื่อขาดออกซิเจนได้แม้ SaO₂ 100% และให้ออกซิเจนก็ไม่ช่วย

C-MCQ-06.s: A 46-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with dyspnoea and near-syncope. Vital signs: PR 130/min, BP 76/58 mmHg, RR 30/min. Heart sounds are muffled, neck veins are engorged and there is a 16 mmHg inspiratory fall in systolic blood pressure. Bedside echocardiography shows a large circumferential pericardial effusion with right atrial and right ventricular diastolic collapse. Which haemodynamic profile best matches her type of shock?
C-MCQ-06.a: High central venous pressure, low cardiac output, high systemic vascular resistance
C-MCQ-06.p: Obstructive shock มี 4 ตัวหลักที่ต้องนึกถึง: cardiac tamponade, massive PE, tension pneumothorax, severe dynamic hyperinflation (auto-PEEP) — ทุกตัวมี **JVP สูง + ปอดไม่มี congestion** (ยกเว้น tension PTX ที่ breath sound หาย)

C-OLD-18.s: Cardiac tamponade causes which category of shock?

C-OLD-19.s: A patient admitted with pneumonia develops fever 39 C, BP 80/45 mmHg, warm extremities and bounding pulses 2 days after starting antibiotics. What type of shock is most likely?

C-OLD-20.s: A patient with cardiomegaly presents with shock, heart rate 130/min and an irregularly irregular pulse, with crepitations at both lung bases and cold extremities. What type of shock is this?

C-OLD-23.s: Anaphylactic shock belongs to which category of shock?

C-OLD-32.s: Which haemodynamic pattern fits distributive (septic) shock before fluid resuscitation?
C-OLD-32.a: Low systemic vascular resistance with high or normal cardiac output

C-OLD-31.s: A patient in prolonged shock is found to have AST 1,800 U/L and ALT 1,600 U/L with normal alkaline phosphatase, which fall rapidly over 3 days after blood pressure is restored. What is the most likely diagnosis?

C-MCQ-10.s: A 55-year-old man is hypotensive in the emergency department with BP 78/50 mmHg, PR 126/min and cool extremities. No history is available. Which single bedside finding is most useful to distinguish hypovolaemic shock from cardiogenic shock in this patient?
C-MCQ-10.p: สอบ OSCE มักให้ "flatted neck vein + แห้งจัด" → ตอบ **ให้ IV isotonic fluid**; ถ้า "JVP สูง + crepitation" → ห้ามให้น้ำ. ที่ bedside ใช้ **POCUS 3 จุด** ช่วย: IVC (volume), heart (EF/effusion/RV), lung (B-line) แยกได้ทั้ง 4 ชนิดในไม่กี่นาที

C-OLD-28.s: Which bedside finding best distinguishes hypovolaemic shock from cardiogenic and obstructive shock?

C-OLD-30.s: During thoracentesis a patient becomes light-headed with cold extremities. BP 80/60 mmHg, pulse 40/min, and breath sounds are equal bilaterally. What is the most likely cause?

CARDIO-10-05-Q1.s: A 61-year-old man presents with hypotension and dyspnoea of sudden onset. Blood pressure is 82/54 mmHg, heart rate 124/min, and his extremities are cool. Bedside ultrasound shows a dilated, poorly contracting right ventricle with septal flattening, a vigorously contracting and underfilled left ventricle, no pericardial effusion, normal lung sliding bilaterally and a plethoric inferior vena cava that does not collapse. Which diagnosis do these findings most support?
CARDIO-10-05-Q1.a: Massive pulmonary embolism causing obstructive shock
CARDIO-10-05-Q1.p: RV โตกับผนังกั้นแบน + LV เล็กแต่บีบแรง + IVC อิ่ม + ไม่มีน้ำรอบหัวใจ = PE ขนาดใหญ่ และอย่าเติมน้ำเยอะ

C-OLD-27.s: A hypotensive patient has flat neck veins, dry mucous membranes, poor skin turgor and a history of profuse diarrhoea. What is the most appropriate initial management?
C-OLD-27.a: Rapid infusion of isotonic crystalloid (0.9% normal saline)

C-OLD-29.s: A patient with severe vomiting and diarrhoea has BP 85/50 mmHg, Na 120 mEq/L, BUN 40 mg/dL and creatinine 1.8 mg/dL. What is the most appropriate initial fluid?

C-MCQ-08.s: A 68-year-old man with pyelonephritis remains hypotensive after receiving 30 mL/kg of balanced crystalloid. Vital signs: BT 38.9 C, PR 118/min, BP 82/40 mmHg, RR 26/min. Extremities are warm with brisk capillary refill and the pulse pressure is wide. Serum lactate is 4.2 mmol/L. Echocardiography shows a hyperdynamic left ventricle with LVEF 65% and a non-collapsed inferior vena cava. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
C-MCQ-08.a: Start intravenous norepinephrine infusion targeting a mean arterial pressure of 65 mmHg
C-MCQ-08.p: Bundle 1 ชั่วโมงแรกของ septic shock: วัด **lactate**, เจาะ **hemoculture ก่อนให้ยา**, ให้ **broad-spectrum antibiotic**, ให้ **crystalloid 30 mL/kg**, และ **เริ่ม vasopressor ถ้า MAP <65 ระหว่างหรือหลังให้น้ำ**; ตัวที่ 2 คือ vasopressin, ถ้ายังไม่พอพิจารณา hydrocortisone

CARDIO-10-07-Q1.s: A 70-year-old man with an anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction has a blood pressure of 84/56 mmHg, heart rate 108/min, cold mottled extremities, a jugular venous pressure of 12 cm and bibasilar crepitations. Echocardiography shows an ejection fraction of 20%. He has already received 500 mL of crystalloid without improvement. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in haemodynamic support?
CARDIO-10-07-Q1.a: Start dobutamine, adding norepinephrine if the mean arterial pressure remains below 65 mmHg
CARDIO-10-07-Q1.p: Cardiogenic shock ให้ dobutamine เพิ่ม CO และเติม norepinephrine ประคองความดัน — ห้ามให้ยา α บริสุทธิ์เพราะเพิ่ม afterload จน CO ยิ่งตก

C-MCQ-07.s: A 34-year-old woman develops generalised urticaria, hoarseness, wheezing and light-headedness 10 minutes after eating shellfish at dinner. Vital signs: PR 124/min, BP 78/44 mmHg, RR 28/min, SpO2 92% on room air. There is peri-oral oedema and diffuse expiratory wheeze. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
C-MCQ-07.a: Intramuscular adrenaline 0.5 mg into the anterolateral thigh
C-MCQ-07.p: Anaphylactic shock = **distributive shock**; ถ้าให้ adrenaline IM 2-3 ครั้งแล้วยังไม่ขึ้น ให้เปลี่ยนเป็น **adrenaline IV infusion** ไม่ใช่ IV bolus (เสี่ยง arrhythmia); ผู้ป่วยที่กิน β-blocker อยู่อาจดื้อ adrenaline → พิจารณา glucagon

C-OLD-24.s: A woman develops generalised urticaria, wheeze and BP 80/50 mmHg minutes after dinner. What is the most appropriate initial treatment?
C-OLD-24.a: Intramuscular adrenaline into the anterolateral thigh

C-OLD-25.s: Urticaria and anaphylaxis are which type of hypersensitivity reaction?

C-OLD-26.s: A patient who survived anaphylactic shock is being discharged. What is the most important item to provide?
C-OLD-26.a: An adrenaline auto-injector with training and a written action plan

C-MCQ-09.s: A 72-year-old man presents with 2 days of worsening dyspnoea and confusion. Vital signs: PR 132/min irregularly irregular, BP 80/58 mmHg, RR 28/min, SpO2 88% on room air. He has cool mottled extremities with capillary refill of 5 seconds, JVP 8 cm above the sternal angle, bibasilar crepitations to the mid zones and an S3 gallop. Chest radiograph shows cardiomegaly with bilateral perihilar opacities. Serum lactate 5.0 mmol/L, creatinine rising from 0.9 to 1.9 mg/dL. Which of the following best describes the type of shock and the most appropriate immediate intervention?
C-MCQ-09.a: Cardiogenic shock; urgent synchronised cardioversion or rate control with haemodynamic support
C-MCQ-09.p: แยก cardiogenic จาก tamponade/PE ด้วย **ปอด**: cardiogenic = crepitation + S3 + pulmonary edema; obstructive = ปอด clear + JVP สูง. แยกจาก hypovolemic ด้วย **JVP/IVC**

C-OLD-21.s: A hypotensive patient has an irregularly irregular tachycardia at 150/min, elevated JVP and cold clammy skin. Which is the most appropriate immediate treatment?

C-OLD-22.s: A 72-year-old man with atrial fibrillation at 130/min develops acute hemiparesis and hypotension. What is the most likely mechanism of the neurological event?

CAR-IHD-MCQ-01.s: A 54-year-old man with no prior cardiac symptoms suddenly develops crushing chest pain at rest. Angiography during the event shows an occluded vessel at a site that had only 40% stenosis on a CT angiogram performed two years earlier. Which mechanism best explains this?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-01.a: Rupture of a lipid-rich, thin-capped plaque with superimposed thrombosis
CAR-IHD-MCQ-01.p: รอยโรคตีบน้อยก็ทำให้เกิด MI ได้ — จึงต้องรักษาทั้งระบบด้วยยา ไม่ใช่แค่ขยายจุดที่ตีบมาก

C-MCQ-14.s: A 55-year-old smoker with a 30 pack-year history collapses at work with crushing chest pain. ECG shows ST elevation in V1-V4. He had been completely asymptomatic and a treadmill test 1 year ago was normal. Coronary angiography shows total thrombotic occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery with only a 40% stenosis in the adjacent segment. Which of the following best explains the pathogenesis of his presentation?
C-MCQ-14.a: Rupture of a lipid-rich plaque with a thin fibrous cap, triggering platelet aggregation and thrombus formation
C-MCQ-14.p: จุดหลอกที่ออกซ้ำ: "ผู้ป่วยเจ็บหน้าอกแต่ CAG ไม่เจอหลอดเลือดตีบ" → นึกถึง **MINOCA** (plaque erosion, vasospasm, microvascular dysfunction, SCAD, myocarditis, embolism) ไม่ใช่ "ไม่เป็นอะไร"

C-OLD-35.s: What is the most common underlying mechanism of ST-elevation myocardial infarction?
C-OLD-35.a: Rupture or erosion of an atherosclerotic plaque with superimposed thrombus

CAR-IHD-MCQ-02.s: A 38-year-old woman describes sharp left-sided chest pain lasting seconds, unrelated to exertion and reproducible by pressing on the chest wall. Resting ECG and echocardiography are normal. According to the ESC stepwise approach, what is the most appropriate next step?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-02.a: Conclude the pain is non-anginal with very low pretest probability and avoid further ischaemia testing
CAR-IHD-MCQ-02.p: PTP ต่ำมาก อย่าตรวจ — ผลบวกส่วนใหญ่จะเป็นบวกลวงและพาไปสู่การตรวจที่รุกล้ำโดยเปล่าประโยชน์

CAR-IHD-MCQ-03.a: Substernal discomfort, provoked by exertion or emotional stress, relieved by rest or nitrates within minutes
CAR-IHD-MCQ-03.p: สามข้อของ typical angina: ตำแหน่ง · ถูกกระตุ้นด้วยการออกแรง · หายเมื่อพักหรือไนเตรต

C-OLD-40.s: What is the mechanism of chest pain that occurs on exertion and resolves with rest in stable coronary disease?
C-OLD-40.a: A fixed atherosclerotic stenosis limits flow so supply cannot meet the increased myocardial oxygen demand

C-OLD-38.s: A 58-year-old man has retrosternal tightness on exertion for 3 months that resolves within 5 minutes of rest. ECG, troponin and chest radiograph at rest are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

C-OLD-48.s: A patient presents with exertional dyspnoea and chest discomfort. What is the most appropriate first investigation?

CAR-IHD-MCQ-04.s: A 60-year-old man with chronic coronary syndrome has been symptom-free for a year on aspirin, atorvastatin and bisoprolol. He asks to stop all medication because he feels well. Which explanation is most accurate?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-04.a: Aspirin and statin reduce future events and death independently of symptoms, so they should continue
CAR-IHD-MCQ-04.p: ไม่มีอาการ ≠ หายจากโรค — statin และ antiplatelet ป้องกันเหตุการณ์ในอนาคต ต้องกินต่อ

CAR-IHD-MCQ-05.s: A 46-year-old smoker has recurrent chest pain at rest between 2 and 5 a.m. ECG during an episode shows transient ST elevation that resolves completely with sublingual nitrate. Coronary angiography shows no significant fixed stenosis. Which treatment should be AVOIDED?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-05.p: ST ยกชั่วคราวตอนกลางดึกแล้วหายสนิท + หลอดเลือดไม่ตีบ = vasospastic angina → ห้าม beta-blocker

C-OLD-49.s: Which statement about the management of chronic stable angina is correct?
C-OLD-49.a: Short-acting nifedipine should not be used because reflex tachycardia may worsen ischaemia

C-MCQ-17.s: A 58-year-old woman has a 6-month history of exertional retrosternal chest tightness relieved by rest. An exercise treadmill test reproduced her symptoms with 1.5 mm of ST depression. Coronary angiography shows smooth epicardial coronary arteries with no obstructive stenosis. Coronary flow reserve measured during the study is 1.8 (normal greater than 2.5). Which of the following best explains her angina?
C-MCQ-17.a: Impaired coronary microvascular vasodilator capacity causing supply-demand mismatch
C-MCQ-17.p: เวลาเจอ "เจ็บหน้าอกแต่ CAG ปกติ" จำกลุ่ม MINOCA/INOCA: **microvascular dysfunction, vasospastic angina (Prinzmetal), SCAD, plaque erosion, coronary embolism, myocarditis, Takotsubo** — ห้ามสรุปว่า "ไม่ใช่โรคหัวใจ"

C-OLD-41.s: A patient with typical angina has normal epicardial coronary arteries on angiography. What is the most likely explanation?
C-OLD-41.a: Coronary microvascular dysfunction with supply-demand mismatch

CAR-IHD-MCQ-06.s: A 70-year-old woman with sepsis and acute kidney injury has a high-sensitivity troponin of 80 ng/L (99th percentile 14 ng/L) on a routine panel. She has no chest pain, her ECG is unchanged from baseline, and echocardiography shows no new wall motion abnormality. What is the most appropriate interpretation?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-06.a: Myocardial injury without evidence of ischaemia; this does not meet the definition of acute MI
CAR-IHD-MCQ-06.p: Troponin ขึ้น + ไม่มีหลักฐานขาดเลือด = myocardial injury ไม่ใช่ MI — รักษาสาเหตุหลักและดูแนวโน้ม

C-OLD-36.s: Which chest pain pattern is most consistent with acute coronary syndrome?
C-OLD-36.a: Pain at rest or with a crescendo pattern, radiating to the jaw or arm, with diaphoresis

CAR-IHD-MCQ-07.s: A 35-year-old man has 40 minutes of crushing chest pain. ECG shows 2 mm ST elevation in V2 and V3, with no LVH or LBBB. Which statement is correct?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-07.a: This does not meet the V2-V3 threshold for men under 40 years, which is 2.5 mm; repeat the ECG and consider additional leads
CAR-IHD-MCQ-07.p: ชาย < 40 ปี ต้อง ≥ 2.5 mm ใน V2–V3 — ไม่ถึงเกณฑ์ไม่ได้แปลว่าไม่ใช่ ACS ให้ทำ ECG ซ้ำและเพิ่มลีด

CAR-IHD-MCQ-08.s: A 62-year-old man with ongoing chest pain has ECG showing 2 mm ST depression in V1-V3 with tall, upright terminal T waves. Which is the most appropriate next step?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-08.a: Record posterior leads V7-V9 looking for ST elevation of at least 0.5 mm
CAR-IHD-MCQ-08.p: ST depression V1–V3 + T ปลายบวก = ทำ V7–V9 ทันที — อย่าเรียกเป็น NSTEMI แล้วรอ

C-OLD-42.s: An ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF. Which additional leads should be recorded?

C-OLD-43.s: ST elevation in leads V1 to V4 corresponds to infarction of which wall and which artery?
C-OLD-43.a: Anterior wall — left anterior descending artery

C-OLD-53.s: When reading a 12-lead ECG of suspected STEMI, which sequence should be described?
C-OLD-53.a: Rate, rhythm, axis, intervals, chamber enlargement, ST-T changes and Q waves

C-OLD-54.s: An ECG shows ST elevation in II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL, rate 75/min, sinus rhythm and narrow QRS. What is the complete interpretation?
C-OLD-54.a: Normal sinus rhythm with acute inferior wall ST-elevation myocardial infarction

C-OLD-51.s: A 60-year-old woman with diabetes, dyslipidaemia and known coronary disease has 10 minutes of chest tightness. ECG shows ST elevation in I, aVL and V2-V6 with reciprocal depression in II, III and aVF, and troponin-I is 8 ng/mL. What is the diagnosis?

C-MCQ-15.s: A 60-year-old man presents with 90 minutes of chest pain and nausea. ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with ST elevation greater in III than in II, and reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL. Vital signs on arrival: PR 58/min, BP 118/74 mmHg, lungs clear, JVP 7 cm above the sternal angle. Sublingual nitroglycerine is given and his blood pressure falls to 72/48 mmHg. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management, and which additional ECG leads would confirm the underlying problem?
C-MCQ-15.a: Rapid intravenous isotonic saline; record leads V3R and V4R
C-MCQ-15.p: **Inferior STEMI + hypotension หลังให้ nitrate = RV infarct จนกว่าจะพิสูจน์ว่าไม่ใช่** → ให้น้ำ ไม่ให้ยาลด preload; และระวัง AV block เพราะ RCA เลี้ยง AV node

CAR-IHD-MCQ-09.s: A patient is diagnosed with STEMI at a rural hospital without a catheterisation laboratory. The nearest PCI centre is 3 hours away by road, so expected first-medical-contact-to-wire time is about 200 minutes. What is the most appropriate management?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-09.a: Give fibrinolysis within 10 minutes of STEMI diagnosis, then transfer to a PCI centre
CAR-IHD-MCQ-09.p: คาดว่าเกิน 120 นาทีถึง wire = ให้ยาละลายลิ่มเลือดภายใน 10 นาที แล้วส่งต่อ — STEMI ไม่ต้องรอ troponin

C-MCQ-11.s: A 58-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension presents 70 minutes after the onset of crushing retrosternal chest pain radiating to the left jaw, with diaphoresis. Vital signs: PR 96/min, BP 138/86 mmHg, lungs clear. ECG shows ST elevation of 3 mm in leads I, aVL and V2-V6 with reciprocal ST depression in II, III and aVF. High-sensitivity troponin-I is elevated. Your hospital has no catheterisation laboratory, but a PCI-capable centre can receive the patient and inflate the balloon 95 minutes from now. Which of the following is the most appropriate reperfusion strategy?
C-MCQ-11.a: Transfer immediately for primary percutaneous coronary intervention
C-MCQ-11.p: จำตัวเลข: door-to-balloon **≤90 นาที** (รพ.ที่มี cath lab), first medical contact-to-PCI **≤120 นาที**, door-to-needle ของ fibrinolytic **≤30 นาที (ควร ≤10)**. ข้อสอบชอบให้เวลา "120 นาที" แล้วดูว่าจะเลือกอะไร

C-OLD-33.s: A patient with ST elevation in V1-V4 and elevated troponin-T can reach a PCI-capable centre within 120 minutes of first medical contact. What is the most appropriate reperfusion strategy?
C-OLD-33.a: Transfer for primary percutaneous coronary intervention

C-OLD-52.s: Why is primary PCI preferred over fibrinolysis when both are available within the recommended time?
C-OLD-52.a: It achieves higher rates of vessel patency with lower rates of reinfarction and intracranial haemorrhage

C-OLD-34.s: A patient with acute coronary syndrome has been given aspirin, a P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulant, statin and nitrate. What is the definitive next step in STEMI?
C-OLD-34.a: Reperfusion therapy — primary PCI or fibrinolysis

CAR-IHD-MCQ-10.s: Ninety minutes after fibrinolysis for an inferior STEMI, the patient still has chest pain and the ST elevation has decreased by only 20%. What is the most appropriate management?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-10.a: Immediate transfer for rescue percutaneous coronary intervention
CAR-IHD-MCQ-10.p: ST ลดน้อยกว่า 50% ที่ 60–90 นาที = ล้มเหลว → rescue PCI ทันที ห้ามให้ยาละลายลิ่มเลือดซ้ำ

C-MCQ-12.s: A 64-year-old man in a district hospital has an inferior STEMI that began 2 hours ago. The nearest PCI centre is 4 hours away by road. Vital signs: PR 88/min, BP 150/92 mmHg. Which of the following features in his history would be an absolute contraindication to fibrinolytic therapy?
C-MCQ-12.a: Ischaemic stroke with residual hemiparesis 3 weeks ago
C-MCQ-12.p: ถ้ามี absolute contraindication ต่อ fibrinolytic ใน STEMI → ต้อง **ส่งไปทำ primary PCI ไม่ว่าจะไกลแค่ไหน** (transfer for PCI เป็นทางเดียว); อย่าตอบ "รักษาแบบ medical เฉยๆ"

C-OLD-50.s: A patient with an anterolateral STEMI is treated with fibrinolysis. Which finding best indicates successful reperfusion at 90 minutes?
C-OLD-50.a: Resolution of ST elevation by more than 50 percent with relief of chest pain

CAR-IHD-MCQ-11.s: According to the 2020 ESC NSTE-ACS guideline as presented, which statement about biomarkers is correct?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-11.a: Routine measurement of CK, CK-MB, h-FABP or copeptin in addition to hs-cTn is NOT recommended
CAR-IHD-MCQ-11.p: ยุค hs-troponin: เลิกส่ง CK-MB เป็นกิจวัตร · BNP ใช้บอกพยากรณ์ ไม่ใช่วินิจฉัย

C-MCQ-13.s: A 62-year-old woman with hypertension and dyslipidaemia presents with three episodes of retrosternal pressure in the past 24 hours, each lasting 20 minutes, the last occurring at rest 1 hour ago and now resolved. Previously her chest discomfort occurred only on walking uphill and resolved with rest. Vital signs and cardiac examination are normal. The initial 12-lead ECG and high-sensitivity troponin-I are both normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
C-MCQ-13.a: Admit for serial ECG and repeat high-sensitivity troponin, and start aspirin plus an anticoagulant
C-MCQ-13.p: Typical angina 3 ข้อ: (1) retrosternal, (2) เกิดจาก exertion/emotion, (3) ดีขึ้นด้วยพักหรือ nitrate — ครบ 3 = typical, 2 = atypical, ≤1 = non-cardiac. ข้อสอบเก่าถามซ้ำว่าอันไหน "considered ACS" → **pain radiating to back/jaw + rest pain + crescendo**, ไม่ใช่ pain on exertion only

C-OLD-37.s: A patient has typical chest pain at rest for 20 minutes with dyspnoea. ECG shows no ST elevation and troponin is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

C-OLD-39.s: A patient with ongoing chest pain has a normal ECG and normal initial troponin-I taken 1 hour after pain onset. What is the most appropriate next step?
C-OLD-39.a: Repeat ECG and troponin serially over the next few hours

CAR-IHD-MCQ-12.s: A 68-year-old man with NSTE-ACS has ongoing chest pain despite nitrates and morphine, blood pressure 82/50 mmHg, and ECG showing 2 mm ST depression in leads I, II, aVL, V4-V6 with ST elevation in aVR. What is the recommended timing of invasive strategy?
