CAR-IHD-MCQ-12.p: ช็อก หรือเจ็บไม่หยุดแม้ให้ยา หรือ ST depression ≥ 6 ลีด + aVR ยก = สวนภายใน 2 ชั่วโมง

CAR-IHD-MCQ-13.s: A haemodynamically stable 55-year-old man with NSTEMI has no recurrent pain after treatment and a GRACE risk score of 165. When should invasive angiography be performed?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-13.p: NSTEMI หรือ GRACE > 140 = สวนภายใน 24 ชั่วโมง — stress test ก่อนใช้เฉพาะกลุ่มเสี่ยงต่ำ

CAR-IHD-MCQ-14.s: A 72-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on apixaban presents with NSTEMI and undergoes PCI with a drug-eluting stent. Which antithrombotic regimen best matches the guideline presented?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-14.a: Apixaban, aspirin and clopidogrel for up to 1 week, then apixaban plus clopidogrel until 12 months, then apixaban alone
CAR-IHD-MCQ-14.p: AF + PCI: TAT 1 สัปดาห์ → NOAC + clopidogrel ถึง 12 เดือน → NOAC เดี่ยว — ห้าม ticagrelor/prasugrel ใน TAT

CAR-IHD-MCQ-15.s: A 58-year-old man with NSTE-ACS and a history of ischaemic stroke 3 years ago is scheduled for PCI. Which P2Y12 inhibitor is CONTRAINDICATED?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-15.p: เคยเป็น stroke หรือ TIA = ห้าม prasugrel เด็ดขาด — เลือก ticagrelor หรือ clopidogrel แทน

CAR-IHD-MCQ-16.s: Which secondary prevention measure after myocardial infarction is described in the lecture as potentially the most cost-effective of all, with a 36% reduction in mortality among those who succeed?
CAR-IHD-MCQ-16.p: เลิกบุหรี่ = ลดตาย 36% · cardiac rehab = ลดตายจากหัวใจ 22% — สองตัวเลขนี้จำให้แม่น

C-MCQ-16.s: Which of the following patients has the strongest indication for high-intensity statin therapy regardless of the baseline LDL-cholesterol level?
C-MCQ-16.a: A 60-year-old man 2 days after an acute ischaemic stroke of atherosclerotic origin
C-MCQ-16.p: ก่อนเริ่ม statin ต้อง **คัด secondary cause ของ dyslipidemia**: hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis, DM ที่คุมไม่ได้, แอลกอฮอล์, ยา (steroid, thiazide, retinoid, protease inhibitor). ระวัง **statin + fibrate = rhabdomyolysis** ซึ่งเป็นโจทย์ MEQ ของ MED33

C-OLD-45.s: Which patient has the clearest indication for high-intensity statin therapy?
C-OLD-45.a: A 60-year-old man 2 weeks after an acute ischaemic stroke of atherosclerotic origin

C-OLD-46.s: A 35-year-old man whose father died of myocardial infarction at 40 has LDL 260 mg/dL, tendon xanthomata at the Achilles tendon and corneal arcus. Which defect is most likely?

C-OLD-47.s: A 28-year-old asymptomatic man has a strong family history of premature coronary disease. Which investigation is most appropriate first?

C-OLD-55.s: After reperfusion, which combination is standard long-term secondary prevention following myocardial infarction?
C-OLD-55.a: Dual antiplatelet therapy, high-intensity statin, beta-blocker and ACE inhibitor with risk-factor control

C-OLD-44.s: Three days after an inferior STEMI a patient develops acute dyspnoea, hypotension and a new loud pansystolic murmur with a thrill at the lower sternal border. What is the most likely complication?
C-OLD-44.a: Mechanical complication — ventricular septal rupture or acute mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture

CAR-AF-MCQ-01.s: Compared with people in sinus rhythm, approximately how much does atrial fibrillation increase the risk of ischaemic stroke?

CAR-AF-MCQ-02.s: Where in the heart do thrombi most commonly form in patients with atrial fibrillation?
CAR-AF-MCQ-02.p: ลิ่มเลือดใน AF เกิดที่ LAA มากที่สุด

CAR-AF-MCQ-03.s: A 34-year-old woman with new-onset atrial fibrillation has had 4 kg weight loss, tremor and heat intolerance. Which blood test must be checked first to identify a reversible cause?
CAR-AF-MCQ-03.p: AF ใหม่ทุกราย → ตรวจไทรอยด์

C-MCQ-21.s: A 42-year-old man reports recurrent episodes of palpitations with an irregular pulse, each lasting several hours and resolving spontaneously. The episodes characteristically occur on Monday mornings after heavy weekend drinking. He has no hypertension, no diabetes and no structural heart disease; echocardiography and thyroid function tests are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis and the most appropriate intervention?
C-MCQ-21.a: Alcohol-induced paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; advise abstinence from alcohol
C-MCQ-21.p: New-onset AF ต้องคัด reversible cause ทุกครั้ง: **thyrotoxicosis, แอลกอฮอล์, OSA, ไข้/ติดเชื้อ, hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia, PE, ischemia, ยา (theophylline, sympathomimetic)**

C-OLD-61.s: A 45-year-old man has palpitations every Monday after weekend drinking. ECG during symptoms shows atrial fibrillation that terminates spontaneously. What is the most likely precipitant?

C-OLD-62.s: Untreated hyperthyroidism most characteristically precipitates which arrhythmia?

C-OLD-63.s: A patient has fever 39 C, heart failure, atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, agitation and suppressed TSH with high free T4. What is the diagnosis?

C-OLD-64.s: A patient presents with palpitations and an otherwise normal examination. Which two investigations are most appropriate first?

C-OLD-69.s: An ECG shows sinus tachycardia in a patient with weight loss, tremor and heat intolerance. What is the most likely diagnosis?

CAR-AF-MCQ-04.s: A 68-year-old man has AF at 170/min. He is confused, BP 76/44 mmHg, with cold extremities and crackles to the mid-zones. Which features make this AF 'haemodynamically unstable'?
CAR-AF-MCQ-04.a: Hypotension, altered mental status and acute pulmonary oedema
CAR-AF-MCQ-04.p: Unstable = hypotension · ซึม · pulmonary edema · chest pain · shock

C-OLD-59.s: What is the characteristic physical finding of atrial fibrillation?
C-OLD-59.a: An irregularly irregular pulse with a pulse deficit

C-OLD-67.s: A patient with known heart failure develops palpitations with an irregular tachycardia at 150/min and worsening dyspnoea. What is the most likely arrhythmia?
C-OLD-67.a: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

C-OLD-68.s: An 80-year-old man has palpitations followed by transient loss of consciousness. BP 140/90 mmHg, pulse irregular 110-160/min. What is the most likely cause of the syncope?
C-OLD-68.a: Reduced cardiac output from the rapid irregular ventricular rate

C-OLD-70.s: A patient with palpitations and dyspnoea has no palpable pulse but is conscious and talking. The monitor shows atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. What should be done?
C-OLD-70.a: Recheck the pulse and monitor leads; if the patient is unstable, perform synchronised cardioversion

CAR-AF-MCQ-05.s: Which combination of ECG findings fulfils the lecture's three criteria for atrial fibrillation?
CAR-AF-MCQ-05.a: Irregular R-R, no distinct P waves, atrial rate above 300/min
CAR-AF-MCQ-05.p: AF: R-R ไม่สม่ำเสมอ + ไม่มี P + atrial rate > 300

CAR-AF-MCQ-06.s: A 63-year-old man's smartwatch (photoplethysmography only, no ECG function) alerts him to 'possible AF'. He feels well. What is the next step?
CAR-AF-MCQ-06.a: Confirm with an ECG-based recording (12-lead ECG or ambulatory ECG)
CAR-AF-MCQ-06.p: PPG/smartwatch → ยืนยันด้วย ECG ก่อนเสมอ

C-OLD-71.s: An ECG shows an irregularly irregular rhythm with absent P waves and a ventricular rate of 130/min. What is the interpretation?
C-OLD-71.a: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

C-OLD-60.s: An elderly patient with tachy-brady syndrome has an irregularly irregular pulse alternating with pauses and dizziness. What is the underlying problem?
C-OLD-60.a: Sick sinus syndrome with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation

CAR-AF-MCQ-07.s: A patient has had continuous atrial fibrillation for 3 weeks. Which stage is this?
CAR-AF-MCQ-07.p: > 7 วัน = persistent · > 1 ปี = long-standing

CAR-AF-MCQ-08.s: A woman with AF reports palpitations and fatigue that stop her from doing her usual housework. What is her EHRA symptom class?
CAR-AF-MCQ-08.p: EHRA III = กระทบกิจวัตร · IV = หยุดกิจวัตร

CAR-AF-MCQ-09.s: A 72-year-old woman with hypertension and type 2 diabetes has non-valvular AF. What is her CHA2DS2-VASc score?
CAR-AF-MCQ-09.p: อายุ 65–74 = 1 · ≥ 75 = 2 · หญิง +1 ใน VASc

CAR-AF-MCQ-10.s: A 55-year-old man with paroxysmal AF has no hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, vascular disease or prior stroke. What is the recommendation for stroke prevention?
CAR-AF-MCQ-10.a: No antithrombotic therapy; reassess risk factors periodically
CAR-AF-MCQ-10.p: CHA₂DS₂-VASc 0 ชาย/1 หญิง → ไม่ต้องให้ยา · ประเมินซ้ำ

CAR-AF-MCQ-11.s: Under the ESC 2024 approach (CHA2DS2-VA), what is the main change from CHA2DS2-VASc?
CAR-AF-MCQ-11.a: Female sex is no longer scored
CAR-AF-MCQ-11.p: CHA₂DS₂-VA = ตัดคะแนนเพศ

C-MCQ-18.s: A 70-year-old woman with hypertension and type 2 diabetes is found to have an irregularly irregular pulse. ECG confirms atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of 92/min. She has no valvular disease on echocardiography and no history of stroke or bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to decide on antithrombotic therapy?
C-MCQ-18.a: Calculate the CHA2DS2-VASc score and start a direct oral anticoagulant if the score is 2 or more in women
C-MCQ-18.p: **Valvular AF (rheumatic mitral stenosis ระดับ moderate-severe หรือ mechanical valve) ต้องใช้ warfarin ห้ามใช้ DOAC** — ข้อสอบไทยชอบออกเพราะ RHD ยังพบมาก. ระวังความต่างของแนวทาง: **ACC/AHA ใช้เกณฑ์ ≥2 ทั้งสองเพศ** แต่ **ESC ใช้ชาย ≥2 / หญิง ≥3 เป็น class I (ชาย 1 / หญิง 2 = class IIa)** — ถ้าอาจารย์สอนตาม ESC ให้ตอบตามเกณฑ์แยกเพศ

C-OLD-56.s: Which score should be used to decide on anticoagulation for stroke prevention in non-valvular atrial fibrillation?

C-OLD-66.s: A patient with atrial flutter develops an embolic stroke. What is the underlying mechanism?
C-OLD-66.a: Thrombus formation in the fibrillating/fluttering atrium with embolisation

CAR-AF-MCQ-12.s: Which anticoagulant's effect is reversed specifically by idarucizumab?

CAR-AF-MCQ-13.s: A 78-year-old woman weighing 55 kg with non-valvular AF has serum creatinine 1.2 mg/dL. Which apixaban dose is appropriate?
CAR-AF-MCQ-13.p: Apixaban ลดขนาดเมื่อเข้า 2 ใน 3 (≥ 80 ปี · ≤ 60 กก. · Cr ≥ 1.5)

C-MCQ-22.s: A 48-year-old woman with rheumatic heart disease and moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis (mitral valve area 1.2 cm2) develops atrial fibrillation. Her CHA2DS2-VASc score is 2. Renal and liver function are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate antithrombotic therapy?
C-MCQ-22.a: Warfarin with a target INR of 2.0 to 3.0
C-MCQ-22.p: สรุปที่ต้องจำ: **Mechanical valve + moderate/severe rheumatic MS = warfarin เท่านั้น**; DOAC ใช้ได้ใน non-valvular AF และ bioprosthetic valve (หลัง 3 เดือนแรก). AF + MS ยังเป็นต้นเหตุคลาสสิกของ stroke ในข้อสอบ

C-OLD-65.s: A patient with rheumatic mitral stenosis and atrial fibrillation develops sudden right hemiparesis. Which anticoagulant is indicated?

CAR-AF-MCQ-14.s: A patient taking warfarin 2 mg daily for AF has an INR of 1.0 today (previous INRs were 2.3–2.6). What should be done first?
CAR-AF-MCQ-14.a: Ask how the patient has been taking the medication before changing the dose
CAR-AF-MCQ-14.p: INR ต่ำผิดคาด → ถามการกินยาก่อน

CAR-AF-MCQ-15.s: A patient on warfarin 5 mg daily (35 mg/week) has INR 3.5 with no bleeding. Diet and medicines are unchanged. Which adjustment matches the lecture's rule?
CAR-AF-MCQ-15.a: Hold one dose, then reduce to about 31.5 mg/week (4.5 mg daily)
CAR-AF-MCQ-15.p: INR 3–5 ไม่มีเลือดออก: งด 1 วัน + ลด 10%/สัปดาห์

CAR-AF-MCQ-16.s: A patient on warfarin presents with melaena, BP 84/50 mmHg and INR 6.8. Which management is most appropriate in addition to resuscitation?
CAR-AF-MCQ-16.a: Stop warfarin, give vitamin K 10 mg intravenously and replace clotting factors with FFP or PCC
CAR-AF-MCQ-16.p: Warfarin + major bleed: vit K 10 มก. IV + FFP/PCC

CAR-AF-MCQ-17.s: A 66-year-old man with severe COPD (frequent bronchospasm) has persistent AF at 128/min, BP 138/84 mmHg and normal LVEF. Which first-line rate-control drug is most suitable?

CAR-AF-MCQ-18.s: A 25-year-old man has an irregular, very rapid, wide-complex tachycardia at 240/min with varying QRS width; his resting ECG shows a short PR and delta wave. BP is 118/72 mmHg. Which drug must be AVOIDED?
CAR-AF-MCQ-18.p: Pre-excited AF: ห้าม AV nodal blocker

C-OLD-57.s: A 70-year-old man with atrial fibrillation at 140/min, stable blood pressure and no heart failure needs rate control. Which drug is most appropriate first?
C-OLD-57.a: A beta-blocker such as metoprolol (or a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker)

C-OLD-58.s: Which drug controls symptoms of atrial fibrillation by controlling rate or rhythm rather than preventing stroke?

C-MCQ-19.s: A 76-year-old man with known heart failure (LVEF 28%) presents with 3 days of orthopnoea. Vital signs: PR 148/min irregularly irregular, BP 88/60 mmHg, RR 26/min, SpO2 90% on room air. He has JVP 9 cm, bibasilar crepitations and 2+ pedal oedema. ECG shows atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response and no pre-excitation. He is alert and not in extremis. Which of the following is the most appropriate drug for ventricular rate control in this patient?
C-MCQ-19.p: AF + **pre-excitation (WPW)**: **ห้ามให้ digoxin, β-blocker, verapamil/diltiazem, adenosine** เพราะบล็อก AV node ทำให้ impulse ไปลง accessory pathway ทั้งหมด → VF; ให้ **procainamide หรือ cardioversion**

CAR-AF-MCQ-19.s: A 60-year-old man has had AF for an unknown duration with palpitations; he is haemodynamically stable. Elective cardioversion is planned. Which approach is correct?
CAR-AF-MCQ-19.a: Anticoagulate for 3 weeks before and at least 4 weeks after cardioversion, or perform TEE to exclude thrombus first
CAR-AF-MCQ-19.p: Elective CV: OAC 3 สัปดาห์ก่อน + 4 สัปดาห์หลัง หรือ TEE

C-MCQ-20.s: A 59-year-old man presents with palpitations and dizziness. Vital signs: PR 186/min, BP 74/46 mmHg, RR 28/min. He is diaphoretic, confused and has cool extremities. ECG shows a regular monomorphic wide-complex tachycardia at 186/min. A carotid pulse is palpable. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management?
C-MCQ-20.p: ตาราง 3 สถานการณ์: **มี pulse + stable** → ยา; **มี pulse + unstable** → synchronised cardioversion; **ไม่มี pulse** → unsynchronised defibrillation + CPR. Pulseless VT/VF = **defibrillation ทันทีเป็นสิ่งสำคัญที่สุด**

CAR-AF-MCQ-20.s: A 52-year-old man with paroxysmal AF has BMI 33 kg/m², untreated hypertension, snoring with daytime sleepiness and drinks heavily at weekends. Which intervention is MOST likely to reduce his AF burden over the long term?
CAR-AF-MCQ-20.a: Comprehensive risk-factor management: weight loss, BP control with ACEI/ARB, treatment of sleep apnoea and alcohol reduction
CAR-AF-MCQ-20.p: C: ลดน้ำหนัก คุมความดัน รักษา OSA ลดสุรา → AF ลดลง

CAR-VHD-MCQ-01.s: On examination a harsh systolic murmur is accompanied by a palpable vibration over the same area. What is the minimum grade of this murmur?

CAR-VHD-MCQ-02.s: Which murmur is characteristically low-pitched, heard best with the bell at the apex in the left lateral decubitus position?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-02.p: Rumbling + bell + ตะแคงซ้าย = MS

C-OLD-82.s: A continuous machinery murmur heard below the left clavicle in a young adult suggests which lesion?

C-OLD-91.s: A patient has right atrial and right ventricular enlargement with a fixed widely split S2 and a systolic murmur at the left upper sternal border. What is the most likely diagnosis?

C-OLD-81.s: Three days after an acute myocardial infarction a patient develops a new pansystolic murmur at the lower left sternal border with a thrill and acute pulmonary oedema. What is the most likely cause?

C-OLD-83.s: A patient has a loud P2, elevated JVP, hepatomegaly and leg oedema with clear lungs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
C-OLD-83.a: Pulmonary hypertension with right heart failure

CAR-VHD-MCQ-03.s: In mitral stenosis, which finding indicates more severe stenosis?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-03.a: A shorter interval between S2 and the opening snap
CAR-VHD-MCQ-03.p: S2–OS สั้น + rumble ยาว = MS รุนแรง

CAR-VHD-MCQ-04.s: A 38-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis develops hoarseness. What is the mechanism?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-04.a: Compression of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve by an enlarged left atrium or pulmonary artery (Ortner's syndrome)
CAR-VHD-MCQ-04.p: เสียงแหบใน MS = Ortner's syndrome

C-MCQ-23.s: A 45-year-old woman from a rural province presents with 1 year of progressive exertional dyspnoea and recent haemoptysis. Which of the following physical findings is most consistent with mitral stenosis?
C-MCQ-23.a: An early diastolic high-frequency sound following S2 at the apex, followed by a low-pitched diastolic rumble
C-MCQ-23.p: MS ที่ออกสอบซ้ำทุกปี: **diastolic rumbling murmur at apex + opening snap + loud S1 + loud P2**; complication ที่ต้องนึกถึงคือ **AF, systemic embolism, pulmonary HT → RHF, hemoptysis** และในหญิงตั้งครรภ์จะ decompensate เพราะ HR และ volume เพิ่ม

C-OLD-72.s: Which physical finding is consistent with mitral stenosis?
C-OLD-72.a: An opening snap followed by a diastolic rumbling murmur at the apex

C-OLD-73.s: Which finding is NOT a sign of mitral stenosis?
C-OLD-73.a: Systolic ejection murmur at the right upper parasternal border

C-OLD-74.s: A patient has a low-pitched diastolic rumbling murmur heard best at the apex in the left lateral decubitus position, with a loud S1. What is the diagnosis?

C-OLD-94.s: Which valve lesion is the most common long-term sequela of acute rheumatic fever in Thailand?

CAR-VHD-MCQ-05.s: A 35-year-old woman with symptomatic rheumatic mitral stenosis has MVA 1.1 cm², pliable non-calcified leaflets, only mild MR and no left atrial thrombus on TEE. What is the recommended intervention?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-05.p: MS มีอาการ + ลิ้นเหมาะ → PMBC

CAR-VHD-MCQ-06.s: A woman with moderate–severe rheumatic mitral stenosis develops atrial fibrillation. Which anticoagulant is recommended?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-06.p: Rheumatic MS + AF = warfarin ไม่ใช่ NOAC

C-OLD-92.s: Echocardiography in a patient with a murmur shows a thickened mitral valve with restricted opening and a mean gradient of 12 mmHg. What is the diagnosis?

C-OLD-93.s: A 40-year-old woman has 1 month of exertional dyspnoea and orthopnoea, an irregularly irregular pulse, a loud S1 with an opening snap and a diastolic rumble at the apex. What is the most likely complete diagnosis?
C-OLD-93.a: Rheumatic mitral stenosis with atrial fibrillation and heart failure

CAR-VHD-MCQ-07.s: Three days after an inferior STEMI, a patient suddenly develops severe pulmonary oedema and hypotension. A new, soft, short apical systolic murmur is heard without a thrill. What is the most likely cause?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-07.a: Papillary muscle rupture causing acute mitral regurgitation
CAR-VHD-MCQ-07.p: หลัง MI: murmur ที่ apex ไม่มี thrill + pulmonary edema = papillary rupture

C-MCQ-28.s: A 30-year-old woman is found to have a mid-systolic click followed by a late systolic murmur at the apex. On standing, the click occurs earlier and the murmur becomes longer; on squatting, the click moves later and the murmur shortens. Echocardiography shows billowing of the posterior mitral leaflet into the left atrium with mild mitral regurgitation and normal left ventricular size. Which of the following best explains the change in auscultatory findings on standing?
C-MCQ-28.a: Reduced left ventricular end-diastolic volume allows the leaflet to prolapse earlier in systole
C-MCQ-28.p: MVP เป็นสาเหตุอันดับหนึ่งของ **primary (degenerative) MR** ในประเทศพัฒนาแล้ว; ส่วนใหญ่ prognosis ดี แต่ติดตาม severity ของ MR, ขนาด LV, AF และความเสี่ยง IE. MR รุนแรงที่มีอาการหรือ LVEF ≤60% / LVESD ≥40 mm → ส่งผ่าตัดซ่อมลิ้น

C-OLD-79.s: A patient has a pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla, with bilateral leg oedema and lung crepitations. What is the diagnosis?
C-OLD-79.a: Mitral regurgitation with congestive heart failure

C-OLD-80.s: A young woman has a mid-systolic click followed by a late systolic murmur that moves earlier on standing. What is the diagnosis?

CAR-VHD-MCQ-08.s: An asymptomatic 55-year-old man has severe primary mitral regurgitation from a flail posterior leaflet. LVEF is 58% and LVESD 42 mm. What is the recommended management?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-08.p: Primary MR ไม่มีอาการ + LVEF ≤ 60 หรือ LVESD ≥ 40 → ผ่าตัด

CAR-VHD-MCQ-09.s: A 78-year-old man has exertional syncope. A harsh late-peaking systolic murmur is heard at the right upper sternal border radiating to both carotids. Echo: Vmax 4.6 m/s, mean gradient 52 mmHg, AVA 0.7 cm², LVEF 60%. Transfemoral access is suitable. According to the 2025 ESC/EACTS guideline, what is the preferred treatment?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-09.p: AS รุนแรงมีอาการ อายุ ≥ 70 → TAVI (ESC 2025)

C-MCQ-25.s: A 74-year-old man presents with exertional dyspnoea and two episodes of syncope while climbing stairs. Examination reveals a harsh late-peaking systolic ejection murmur at the right second intercostal space radiating to both carotids, a single S2 and a slow-rising low-amplitude carotid pulse. Echocardiography shows a calcified aortic valve with a mean gradient of 52 mmHg, aortic valve area 0.7 cm2 and LVEF 58%. Which of the following is NOT an expected complication of his condition?
C-MCQ-25.a: Wide pulse pressure with a bounding peripheral pulse
C-MCQ-25.p: Severe AS criteria: **Vmax ≥4 m/s, mean gradient ≥40 mmHg, AVA ≤1.0 cm2**. ในผู้สูงอายุสาเหตุอันดับหนึ่งคือ **calcific degeneration**; อายุ <65 คิดถึง **bicuspid aortic valve**; ในไทยยังต้องนึกถึง **rheumatic** ซึ่งมักมี mitral ร่วม

C-OLD-77.s: A systolic ejection murmur at the right upper sternal border radiating to the carotids with a slow-rising pulse indicates which lesion?

C-OLD-78.s: Which finding is NOT expected in severe aortic stenosis?
C-OLD-78.a: Wide pulse pressure with a collapsing pulse

CAR-VHD-MCQ-10.s: A diastolic blowing murmur of aortic regurgitation is heard loudest at the right second intercostal space rather than the left third intercostal space. What does this suggest?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-10.a: Aortic root disease such as Marfan syndrome or dissection
CAR-VHD-MCQ-10.p: AR ดังที่ ICS 2 ขวา = root disease

CAR-VHD-MCQ-11.s: An asymptomatic 46-year-old man has severe chronic aortic regurgitation. LVEF is 48% with no other cause. What is the recommended management?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-11.p: AR ไม่มีอาการ + LVEF ≤ 50% → AVR

C-MCQ-24.s: A tall, thin 19-year-old woman presents with reduced vision and exertional dyspnoea. She has long arms, arachnodactyly and a high-arched palate. Vital signs: PR 78/min with a rapid upstroke and collapse, BP 180/55 mmHg. A high-pitched blowing decrescendo diastolic murmur is heard at the left sternal border, and the head nods with each heartbeat. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis, and which underlying condition should be suspected?
C-MCQ-24.a: Aortic regurgitation due to aortic root dilatation in Marfan syndrome
C-MCQ-24.p: **Acute AR** (จาก aortic dissection หรือ IE) ต่างจาก chronic โดยสิ้นเชิง: LV ยังไม่ dilate → LVEDP พุ่ง → **pulmonary edema + hypotension + murmur สั้นเบา** และ **ไม่มี wide pulse pressure** → เป็น surgical emergency

C-OLD-75.s: A patient has a wide pulse pressure with a high-pitched blowing decrescendo diastolic murmur at the left sternal border. What is the diagnosis?

C-OLD-76.s: A tall thin 19-year-old woman with long arms and arachnodactyly has BP 180/70 mmHg, a bounding pulse and a high-pitched blowing decrescendo diastolic murmur. What is the most likely underlying condition?
C-OLD-76.a: Aortic regurgitation from aortic root dilatation in Marfan syndrome

CAR-VHD-MCQ-12.s: A pansystolic murmur at the lower left sternal border becomes louder during inspiration. Which lesion is most likely?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-12.p: ดังขึ้นตอนหายใจเข้า = murmur ของหัวใจขวา

CAR-VHD-MCQ-13.s: A 10-year-old girl from a high-RHD-prevalence area has fever 38.2°C and arthritis of the right knee only, 3 weeks after a sore throat. ESR is 45 mm/h and ASO titre is raised. Echocardiography shows pathological mitral regurgitation not audible on auscultation. Under the 2015 revised Jones criteria, how should she be classified?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-13.a: Acute rheumatic fever: two major (subclinical carditis, monoarthritis) plus GAS evidence
CAR-VHD-MCQ-13.p: Jones 2015 ประชากรเสี่ยงสูง: monoarthritis + subclinical carditis นับเป็น major

CAR-VHD-MCQ-14.s: Which finding is a MINOR rather than a major Jones criterion?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-14.p: PR ยาว = minor ไม่ใช่ carditis

C-MCQ-26.s: A 14-year-old boy presents with fever and migratory joint pain that began in the right knee, then moved to the left ankle and left wrist over 5 days. He had a sore throat 3 weeks ago. Examination shows a temperature of 38.3 C, a new apical pansystolic murmur and painless subcutaneous nodules over the extensor surface of the elbows. ESR is 86 mm/h and anti-streptolysin O titre is markedly elevated. Throat swab culture is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation and management?
C-MCQ-26.a: Acute rheumatic fever; give benzathine penicillin G now and continue long-term secondary prophylaxis
C-MCQ-26.p: ระยะเวลาของ secondary prophylaxis: **ไม่มี carditis → 5 ปี หรือถึงอายุ 21 ปี**; **มี carditis แต่ไม่เหลือ valve disease → 10 ปี หรือถึงอายุ 21 ปี**; **มี carditis + residual valve disease → ≥10 ปี หรือถึงอายุ 40 ปี** แล้วแต่อันไหนนานกว่า (รายรุนแรงพิจารณาตลอดชีวิต)

C-OLD-84.s: A 12-year-old has migratory polyarthritis, a new murmur and fever 3 weeks after pharyngitis. Which investigation supports the diagnosis?

C-OLD-85.s: Which skin finding is a major manifestation of acute rheumatic fever?

CAR-VHD-MCQ-15.s: A 16-year-old had acute rheumatic fever with carditis and now has residual moderate mitral regurgitation. How long should secondary prophylaxis continue?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-15.a: At least 10 years after the last episode and at least until age 40, sometimes lifelong
CAR-VHD-MCQ-15.p: Carditis + ลิ้นเสีย → ≥ 10 ปี และถึงอายุ ≥ 40

CAR-VHD-MCQ-16.s: According to the WHO 2024 guideline, what is the preferred agent for secondary prophylaxis of rheumatic fever?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-16.p: Secondary prophylaxis: BPG IM ทุก 4 สัปดาห์

CAR-VHD-MCQ-17.s: A 42-year-old woman with known rheumatic mitral regurgitation has 4 weeks of fever, weight loss and new splenomegaly. What is the single most important first step before starting antibiotics?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-17.a: Obtain at least three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures
CAR-VHD-MCQ-17.p: สงสัย IE → blood culture ≥ 3 ชุดก่อนยา

C-OLD-86.s: A patient has a murmur, leg oedema, fever for 3 weeks and splenomegaly. Which diagnosis should be excluded first?

C-OLD-88.s: In infective endocarditis, what is a Roth spot?
C-OLD-88.a: A retinal haemorrhage with a pale centre

C-OLD-90.s: Which investigation is essential for diagnosing infective endocarditis?
C-OLD-90.a: At least three sets of blood cultures from different sites before antibiotics

CAR-VHD-MCQ-18.s: A patient with a mechanical mitral valve and a documented penicillin allergy (urticaria) is scheduled for a dental extraction. According to current AHA (2021) and ESC (2023) guidance, which prophylaxis is most appropriate?
CAR-VHD-MCQ-18.a: Azithromycin 500 mg orally 30–60 minutes before the procedure
CAR-VHD-MCQ-18.p: แพ้ penicillin → azithromycin/clarithromycin/doxycycline (ไม่ใช่ clindamycin แล้ว)

C-MCQ-27.s: A 54-year-old man is evaluated for 3 months of fever, fatigue and backache. He has no known cardiac disease and no drug allergy. Examination shows splinter haemorrhages under the fingernails, conjunctival haemorrhages and a decrescendo diastolic murmur of aortic insufficiency. Transthoracic echocardiography shows an oscillating mass on the aortic valve. Four sets of blood cultures grow viridans streptococci with a penicillin MIC of 0.06 mcg/mL (fully susceptible). There is no heart failure, abscess or conduction abnormality. Which of the following is the most appropriate antibiotic regimen?
C-MCQ-27.a: Penicillin G intravenously for 4 weeks, or penicillin G plus gentamicin for 2 weeks
C-MCQ-27.p: IE ที่มีข้อบ่งชี้ผ่าตัด: **HF จาก valve destruction, uncontrolled infection (abscess/fistula/เชื้อดื้อ), recurrent embolism หรือ vegetation >10 mm ที่ยังเคลื่อนที่**. Roth spot = **retinal hemorrhage ที่มีจุดขาวกลาง**; Osler node = **เจ็บ**; Janeway lesion = **ไม่เจ็บ**

C-OLD-87.s: A 54-year-old man has fever for 3 months, splinter haemorrhages, conjunctival haemorrhage, a diastolic murmur of aortic regurgitation, and an oscillating mass on the aortic valve. Four sets of blood cultures grow viridans streptococci. What is the appropriate treatment?
C-OLD-87.a: Intravenous penicillin G for 4 weeks, or penicillin G plus gentamicin for 2 weeks

C-OLD-89.s: A patient with a prosthetic heart valve and penicillin allergy is scheduled for a dental extraction involving gingival manipulation. What is the most appropriate prophylaxis?
C-OLD-89.a: A single dose of clindamycin or azithromycin before the procedure

CAR-ECG-MCQ-01.s: On a standard 12-lead ECG recorded at 25 mm/s, the PR interval measures 6 small squares and the QRS duration measures 2.5 small squares. Which interpretation is correct?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-01.a: PR 0.24 s (prolonged, consistent with first-degree AV block); QRS 0.10 s (normal)
CAR-ECG-MCQ-01.p: นับช่องเล็กแล้วคูณ 0.04 เสมอ · PR > 5 ช่องเล็ก = ยาว

CAR-ECG-MCQ-02.s: Which statement best explains why the ST segment is normally isoelectric?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-02.a: All ventricular myocytes are in the plateau phase of the action potential at nearly the same voltage, so no current flows between regions
CAR-ECG-MCQ-02.p: ST ยก/กด = กระแส injury จากเซลล์ที่ศักย์ต่างจากเพื่อน

CAR-ECG-MCQ-03.s: A 28-year-old man had an episode of syncope at rest. His standard 12-lead ECG shows a borderline incomplete right bundle branch pattern in V1–V2 with 1 mm ST elevation. Brugada syndrome is suspected. Which additional recording is most appropriate?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-03.a: Move leads V1 and V2 up to the 3rd and 2nd intercostal spaces (high right precordial leads)
CAR-ECG-MCQ-03.p: Brugada → ขยับ V1–V2 ขึ้น 1–2 ICS

CAR-ECG-MCQ-04.s: During a regular wide-complex tachycardia at 170/min, the team wants to look for independent atrial activity that would support ventricular tachycardia. Which lead arrangement taught in this lecture is designed for this purpose?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-04.a: Lewis lead: RA at the right 2nd intercostal space, LA at the right 4th intercostal space, LL at the right costal margin, then read lead I
CAR-ECG-MCQ-04.p: หา P ที่ซ่อน → Lewis lead (อ่าน lead I)

CAR-ECG-MCQ-05.s: A regular rhythm strip recorded at 25 mm/s shows the distance between consecutive R waves is exactly 4 large squares. What is the heart rate?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-05.p: R ตกเส้นใหญ่ที่ 4 = 75

CAR-ECG-MCQ-06.s: An ECG shows an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm without discernible P waves. A 10-second rhythm strip contains 22 QRS complexes. What is the ventricular rate and the best method to calculate it?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-06.a: 132/min — count QRS complexes on the strip and multiply (22 × 6)
CAR-ECG-MCQ-06.p: ไม่สม่ำเสมอ → นับ QRS ในแถบ (6 s × 10 · 10 s × 6)

CAR-ECG-MCQ-07.s: Which set of findings fulfils the criteria for normal sinus rhythm taught in this lecture?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-07.a: Rate 72/min, regular, upright uniform P waves in I, II and aVF, constant PR 0.16 s, QRS 0.09 s
CAR-ECG-MCQ-07.p: NSR ต้องครบ 5 ข้อ — rate ต่ำกว่า 60 เรียก sinus bradycardia

CAR-ECG-MCQ-08.s: A 70-year-old woman taking digoxin has a regular narrow-complex rhythm at 50/min. P waves are inverted in leads II, III and aVF and immediately follow each QRS complex. What is the origin of this rhythm and why are the P waves inverted?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-08.a: AV junction — the atria are depolarized retrogradely from below, so the impulse travels away from the inferior leads
CAR-ECG-MCQ-08.p: P คว่ำใน II/III/aVF + QRS แคบ + 40–60 = junctional

CAR-ECG-MCQ-09.s: An ECG shows sinus rhythm at 75/min. After every sinus beat there is an early, wide (0.16 s), bizarre QRS complex not preceded by a P wave, with a T wave opposite in direction to the QRS. What is the diagnosis?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-09.p: มาก่อน + กว้าง + ไม่มี P = PVC · ทุกตัวสลับ = bigeminy

CAR-ECG-MCQ-10.s: Thirty minutes after successful primary PCI of the LAD, a patient's monitor shows a regular wide-complex rhythm at 75/min without P waves, alternating with sinus rhythm at 70/min. Blood pressure is 124/76 mmHg and he is asymptomatic. What is the most appropriate management?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-10.a: Observation — this is accelerated idioventricular rhythm, a benign reperfusion arrhythmia
CAR-ECG-MCQ-10.p: AIVR หลัง reperfusion = สัญญาณเปิดหลอดเลือดสำเร็จ · สังเกต

CAR-ECG-MCQ-11.s: A 64-year-old man has palpitations. ECG shows a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at exactly 150/min. In leads II, III and aVF there is a continuous saw-tooth baseline at about 300/min. What is the diagnosis and mechanism?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-11.a: Atrial flutter with 2:1 AV conduction — macro re-entry around the tricuspid annulus
CAR-ECG-MCQ-11.p: HR 150 พอดี + QRS แคบ → หาฟันเลื่อย (flutter 2:1)

CAR-ECG-MCQ-12.s: Which combination is required for a re-entrant tachycardia such as AVNRT to start?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-12.a: Two pathways with different conduction and refractory properties, unidirectional block in one pathway, and slow enough conduction for the blocked pathway to recover
CAR-ECG-MCQ-12.p: ตัดวง re-entry = ทำให้จุดใดจุดหนึ่งของวงดื้อ (vagal, adenosine, shock)

CAR-ECG-MCQ-13.s: A 35-year-old woman has sudden palpitations for 30 minutes. BP 118/74 mmHg, alert, no chest pain. ECG: regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 186/min without visible P waves. A modified Valsalva manoeuvre fails. What is the next step and why must it be given rapidly?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-13.a: Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push followed by a saline flush — it is metabolised within seconds and transiently blocks the AV node, breaking the re-entry circuit
CAR-ECG-MCQ-13.p: AVNRT เสถียร: vagal → adenosine 6 → 12 mg push เร็ว

CAR-ECG-MCQ-14.s: A 70-year-old man with a previous anterior MI has a regular wide-complex tachycardia at 190/min. BP 76/40 mmHg, he is drowsy but has a palpable carotid pulse. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-14.p: มีชีพจร + ไม่เสถียร = synchronized cardioversion

C-MCQ-32.s: A 26-year-old woman presents with sudden-onset palpitations that began abruptly 30 minutes ago while she was sitting. Vital signs: PR 186/min, BP 112/72 mmHg, RR 18/min, fully alert with warm extremities. ECG shows a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 186/min with no visible P waves and no pre-excitation in previous tracings. Valsalva manoeuvre and carotid sinus massage fail to terminate the rhythm. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
C-MCQ-32.a: Intravenous adenosine 6 mg by rapid push, followed by 12 mg if needed
C-MCQ-32.p: ลำดับจัดการ stable SVT: **vagal manoeuvre (modified Valsalva ท่ายกขานอนราบได้ผลดีกว่าเดิม) → adenosine → IV diltiazem/verapamil หรือ beta-blocker → synchronised cardioversion**. ถ้ามี **WPW ร่วมกับ AF (pre-excited)** ห้าม adenosine/CCB/BB/digoxin

C-MCQ-33.s: A 63-year-old man in the coronary care unit suddenly becomes unresponsive. The cardiac monitor shows a wide-complex tachycardia at 210/min. No carotid or femoral pulse is palpable and he is not breathing normally. A defibrillator is at the bedside. Which of the following is the best first therapy?
C-MCQ-33.a: Immediate unsynchronised defibrillation at maximal recommended energy
C-MCQ-33.p: แยกให้ชัด 3 สถานการณ์: **pulseless VT/VF → unsynchronised defibrillation + CPR**; **VT มี pulse แต่ unstable → synchronised cardioversion**; **VT มี pulse และ stable → antiarrhythmic (amiodarone/procainamide) หรือ elective cardioversion**. Polymorphic VT/torsades ให้ **unsynchronised shock + MgSO4**

C-OLD-100.s: A stable patient has a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 180/min with no visible P waves. Vagal manoeuvres fail. What is the next step?

C-OLD-101.s: A patient with monomorphic ventricular tachycardia at 180/min has BP 78/40 mmHg, chest pain and is drowsy but has a pulse. What is the immediate treatment?

C-OLD-102.s: A monitored patient in the ICU suddenly becomes pulseless with ventricular tachycardia on the monitor. What is the best first therapy?

CAR-ECG-MCQ-15.s: An ECG shows a predominantly positive QRS in lead I, a predominantly negative QRS in aVF and a predominantly negative QRS in lead II. What is the QRS axis?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-15.p: I บวก aVF ลบ → ตัดสินด้วย lead II

CAR-ECG-MCQ-16.s: A 45-year-old woman with sudden dyspnoea and tachycardia has a new right axis deviation on her ECG compared with one year ago. Which mechanism best explains the new right axis?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-16.a: Acute right ventricular pressure overload increases the electrical forces generated by the right ventricle
CAR-ECG-MCQ-16.p: RAD ใหม่ + หอบ + tachy → คิด PE/RV strain

CAR-ECG-MCQ-17.s: A 45-year-old man (no prior ECG) has 1 hour of chest pain. His ECG shows 1.5 mm ST elevation in V2 and V3, 0.5 mm in V4, and no ST changes elsewhere. According to the criteria taught, how should this be interpreted?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-17.a: Does not meet STEMI criteria — men aged 40 or older need at least 2 mm in V2–V3; repeat the ECG every 15–30 minutes while symptomatic

CAR-ECG-MCQ-18.s: An ECG shows ST elevation in V2–V6, I and aVL with ST depression in II, III and aVF. What is the diagnosis and the most likely culprit artery?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-18.a: Acute anterolateral STEMI with inferior reciprocal changes — proximal left anterior descending artery
CAR-ECG-MCQ-18.p: ST ยกผนังหนึ่ง + กดฝั่งตรงข้าม = STEMI จริง

C-OLD-104.s: An ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL in a patient with 2 hours of chest pain. What is the diagnosis?

C-OLD-105.s: Which feature identifies a high-risk non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome requiring early invasive strategy within 24 hours?
C-OLD-105.a: Rising troponin with dynamic ST-T changes or a GRACE score above 140

CAR-ECG-MCQ-19.s: A 58-year-old man with long-standing poorly controlled hypertension has an ECG with an S wave of 18 mm in V1 and an R wave of 24 mm in V5, with down-sloping ST depression and T-wave inversion in V5–V6. What is the best interpretation?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-19.a: Left ventricular hypertrophy with strain pattern
CAR-ECG-MCQ-19.p: บวก S V1 + R V5 แล้วเทียบ 35

CAR-ECG-MCQ-20.s: A 32-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis has a P wave in lead II that is 0.14 s wide with two distinct humps, but only 1.5 mm tall. What does this indicate and why?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-20.a: Left atrial enlargement — the enlarged left atrium depolarizes later and longer, prolonging and notching the terminal part of the P wave
CAR-ECG-MCQ-20.p: P mitrale = กว้าง + หยัก (LA) · P pulmonale = สูง (RA)

CAR-ECG-MCQ-21.s: A 74-year-old woman has recurrent sudden syncope without warning. ECG shows sinus rhythm at 80/min, constant PR interval of 0.18 s in conducted beats, QRS 0.14 s with RBBB morphology, and intermittent non-conducted P waves without preceding PR prolongation. Where is the block and what is the definitive treatment?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-21.p: P หลุด + PR คงที่ (+ QRS กว้าง) = ใต้ AV node → pacemaker

CAR-ECG-MCQ-22.s: Six hours after inferior STEMI from RCA occlusion, a patient develops complete heart block with a narrow-QRS escape rhythm at 48/min. BP 104/66 mmHg, alert. Which statement is correct?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-22.a: The block is most likely at the AV node due to ischaemia and high vagal tone; it often responds to atropine and usually resolves
CAR-ECG-MCQ-22.p: CHB + inferior MI = AV node · QRS แคบ · ตอบ atropine · มักหาย

CAR-ECG-MCQ-23.s: Which ECG description is diagnostic of second-degree AV block Mobitz type I?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-23.a: PR interval lengthens progressively until a P wave is not conducted; the PR after the dropped beat is the shortest
CAR-ECG-MCQ-23.p: Wenckebach = PR ยาวขึ้น → หลุด → รีเซ็ต

C-MCQ-29.s: A 68-year-old asymptomatic man has an ECG performed before elective hernia repair. The rhythm strip shows progressive lengthening of the PR interval over three consecutive beats (200, 260, 320 ms) followed by a non-conducted P wave, after which the cycle repeats. The QRS duration is 84 ms. Which of the following is the correct diagnosis and the expected site of block?
C-MCQ-29.a: Second-degree AV block Mobitz type I; block within the AV node
C-MCQ-29.p: เคล็ดจำ: **"Longer, longer, longer, drop → then you have a Wenckebach"** และ **"If some Ps just don't get through, then you have a Mobitz II"**. จุดหลอก: Mobitz I 2:1 conduction อาจแยกจาก Mobitz II ยาก — ใช้ QRS width, การตอบสนองต่อ atropine/exercise (Mobitz I ดีขึ้น, Mobitz II แย่ลง) ช่วยแยก

C-MCQ-30.s: A 76-year-old woman presents with three episodes of syncope in the past month. Her ECG shows sinus rhythm at 78/min with a constant PR interval of 180 ms, intermittent sudden non-conducted P waves without preceding PR prolongation, and a QRS duration of 140 ms with a left bundle branch block pattern. She takes no rate-limiting drugs, and her electrolytes and thyroid function are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate definitive management?
C-MCQ-30.p: ข้อบ่งชี้ pacemaker ที่ต้องจำ: **Mobitz II, complete AV block, high-grade AV block, symptomatic sinus node dysfunction, alternating bundle branch block** — และ **Mobitz I ที่มีอาการหรือบล็อกระดับ infranodal**. ชั่วคราวระหว่างรอ: **transcutaneous/transvenous pacing**

C-MCQ-31.s: A 24-year-old competitive long-distance runner has a pre-participation ECG showing sinus bradycardia at 50/min with a PR interval of 230 ms, narrow QRS and normal repolarisation. He is completely asymptomatic, has no family history of sudden death, and his echocardiogram and electrolytes are normal. The PR interval shortens to 170 ms during exercise. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
C-MCQ-31.a: No specific treatment; reassurance and routine follow-up
C-MCQ-31.p: ตรวจ ECG นักกีฬา: **normal adaptation** = sinus bradycardia, 1st degree AVB, incomplete RBBB, early repolarization, isolated LVH by voltage. **ต้องสืบค้นเพิ่ม** = T wave inversion (นอกเหนือ V1-V3), pathological Q, LBBB, QRS >140 ms, long/short QT, Brugada pattern, ventricular arrhythmia

C-MCQ-34.s: An 80-year-old woman is brought in after collapsing at home. Vital signs: PR 34/min, BP 72/44 mmHg, RR 20/min, and she is drowsy with cool extremities. ECG shows P waves at 84/min and QRS complexes at 34/min with no relationship between them; the QRS is wide. Serum potassium is 4.2 mEq/L, she takes no rate-limiting drugs and troponin is normal. Intravenous atropine 1 mg produces no change. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate next step?
C-MCQ-34.a: Transcutaneous pacing, with preparation for temporary transvenous pacing and subsequent permanent pacemaker
C-MCQ-34.p: สาเหตุ **reversible** ของ bradyarrhythmia ที่ต้องคัดก่อนฝัง pacemaker (จำ): **ยา (BB, CCB, digoxin, amiodarone), hyperkalemia, hypothyroidism, hypothermia, inferior MI, increased ICP, Lyme/infiltrative disease, OSA**

C-OLD-95.s: An ECG shows a constant PR interval of 0.26 seconds with every P wave followed by a QRS complex. What is the diagnosis?

C-OLD-96.s: An asymptomatic 45-year-old man has first-degree AV block on a routine ECG with normal examination. What is the appropriate management?
C-OLD-96.a: Observation with review of AV-nodal blocking drugs

C-OLD-97.s: An ECG shows progressive PR prolongation until a P wave is not conducted, then the cycle repeats. What is the diagnosis?
C-OLD-97.a: Second-degree AV block Mobitz type I (Wenckebach)

C-OLD-98.s: An ECG shows intermittently dropped QRS complexes with a constant PR interval in the conducted beats and a wide QRS. What is the diagnosis and management?
C-OLD-98.a: Mobitz type II block — permanent pacemaker

C-OLD-99.s: An ECG shows P waves and QRS complexes that are completely dissociated, with a ventricular rate of 35/min and a wide QRS. The patient is dizzy with BP 85/50 mmHg. What is the definitive treatment?
C-OLD-99.a: Temporary pacing followed by a permanent pacemaker

CAR-ECG-MCQ-24.s: An ECG shows QRS duration 0.14 s, an rsR' pattern in V1 and a broad slurred S wave in V6. What is the diagnosis and the order of ventricular activation?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-24.a: Right bundle branch block — the left ventricle is activated normally and the right ventricle is activated late through myocardium
CAR-ECG-MCQ-24.p: M ใน V1 = RBBB · W ใน V1 = LBBB

CAR-ECG-MCQ-25.s: A 66-year-old man has 40 minutes of typical crushing chest pain with diaphoresis. ECG shows left bundle branch block; no previous ECG is available. What is the most appropriate approach?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-25.a: Manage as a STEMI equivalent and activate urgent reperfusion while applying Sgarbossa criteria
CAR-ECG-MCQ-25.p: LBBB + เจ็บหน้าอกแบบ ischemia = STEMI equivalent

CAR-ECG-MCQ-26.s: A 61-year-old man on haemodialysis missed two sessions. K⁺ 7.4 mmol/L. ECG: tall peaked T waves, flattened P waves and QRS 0.14 s. What is the first drug to give and how does it act?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-26.a: Intravenous calcium gluconate — it raises the threshold potential and stabilizes the myocardial membrane within minutes without lowering K⁺
CAR-ECG-MCQ-26.p: hyperK + ECG เปลี่ยน → Ca gluconate ก่อนเสมอ

CAR-ECG-MCQ-27.s: A 26-year-old man has sharp chest pain worse on lying flat and relieved by leaning forward, 1 week after a viral illness. Which ECG finding best supports acute pericarditis rather than STEMI?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-27.a: Widespread concave ST elevation with PR-segment depression and no reciprocal ST depression except in aVR
CAR-ECG-MCQ-27.p: ST ยกทั่ว + PR กด = pericarditis

C-OLD-103.s: An ECG shows tall peaked T waves with a widened QRS in a patient with chronic kidney disease. What is the first drug to give?

C-OLD-107.s: A patient with CKD on two nephrotoxic drugs has an ECG showing tall peaked T waves, rate 120/min, sinus rhythm, P waves present and a narrow QRS. What is the interpretation?
C-OLD-107.a: Sinus tachycardia with ECG changes of hyperkalaemia

C-OLD-108.s: Which ECG pattern is most characteristic of acute pericarditis rather than myocardial infarction?
C-OLD-108.a: Widespread concave ST elevation with PR depression and no reciprocal change

C-OLD-109.s: An ECG shows tall peaked T waves in a patient who is drowsy with muscle weakness. What is the diagnosis?

CAR-ECG-MCQ-28.s: In an ECG interpretation station, which written report is the most complete according to the 5-step approach taught?
CAR-ECG-MCQ-28.a: Rate 78/min, sinus rhythm with ventricular bigeminy, normal axis, PR 0.16 s and QRS 0.09 s in sinus beats, no ST–T changes of infarction, no chamber enlargement — NSR with ventricular bigeminy
CAR-ECG-MCQ-28.p: SAQ ECG: เขียนครบทุกขั้นแล้วสรุปเป็นประโยคเดียว

C-OLD-106.s: When describing an ECG in a SAQ station, which set of elements must be reported?
C-OLD-106.a: Rate, rhythm, axis, intervals, chamber enlargement, ST-T changes and Q waves

CH-MCQ-08.s: Which statement best describes how Mycobacterium tuberculosis is transmitted, and what is the most effective single measure to interrupt transmission in a hospital?
CH-MCQ-08.a: Airborne droplet nuclei 1-5 micrometres that remain suspended in air; prompt identification and effective treatment of infectious cases
CH-MCQ-08.p: เกณฑ์ยุติการแยกผู้ป่วยวัณโรคปอดในโรงพยาบาล: **ได้ยาที่เหมาะสมอย่างน้อย 2 สัปดาห์ + อาการทางคลินิกดีขึ้น + AFB smear ลบ 3 ครั้งจากคนละวัน** (และต้องไม่สงสัย MDR-TB ซึ่งต้องรอ culture conversion)

CH-OLD-08.s: A patient with newly diagnosed smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted. Which admission arrangement is most appropriate?
CH-OLD-08.a: Admit to a negative-pressure isolation room and have all staff wear an N95 respirator

CH-OLD-10.s: Reactivation pulmonary tuberculosis in an immunocompetent adult most characteristically involves which part of the lung, and why?
CH-OLD-10.a: Apical and posterior segments of the upper lobes, because of the higher oxygen tension there

CH-MCQ-05.s: A 45-year-old man with diabetes presents with 6 weeks of fever, weight loss and progressive dyspnoea. Chest radiograph shows innumerable uniform 2 mm nodules evenly distributed throughout both lungs. He is confused on examination. Which of the following is the most appropriate combination of investigations?
CH-MCQ-05.a: Sputum and blood for mycobacterial culture, fundoscopy for choroidal tubercles and lumbar puncture
CH-MCQ-05.p: DDx ของ **miliary pattern** บน CXR: **TB, เชื้อรากระจาย (histoplasmosis, cryptococcosis), มะเร็งแพร่กระจาย (thyroid, renal cell, melanoma), silicosis, sarcoidosis และ hypersensitivity pneumonitis**

CH-MCQ-01.s: A 28-year-old healthy woman is the household contact of her father, who has just been diagnosed with smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. She is asymptomatic with a normal chest radiograph. An interferon-gamma release assay is positive. She is not pregnant, has normal liver function and takes no medication. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
CH-MCQ-01.a: Treat for latent tuberculosis infection after active disease has been excluded
CH-MCQ-01.p: **IGRA เหนือกว่า TST ในผู้ที่เคยฉีด BCG** เพราะไม่ข้ามปฏิกิริยากับ BCG และ NTM ส่วนใหญ่; ทั้งสองวิธี **แยก latent จาก active ไม่ได้** และ **ผลลบไม่ตัดโรค** โดยเฉพาะในผู้ที่ภูมิคุ้มกันต่ำ

CH-OLD-11.s: A 34-year-old man with HIV infection who has never received antiretroviral therapy presents with 3 weeks of dry cough and progressive exertional dyspnoea. CD4 count is 125 cells/microlitre. Chest radiograph shows bilateral perihilar ground-glass opacities. Which organism is most likely responsible?

CH-OLD-09.s: Which investigation is the gold standard for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis?

CH-MCQ-03.s: A 32-year-old man presents with 3 weeks of headache, low-grade fever and progressive drowsiness, followed by a left sixth cranial nerve palsy. Lumbar puncture shows opening pressure 28 cmH2O, clear but slightly xanthochromic fluid, WBC 220 cells/microlitre with 85 percent lymphocytes, protein 180 mg/dL and CSF glucose 28 mg/dL with simultaneous blood glucose 100 mg/dL. Which diagnosis is most likely, and which adjunctive treatment improves survival?
CH-MCQ-03.p: **การเริ่ม ART ในผู้ป่วย HIV ที่มี TB meningitis ควรเลื่อนไปประมาณ 4-8 สัปดาห์** (ต่างจาก TB ที่อื่นซึ่งเริ่มใน 2 สัปดาห์เมื่อ CD4 ต่ำ) เพราะ **paradoxical IRIS ในสมองอันตรายถึงชีวิต**

CH-OLD-02.s: A patient receiving the 2HRZE/4HR anti-tuberculous regimen develops painless blurring of vision in both eyes with impaired colour discrimination after several weeks of treatment. There is no eye redness or pain. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?
CH-OLD-02.a: Stop ethambutol and refer to an ophthalmologist

CH-OLD-05.s: Which anti-tuberculous drug causes peripheral neuropathy, and what is given to prevent it?

CH-OLD-03.s: Which anti-tuberculous drug most characteristically causes hyperuricaemia and may precipitate an acute gouty attack?

CH-OLD-04.s: A patient completing anti-tuberculous therapy notices that his urine, tears and sweat have turned orange-red. He feels well and liver function tests are normal. Which drug is responsible?

CH-OLD-01.s: A 30-year-old previously healthy woman with smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis was started on isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol once daily. After 1 week she develops progressive nausea, vomiting and malaise. Physical findings are unremarkable. Liver function tests: total bilirubin / direct bilirubin 2.8 / 1.6 mg/dL, AST/ALT 180/170 U/L, ALP 150 U/L (normal <115). What is the most appropriate immediate management?
CH-OLD-01.a: Stop all hepatotoxic drugs, switch to ethambutol plus a fluoroquinolone, then perform a drug challenge test when liver function recovers

CH-MCQ-06.s: A patient with drug-susceptible smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis has completed 2 months of isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol under directly observed therapy. He feels much better and has gained weight, but the sputum smear at the end of the second month is still positive. What is the most appropriate next step?
CH-MCQ-06.a: Send sputum for culture and drug susceptibility testing, and continue treatment while awaiting results
CH-MCQ-06.p: **กฎทองของวัณโรค: ห้ามเติมยาเพียงตัวเดียวเข้าไปในสูตรที่ไม่ได้ผล** — ถ้าจะเปลี่ยนต้องเปลี่ยนเป็นสูตรใหม่ที่มียาที่เชื้อยังไวอย่างน้อย 3-4 ตัว

CH-OLD-07.s: A patient with smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis has been on the standard regimen for 8 weeks but his sputum smear remains AFB positive and his symptoms have not improved. He obtains his medication from the local health centre and admits missing doses frequently. Which is the most likely explanation and the best next step?
CH-OLD-07.a: Poor adherence; assess and reinforce adherence with directly observed therapy while sending sputum for culture and drug susceptibility testing

CH-MCQ-07.s: A patient with end-stage renal disease on haemodialysis is diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis. Which pair of first-line drugs requires dose or interval adjustment in this setting?
CH-MCQ-07.p: ในผู้ป่วยโรคตับ: **pyrazinamide เป็นพิษต่อตับมากที่สุด** → ในตับแข็งรุนแรงอาจต้องใช้สูตรที่ไม่มี PZA (2HRE/7HR) หรือสูตรที่มียาตับ ≤1 ตัวในรายที่รุนแรงมาก

CH-MCQ-02.s: A 26-year-old woman at 12 weeks of gestation is diagnosed with smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. Which anti-tuberculous drug must be avoided during her pregnancy?
CH-MCQ-02.p: ยาวัณโรคแนวที่สองที่ **ห้ามในครรภ์** เพิ่มเติม: **fluoroquinolone, ethionamide (teratogenic ชัด), aminoglycoside ทุกตัว**

CH-MCQ-04.s: A 29-year-old man is newly diagnosed with HIV infection and smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. His CD4 count is 30 cells/microlitre. Anti-tuberculous therapy is started. Which statement about starting antiretroviral therapy is correct?
CH-MCQ-04.a: Start antiretroviral therapy within the first 2 weeks of anti-tuberculous treatment because the CD4 count is below 50
CH-MCQ-04.p: ผู้ป่วย HIV ที่เป็น TB มักมีภาพ **ไม่คลาสสิก**: CXR อาจเป็น **lower zone infiltrate, lymphadenopathy, miliary หรือแม้แต่ปกติ** และ **smear มักลบ** เมื่อ CD4 ต่ำ → ใช้ **molecular test และ urine LF-LAM** ช่วย

CH-OLD-12.s: A patient with pulmonary tuberculosis develops acute kidney injury 10 days after starting the standard four-drug regimen. Which urinary finding would best support drug-induced acute interstitial nephritis as the cause?
CH-OLD-12.a: Sterile pyuria with white blood cell casts

CH-OLD-06.s: What is the definition of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB)?
CH-OLD-06.a: Resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin

CHEST-26-01-Q1.s: An arterial blood gas is drawn from a patient breathing room air. The sample sits at room temperature for 45 minutes before analysis and a visible air bubble was not expelled from the syringe. Compared with the patient's true values, which of the following patterns is most likely to be reported?
CHEST-26-01-Q1.a: PaO2 that may be falsely high from the air bubble and falsely low from delayed analysis, with a falsely low PaCO2
CHEST-26-01-Q1.p: ตัวอย่าง ABG ที่มีฟองอากาศและตั้งทิ้งไว้นาน = แปลผลไม่ได้ ต้องเจาะใหม่ อย่าฝืนอธิบายค่าที่ได้

CH-MCQ-13.s: Which set of conditions shifts the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve to the RIGHT, favouring oxygen release to the tissues?
CH-MCQ-13.a: Increased temperature, increased PaCO2, acidosis and increased 2,3-diphosphoglycerate
CH-MCQ-13.p: **Methaemoglobinaemia** (จาก dapsone, ยาชาเฉพาะที่, nitrate): ผู้ป่วยเขียวคล้ำแต่ **PaO2 ปกติ** และ **pulse oximeter ค้างอยู่ราว 85% ไม่ว่าจะให้ออกซิเจนเท่าไร**; เลือดสีน้ำตาลช็อกโกแลต รักษาด้วย **methylene blue**

CH-MCQ-16.s: A 45-year-old man is rescued from a house fire. He is confused with a headache and nausea. SpO2 by pulse oximetry reads 99 percent on room air and arterial PaO2 is 96 mmHg. Which statement best explains the discrepancy between his clinical state and the oxygen readings?
CH-MCQ-16.a: Pulse oximetry cannot distinguish carboxyhaemoglobin from oxyhaemoglobin, so co-oximetry is needed
CH-MCQ-16.p: สถานการณ์อื่นที่ **pulse oximetry เชื่อไม่ได้**: **methaemoglobinaemia (ค้างราว 85%)**, ภาวะซีดรุนแรง, ปลายมือเย็น/perfusion ต่ำ, ยาสีเล็บเข้ม, การเคลื่อนไหวมาก, บิลิรูบินสูงมาก และสีย้อมทางหลอดเลือดดำ

CH-MCQ-09.s: A 70-year-old man breathing room air has an arterial blood gas showing pH 7.36, PaCO2 40 mmHg and PaO2 60 mmHg. Assume the respiratory quotient is 0.8. What is his alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient, and what does it indicate?
CH-MCQ-09.a: Approximately 40 mmHg; widened, indicating intrinsic lung disease
CH-MCQ-09.p: **ถ้า PaCO2 สูงและ A-a gradient ปกติ → ปัญหาอยู่นอกปอด (การหายใจ)** ให้มองหา CNS depression, ยา, กล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรง, ผนังทรวงอกผิดรูป; **ถ้า PaCO2 สูงแต่ A-a gradient กว้างด้วย → โรคปอดเอง** เช่น COPD ที่รุนแรง

CH-OLD-17.s: Which statement correctly describes a physiological shunt?
CH-OLD-17.a: Alveolar units that are perfused but not ventilated, causing hypoxaemia that does not correct with supplemental oxygen

CH-OLD-20.s: Which of the following causes hypoxaemia with a NORMAL alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient?

CH-OLD-18.s: A patient has severe hypoxaemia with a markedly increased alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient that does not improve despite a high fraction of inspired oxygen. Bilateral infiltrates are present on chest radiograph and there is no evidence of cardiac failure. Which condition best explains this?

CH-OLD-22.s: A 36-year-old woman with HIV infection presents with 2 weeks of progressive exertional dyspnoea, low-grade fever and dry cough. Examination: BT 38 C, PR 130/min, RR 30/min, mild pallor, oral hairy leukoplakia, normal breath sounds with no adventitious sounds. ABG on room air: pH 7.45, PaO2 55 mmHg, PaCO2 30 mmHg, O2 saturation 80 percent. Apart from oxygen therapy, which treatment is most appropriate?

CH-MCQ-10.s: Which arterial blood gas result on room air defines type 2 (hypercapnic) respiratory failure?
CH-MCQ-10.p: **Acute-on-chronic**: ผู้ป่วย COPD ที่มี CO2 คั่งเรื้อรังจะมี **HCO3 สูงชดเชยและ pH เกือบปกติ** — สิ่งที่บอกว่า "เฉียบพลัน" คือ **pH ที่ตก** ไม่ใช่ระดับ PaCO2

CH-OLD-19.s: A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department confused and drowsy. Arterial blood gas: PaO2 170 mmHg (on supplemental oxygen), PaCO2 56 mmHg, pH 7.28. He has a 15 pack-year smoking history and pulmonary function testing 3 months ago showed severe airway obstruction. What is the most likely cause of his hypercapnic respiratory failure?
CH-OLD-19.a: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with excessive oxygen administration

CH-OLD-14.s: A patient becomes dyspnoeic 6 hours ago. Arterial blood gas on room air: pH 7.26, PaCO2 60 mmHg, HCO3 26 mEq/L, O2 saturation 80 percent. Which interpretation is correct?
CH-OLD-14.a: Acute respiratory acidosis with minimal metabolic compensation

CH-MCQ-14.s: A 72-year-old man with severe COPD is brought to the emergency department with an exacerbation. SpO2 is 84 percent on room air. Which oxygen strategy is most appropriate while awaiting arterial blood gas results?
CH-MCQ-14.a: Controlled oxygen by nasal cannula or Venturi mask targeting SpO2 88 to 92 percent
CH-MCQ-14.p: ผู้ป่วยกลุ่มอื่นที่ใช้เป้า **88-92%** เช่นกัน: **obesity hypoventilation, ผนังทรวงอกผิดรูป (kyphoscoliosis), โรคกล้ามเนื้ออ่อนแรงเรื้อรัง, bronchiectasis รุนแรง และ cystic fibrosis** — ส่วนผู้ป่วยทั่วไปที่ไม่เสี่ยงคั่ง CO2 ใช้เป้า **94-98%**

CH-OLD-13.s: An arterial blood gas shows pH 7.15, PaCO2 30 mmHg and HCO3 10 mEq/L. Which acid-base disorder is present?
CH-OLD-13.a: Mixed metabolic acidosis and respiratory acidosis

CH-OLD-15.s: A 60-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents with worsening dyspnoea. Arterial blood gas: pH 7.30, PaCO2 80 mmHg, HCO3 38 mEq/L. Which interpretation is correct?
CH-OLD-15.a: Acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis with partial metabolic compensation

CH-MCQ-11.s: A 24-year-old woman presents with breathlessness and tingling around the mouth and fingers. Arterial blood gas on room air: pH 7.52, PaCO2 26 mmHg, PaO2 105 mmHg, HCO3 21 mEq/L. Which finding in the history would most strongly argue AGAINST a benign hyperventilation syndrome and require urgent further investigation?
CH-MCQ-11.a: Pleuritic chest pain with unilateral calf swelling
CH-MCQ-11.p: ใน **salicylate poisoning** จะพบ **respiratory alkalosis ร่วมกับ high anion gap metabolic acidosis พร้อมกัน** ทำให้ pH อาจดูเกือบปกติ — เป็นกับดักที่ออกสอบ (โจทย์ LMS ของ MED35 ก็ใช้รูปแบบนี้)

CH-MCQ-12.s: A 48-year-old man with gastric outlet obstruction has vomited repeatedly for 5 days. Arterial blood gas: pH 7.52, PaCO2 48 mmHg, HCO3 38 mEq/L. Electrolytes: Na 138, K 2.8, Cl 88 mEq/L. Urine chloride is 8 mEq/L. What is the most appropriate treatment?
CH-MCQ-12.a: Intravenous 0.9 percent sodium chloride with potassium chloride replacement
CH-MCQ-12.p: การชดเชยของ **metabolic alkalosis**: PaCO2 ขึ้นประมาณ **0.7 mmHg ต่อ HCO3 ที่ขึ้น 1 mEq/L** — เคสนี้ HCO3 ขึ้น 14 → คาด PaCO2 ≈ 40 + 10 = **50** ซึ่งใกล้เคียงค่าที่วัดได้ (48) = ชดเชยเหมาะสม; และการชดเชยมี **เพดานราว PaCO2 55 mmHg** เพราะร่างกายจะไม่ยอม hypoventilate จนขาดออกซิเจน

CH-OLD-16.s: A 56-year-old diabetic man presents with fever, productive cough and vomiting for 3 days. Vital signs: BT 38.5 C, PR 110/min, RR 28/min, BP 95/55 mmHg, moderate dehydration, crepitations at the lower lung. Laboratory results: blood sugar 128 mg/dL, BUN 14, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, Na 140, K 4.1, Cl 78, HCO3 15 mEq/L, albumin 4.0 g/dL. ABG: pH 7.50, PaO2 70 mmHg, PaCO2 20 mmHg. What best describes the acid-base abnormality?
CH-OLD-16.a: Respiratory alkalosis from pneumonia, metabolic alkalosis from vomiting and high anion gap metabolic acidosis from lactic acidosis

CH-MCQ-15.s: A patient has Na 140, Cl 107, HCO3 12 mEq/L and albumin 4.0 g/dL. The arterial pH is 7.30 with PaCO2 26 mmHg. What does the delta ratio indicate?
CH-MCQ-15.a: The delta ratio is approximately 0.8, indicating a coexisting normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
CH-MCQ-15.p: ลำดับการอ่าน ABG ที่ไม่ควรข้าม: **(1) pH (2) ความผิดปกติปฐมภูมิ (3) การชดเชยด้วยสูตร (4) anion gap ที่ปรับ albumin แล้ว (5) delta ratio** — ทำครบ 5 ขั้นจะไม่พลาด mixed disorder

CH-OLD-21.s: A patient with diabetic ketoacidosis has an arterial blood gas showing pH 7.26, PaCO2 23 mmHg and HCO3 10 mEq/L, with Na 140, Cl 100 mEq/L. Which interpretation is correct?
CH-OLD-21.a: High anion gap metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation

CH-EP-MCQ-01.s: A 38-year-old man on maintenance haemodialysis for end-stage renal disease is diagnosed with tuberculous cervical lymphadenitis. He has no cough. Which additional step is essential before deciding on infection-control measures?
CH-EP-MCQ-01.a: Chest radiograph and sputum examination to look for concurrent pulmonary TB
CH-EP-MCQ-01.p: EPTB ทุกราย → CXR + เสมหะ เพื่อหาวัณโรคปอดที่ซ่อนอยู่

CH-EP-MCQ-02.s: According to Thai surveillance data presented in the lecture, approximately what proportion of all notified TB cases are extrapulmonary?
CH-EP-MCQ-02.p: EPTB ≈ 12–13% · วัณโรคปอด ≈ 80%

CH-EP-MCQ-03.s: A 31-year-old man with newly diagnosed HIV infection (CD4 count 42 cells/µL) has 6 weeks of fever and weight loss. Chest radiograph shows innumerable 2-mm nodules throughout both lungs. Based on the pattern of EPTB by HIV status, which form of tuberculosis is he most likely to have?
CH-EP-MCQ-03.p: HIV + CD4 ต่ำ + miliary → disseminated TB · อย่าลืมหา TB meningitis

CH-EP-MCQ-04.s: Which EPTB site was most characteristic of HIV-negative rather than HIV-positive patients in the Thai series presented?
CH-EP-MCQ-04.p: HIV ลบ → pleura และ bone/spine · HIV บวก → disseminated

CH-EP-MCQ-05.s: A 27-year-old woman is newly diagnosed with tuberculous lymphadenitis. Which test must be offered to every patient with tuberculosis because its result changes management?
CH-EP-MCQ-05.p: ผู้ป่วยวัณโรคทุกราย → ตรวจ HIV

CH-EP-MCQ-06.s: A 45-year-old man has a lymphocytic exudative pleural effusion. Pleural fluid AFB smear is negative. Which statement about this result is most accurate?
CH-EP-MCQ-06.a: It is expected, because AFB smear of pleural fluid is positive in fewer than 10% of tuberculous pleuritis cases
CH-EP-MCQ-06.p: Pleural fluid AFB smear บวก < 10% → ลบไม่ได้ตัดโรค

CH-EP-MCQ-07.s: Which advantage belongs to mycobacterial culture rather than to a nucleic acid amplification test such as GeneXpert?
CH-EP-MCQ-07.a: Distinguishing live from dead bacilli and allowing full drug-susceptibility testing
CH-EP-MCQ-07.p: Culture = เชื้อเป็น/ตาย + NTM + DST ครบ · NAAT = เร็ว + RIF resistance

CH-EP-MCQ-08.s: In which specimen does GeneXpert (NAAT) have the highest pooled sensitivity for EPTB according to the lecture?
CH-EP-MCQ-08.p: Xpert ไว: LN 0.96 >> pleural fluid 0.34

CH-EP-MCQ-09.s: A 40-year-old woman with suspected tuberculous meningitis has a tuberculin skin test of 0 mm. What is the correct interpretation?
CH-EP-MCQ-09.a: A negative TST does not exclude active TB; TST is not a diagnostic test for active disease
CH-EP-MCQ-09.p: TST ไม่ใช้วินิจฉัย active TB — ลบก็ตัดโรคไม่ได้

CH-EP-MCQ-10.s: Pleural fluid from a 30-year-old man shows: straw-coloured exudate, WBC 2,400/µL with 85% lymphocytes, 2% eosinophils, rare mesothelial cells, protein 5.1 g/dL, glucose lower than serum, ADA 68 U/L, cytology negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CH-EP-MCQ-10.p: Lymphocytic exudate + ADA > 40 + mesothelial น้อย = TB pleuritis

CH-EP-MCQ-11.s: A 55-year-old man has a lymphocyte-predominant pleural effusion with ADA 52 U/L. Pleural fluid cytology is negative, but he has generalised lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly. Which condition is the most important cause of a false-positive ADA to exclude?
CH-EP-MCQ-11.p: ADA สูง + lymphocyte เด่น → วัณโรค หรือ lymphoma

CH-EP-MCQ-12.s: Why is adenosine deaminase elevated in tuberculous serositis?
CH-EP-MCQ-12.a: It reflects T-lymphocyte proliferation and purine metabolism during an active cell-mediated immune response
CH-EP-MCQ-12.p: ADA = ตัวแทนของ T-cell ที่แบ่งตัว ไม่ใช่ของตัวเชื้อ

CH-EP-MCQ-13.s: Which ADA cut-off is used for tuberculous peritonitis in ascitic fluid, according to the lecture?

CH-EP-MCQ-14.s: A 34-year-old man has 4 weeks of low-grade fever, dry cough, left pleuritic chest pain and 5 kg weight loss. He did not improve after 7 days of amoxicillin-clavulanate plus azithromycin. Chest radiograph shows a moderate left pleural effusion without parenchymal infiltrate. What is the most appropriate next step?
CH-EP-MCQ-14.a: Diagnostic thoracentesis with cell count, protein, LDH, glucose, ADA, cytology, AFB smear, NAAT and mycobacterial culture
CH-EP-MCQ-14.p: น้ำในเยื่อหุ้มปอดที่ยังไม่รู้สาเหตุ → เจาะส่งตรวจให้ครบรวม ADA

CH-EP-MCQ-15.s: A 29-year-old woman has a lymphocytic exudative pleural effusion with ADA 74 U/L, negative AFB smear, negative Xpert MTB/RIF on pleural fluid and negative cytology. What is the best management?
CH-EP-MCQ-15.a: Start anti-tuberculous therapy (2IRZE/4IR) while awaiting mycobacterial culture
CH-EP-MCQ-15.p: TB pleura: เริ่มยาได้จาก ADA + lymphocyte · 6 เดือน · ไม่ให้ steroid

CH-EP-MCQ-16.s: A 26-year-old man has 6 weeks of painless, firm, bilateral posterior cervical lymph node enlargement without redness or warmth. He has low-grade evening fever. Which investigation gives the highest diagnostic yield?
CH-EP-MCQ-16.a: Fine needle aspiration or excisional biopsy of the node for histology, AFB, NAAT and culture
CH-EP-MCQ-16.p: ต่อมน้ำเหลืองโตเรื้อรัง → ต้องได้เนื้อเยื่อ (FNA/excision)

CH-EP-MCQ-17.s: A 58-year-old heavy smoker has a 3-cm hard, painless, fixed upper cervical lymph node for 2 months. FNA shows no granuloma. According to the lecture's approach, what must be done next?
CH-EP-MCQ-17.a: Search for a primary head and neck malignancy (e.g., nasopharynx) and obtain tissue diagnosis
CH-EP-MCQ-17.p: ก้อนที่คอแข็งยึดติดในผู้สูงอายุ → หามะเร็งศีรษะลำคอก่อน

CH-EP-MCQ-18.s: A woman with culture-confirmed, drug-susceptible TB lymphadenitis develops enlargement of the treated node and a new adjacent node 5 weeks into standard therapy. She is otherwise improving. What is the most appropriate management?
CH-EP-MCQ-18.a: Recognise a paradoxical reaction and continue the same regimen, aspirating the node if fluctuant
CH-EP-MCQ-18.p: LN โตขึ้นระหว่างรักษาเชื้อไวต่อยา = paradoxical reaction → ยาเดิมต่อ

CH-EP-MCQ-19.s: A 47-year-old man has 4 months of progressive thoracolumbar back pain with focal tenderness over T12, night sweats and weight loss. MRI shows destruction of the anterior T11–T12 vertebral bodies with a large bilateral paraspinal abscess extending into the psoas; the intervening disc is relatively preserved. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CH-EP-MCQ-19.p: ปวดหลังเป็นเดือน + ทำลายตัวกระดูกด้านหน้า + psoas abscess = Pott's

CH-EP-MCQ-20.s: A patient with TB spondylitis on standard therapy for 6 weeks has persistent lower-limb weakness from cord compression that has not improved. Which is the most appropriate step?
CH-EP-MCQ-20.a: Refer for urgent surgical decompression and stabilisation
CH-EP-MCQ-20.p: Pott's + neuro deficit ไม่ดีขึ้นแม้ได้ยา หรือ spinal instability → ผ่าตัด

CH-EP-MCQ-21.s: A 36-year-old man has 3 weeks of headache, low-grade fever and increasing drowsiness, with a new right sixth cranial nerve palsy. CSF: opening pressure raised, clear fluid, WBC 280/µL (80% lymphocytes), protein 240 mg/dL, glucose 32 mg/dL (blood glucose 110 mg/dL). What is the most appropriate treatment?

CH-EP-MCQ-22.s: Which CSF finding is characteristic of early tuberculous meningitis and may mislead the clinician?
CH-EP-MCQ-22.a: A neutrophil-predominant pleocytosis that later shifts to mononuclear cells
CH-EP-MCQ-22.p: CSF TB ระยะแรก PMN เด่นได้ แล้วเปลี่ยนเป็น mononuclear

CH-EP-MCQ-23.s: A patient with advanced HIV (CD4 25 cells/µL) not yet on antiretroviral therapy is diagnosed with tuberculous meningitis. When should ART generally be started?
CH-EP-MCQ-23.a: After about 4–8 weeks of anti-tuberculous therapy
CH-EP-MCQ-23.p: TBM + HIV → เริ่ม ART หลังยาวัณโรคราว 4–8 สัปดาห์

CH-EP-MCQ-24.s: A 44-year-old HIV-negative man has a large pericardial effusion. Pericardiocentesis yields serosanguinous fluid with lymphocyte predominance, high protein, ADA 62 U/L and no malignant cells. He is started on 2IRZE/4IR. Regarding adjunctive corticosteroid, which statement best matches the lecture?
CH-EP-MCQ-24.a: Conditional indication: may be used in HIV-negative patients because it reduces constriction and the need for pericardiocentesis or pericardiectomy
CH-EP-MCQ-24.p: Steroid: meningitis = absolute · pericarditis = conditional (HIV ลบ) · ที่เหลือ = ไม่แนะนำ

CH-EP-MCQ-25.s: A 32-year-old woman has 2 months of abdominal distension, diffuse abdominal pain, evening fever and weight loss. Ascitic fluid: SAAG 0.6 g/dL, total protein 4.8 g/dL, WBC 1,100/µL (88% lymphocytes), ADA 58 U/L, cytology negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CH-EP-MCQ-25.p: Ascites SAAG ต่ำ + protein สูง + lymphocyte + ADA > 36–40 = TB peritonitis

CH-EP-MCQ-26.s: A 40-year-old man has 3 months of right lower quadrant pain, fever and weight loss. CT shows thickening of the terminal ileum and caecum with enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes. Colonoscopic ileal biopsy shows caseating granulomas. What is the diagnosis and the key differential that the biopsy has helped exclude?
CH-EP-MCQ-26.p: Ileocecal thickening + caseating granuloma = intestinal TB (แยกจาก Crohn)

CH-EP-MCQ-27.s: A 52-year-old man with a history of treated pulmonary TB has recurrent dysuria and microscopic haematuria. Urinalysis repeatedly shows pyuria, but routine urine cultures are negative. Which test is most appropriate next?
CH-EP-MCQ-27.a: Three consecutive early-morning urine samples for AFB, NAAT and mycobacterial culture
CH-EP-MCQ-27.p: Sterile pyuria + hematuria → คิด GU TB → urine AFB/culture เช้า 3 วัน

CH-EP-MCQ-28.s: In genitourinary tuberculosis, which situation is an indication for nephrectomy according to the lecture?
CH-EP-MCQ-28.a: A non-functioning kidney associated with intractable hypertension or continuous severe flank pain
CH-EP-MCQ-28.p: GU TB: ผ่าตัดไตเมื่อไม่ทำงาน + HT คุมไม่ได้/ปวดสีข้างต่อเนื่อง

CH-EP-MCQ-29.s: Which extrapulmonary TB site requires the longest standard duration of treatment according to the Thai guideline shown in the lecture?
CH-EP-MCQ-29.p: CNS TB = 12 เดือน (2IRZE/10IR) — นานที่สุด

CH-EP-MCQ-30.s: For which form of tuberculosis is adjunctive corticosteroid NOT recommended as routine therapy?
CH-EP-MCQ-30.p: ไม่ให้ steroid: LN · pleura · bone/spine · GU

CH-EP-MCQ-31.s: A patient on 2IRZE for TB lymphadenitis develops purpura, thrombocytopenia and hypotension shortly after restarting his medication following a 2-week interruption. Which drug is most likely responsible?
CH-EP-MCQ-31.p: R: จ้ำเลือด เกล็ดเลือดต่ำ ช็อก flu-like — มักเกิดเมื่อกินยาไม่สม่ำเสมอ

CH-EP-MCQ-32.s: A 50-year-old man with diabetes and tuberculous pleuritis is starting 2IRZE/4IR. Which supplement should be given to prevent a nerve toxicity of this regimen?
CH-EP-MCQ-32.p: H → neuropathy → pyridoxine 50–100 มก./วัน

CH-EP-MCQ-33.s: A 30-year-old woman is diagnosed with tuberculous cervical lymphadenitis. Chest radiograph is normal and three sputum samples are negative by smear and Xpert. She asks whether she must be admitted to an isolation room. What is the most appropriate advice?
CH-EP-MCQ-33.a: She does not need airborne isolation, because extrapulmonary TB without pulmonary or laryngeal involvement is generally not transmissible by air
CH-EP-MCQ-33.p: EPTB ล้วนที่ตัดวัณโรคปอดแล้ว → ไม่ต้องแยกห้อง airborne

CH-RP-MCQ-01.s: A 30-year-old woman has Hb 6 g/dL from menorrhagia. SpO2 is 99% on room air and PaO2 is 98 mmHg. Increasing inspired oxygen raises her PaO2 to 300 mmHg. Which statement about her oxygen delivery is correct?
CH-RP-MCQ-01.a: Her arterial oxygen content is about 40% of normal, and raising PaO2 adds only about 0.6 mL O2/dL
CH-RP-MCQ-01.p: ซีดมาก sat 100% ก็ยังขาด O₂ ได้ — O₂ ที่ละลายช่วยน้อยมาก

CH-RP-MCQ-02.s: Which of the following shifts the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve to the RIGHT?
CH-RP-MCQ-02.p: 2,3-DPG ↑ = ขวา: ที่สูง ซีดเรื้อรัง ไทรอยด์เป็นพิษ

CH-RP-MCQ-03.s: A family of four is brought from a closed room heated by a charcoal stove. All have headache and confusion. The father's SpO2 is 99% on room air, but arterial blood gas shows a measured SaO2 of 72% by co-oximetry. What is the most likely explanation?
CH-RP-MCQ-03.p: SpO₂ ปกติ + อาการขาด O₂ + ห้องปิด → CO · ต้องวัด SaO₂ ด้วย co-oximetry

CH-RP-MCQ-04.s: An 82-year-old man with no lung disease has a routine arterial blood gas on room air: PaO2 65 mmHg, PaCO2 38 mmHg. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
CH-RP-MCQ-04.a: Within the acceptable range for his age
CH-RP-MCQ-04.p: PaO₂ ปกติลดตามอายุ — 80 ปี > 60 ก็ยอมรับได้

CH-RP-MCQ-05.s: A 25-year-old man is found drowsy after taking an unknown amount of his mother's morphine tablets. Room-air arterial blood gas: pH 7.22, PaCO2 70 mmHg, PaO2 55 mmHg. What is his alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient and what does it indicate?
CH-RP-MCQ-05.a: About 8 mmHg; hypoxaemia is fully explained by hypoventilation
CH-RP-MCQ-05.p: PaCO₂ สูง + A-a ปกติ = hypoventilation ล้วน → แก้ที่ ventilation

CH-RP-MCQ-06.s: Which patient's hypoxaemia is expected to have a NORMAL alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient?
CH-RP-MCQ-06.a: A 30-year-old woman with myasthenic crisis and no aspiration
CH-RP-MCQ-06.p: Neuromuscular → hypoventilation → A-a ปกติ · ติดตามด้วย FVC/NIF

CH-RP-MCQ-07.s: A 40-year-old man with ARDS from severe pneumonia is intubated. On FiO2 1.0 his PaO2 is only 70 mmHg. Increasing FiO2 further is not possible. Which intervention addresses the main mechanism of his hypoxaemia?
CH-RP-MCQ-07.a: Increase positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) to recruit collapsed alveoli
CH-RP-MCQ-07.p: Shunt ไม่ตอบ O₂ → แก้ด้วย PEEP/prone

CH-RP-MCQ-08.s: A 58-year-old man with interstitial lung disease has SpO2 96% at rest, which falls to 84% after walking for 3 minutes. Which mechanism best explains the exercise-induced desaturation?
CH-RP-MCQ-08.a: Diffusion limitation from shortened capillary transit time
CH-RP-MCQ-08.p: ILD: sat ตกตอนออกแรง = diffusion limitation

CH-MCQ-22.s: A 48-year-old previously healthy man has community-acquired pneumonia. On a non-rebreather mask at 15 L/min he is alert and cooperative, respiratory rate 30/min, SpO2 89%. Arterial blood gas: pH 7.46, PaCO2 31 mmHg, PaO2 56 mmHg, HCO3 22 mmol/L. Chest radiograph shows bilateral lower-zone consolidation. He is haemodynamically stable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in oxygen therapy?
CH-MCQ-22.a: High-flow nasal cannula oxygen with close monitoring of the ROX index
CH-MCQ-22.p: HFNC = ทางเลือกแรกของ type 1; BiPAP = ทางเลือกแรกของ type 2 — ติดตามด้วย ROX index, < 3.85 ที่ 12 ชม. ให้รีบใส่ท่อ

CH-OLD-32.s: A patient with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease has persistent dyspnoea and SpO2 88 percent despite oxygen by nasal cannula. ABG shows pH 7.28, PaCO2 65 mmHg and HCO3 28 mEq/L. He is alert and able to protect his airway. What is the most appropriate next step?

CH-RP-MCQ-09.s: A 62-year-old obese woman becomes hypoxaemic on postoperative day 1 after an upper abdominal operation. She is alert, temperature 37.4 °C, and has decreased breath sounds at both lung bases. Chest radiograph shows bibasal plate-like opacities. Which type of respiratory failure is this and what is the most appropriate initial management?
CH-RP-MCQ-09.a: Type 3 (perioperative) from atelectasis; sit upright, provide analgesia, incentive spirometry and early mobilisation
CH-RP-MCQ-09.p: หลังผ่าตัดวันแรก ปอดฐานแฟบ = Type III → เปิดปอดคืน

CH-OLD-33.s: A 60-year-old man has decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion at the right lower chest with decreased tactile fremitus and reduced chest wall expansion on that side. Which condition do these findings indicate?

CH-RP-MCQ-10.s: A 35-year-old man with right lower lobe pneumonia complains of sharp pain at the tip of his right shoulder that worsens with deep breathing. Shoulder examination is normal. Which nerve carries this pain?
CH-RP-MCQ-10.p: ปวดร้าวไหล่จากปอด = central diaphragmatic pleura → phrenic

CH-OLD-28.s: A 25-year-old tall thin man develops sudden right-sided chest pain and dyspnoea. Examination shows decreased breath sounds and hyperresonance to percussion on the right, with the trachea deviated to the left and blood pressure 80/50 mmHg. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
CH-OLD-28.a: Immediate needle decompression followed by intercostal chest drain insertion

CH-RP-MCQ-11.s: A 70-year-old man on mechanical ventilation suddenly becomes hypotensive (BP 70/40 mmHg) with rising peak airway pressures. Bedside ultrasound of the right anterior chest shows absent lung sliding and a 'barcode' pattern on M-mode; a lung point is seen in the right lateral chest. Which statement is correct?
CH-RP-MCQ-11.a: The lung point confirms pneumothorax; decompress immediately without waiting for a chest radiograph
CH-RP-MCQ-11.p: Lung point = ยืนยัน · บนเครื่องช่วยหายใจ + BP ตก = decompress เลย

CH-RP-MCQ-12.s: Which of the following patients has a SECONDARY spontaneous pneumothorax?
CH-RP-MCQ-12.p: Secondary = มีโรคปอดเดิม (COPD พบบ่อยสุด) → admit

CH-MCQ-18.s: A 68-year-old man with severe emphysema develops sudden right-sided chest pain and breathlessness. He is haemodynamically stable. Chest radiograph shows a 15 percent right pneumothorax with no mediastinal shift. Which management is most appropriate?
CH-MCQ-18.a: Admit and insert an intercostal chest drain
CH-MCQ-18.p: **ห้ามดำน้ำลึกตลอดชีวิต** หลังเป็น pneumothorax เว้นแต่ได้รับการผ่าตัดป้องกันแบบถาวร; การเดินทางโดยเครื่องบินให้รอจน **ปอดขยายเต็มที่และยืนยันด้วยภาพรังสี** (โดยทั่วไปรออย่างน้อย 1-2 สัปดาห์หลังหาย)

CH-MCQ-24.s: A 22-year-old tall, slim man who smokes 10 cigarettes a day has had his second right-sided primary spontaneous pneumothorax within 9 months; both were treated with intercostal drainage. He is an avid scuba diver and asks about future activities. Which of the following statements is the most appropriate advice?
