HON-WBC-MCQ-13.s: A 55-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis has a spleen palpable 8 cm below the costal margin. WBC 2,600/µL (ANC 1,300/µL), platelets 58,000/µL, haemoglobin 11 g/dL. Bone marrow is normocellular with normal maturation. Which mechanism best explains the neutropenia?
HON-WBC-MCQ-13.a: Sequestration of neutrophils in an enlarged spleen
HON-WBC-MCQ-13.p: ม้ามโต + ต่ำหลายสาย + ไขกระดูกปกติ = sequestration

HON-WBC-MCQ-14.s: A patient receiving chemotherapy has ANC 80/µL and fever 38.6 °C. Chest examination is normal, chest radiograph shows only a subtle opacity, and urinalysis shows no pyuria despite a urine culture later growing E. coli. Why are localising signs so scant?
HON-WBC-MCQ-14.a: Neutrophils are required to form pus and inflammatory infiltrates, so classic signs are blunted
HON-WBC-MCQ-14.p: ไม่มี neutrophil = ไม่มีหนอง — อย่ารอหาตำแหน่งติดเชื้อ

MOCK-056.s: 35yo woman presents with fatigue, bruising, fever. CBC: Hb 6.2, WBC 1,200 (ANC 200), Plt 12,000, Reticulocyte 0.1%. Bone marrow shows >90% fat space replacement. Diagnosis?

HON-WBC-MCQ-15.s: A 42-year-old man has 3 weeks of fatigue and swollen, spongy gums that bleed easily. WBC 68,000/µL with 70% large blasts with folded nuclei that are strongly non-specific esterase positive; haemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, platelets 31,000/µL. Why are the gums swollen?
HON-WBC-MCQ-15.a: Gingival infiltration by leukemic cells with monocytic differentiation
HON-WBC-MCQ-15.p: เหงือกบวม + blast = AML monocytic (M4/M5)

HON-WBC-MCQ-16.s: A 31-year-old woman presents with gum bleeding, widespread ecchymoses and heavy menstrual bleeding. Platelets 18,000/µL, PT prolonged, fibrinogen 72 mg/dL, D-dimer markedly raised. The smear shows abnormal promyelocytes with heavy granules and bundles of Auer rods. What is the most important immediate step?
HON-WBC-MCQ-16.a: Start all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) immediately while supporting with platelets and cryoprecipitate
HON-WBC-MCQ-16.p: สงสัย APL → ATRA ทันที · ห้าม leukapheresis

HON-WBC-MCQ-17.s: A 6-year-old boy has 2 weeks of leg pain that wakes him at night, limping, pallor and petechiae. There is tenderness over the sternum and tibiae. What mechanism best explains the bone pain?
HON-WBC-MCQ-17.a: Expansion of the marrow cavity by proliferating blasts, raising intramedullary pressure and stretching the periosteum
HON-WBC-MCQ-17.p: ปวดกระดูก + ซีด + จุดเลือดในเด็ก = คิดถึง ALL

HON-WBC-MCQ-18.s: A 64-year-old man with newly diagnosed AML has WBC 186,000/µL (90% blasts), haemoglobin 6.9 g/dL, platelets 22,000/µL, SpO2 89% on room air, headache and confusion. Which action should be avoided at this point?
HON-WBC-MCQ-18.a: Transfusing packed red cells to raise haemoglobin to 10 g/dL
HON-WBC-MCQ-18.p: Leukostasis: ห้ามให้ PRC จนกว่า WBC จะลด

HON-WBC-MCQ-19.s: Leukostasis develops in AML at WBC counts of 50,000–100,000/µL but is rarely seen in CLL even above 500,000/µL. What best explains this difference?
HON-WBC-MCQ-19.a: Myeloblasts are large, rigid and adhesive to endothelium, whereas CLL lymphocytes are small and deformable
HON-WBC-MCQ-19.p: Leukostasis ขึ้นกับขนาดและความแข็งของเซลล์ ไม่ใช่จำนวนอย่างเดียว

HON-WBC-MCQ-20.s: A 26-year-old man has a 3.5-cm rubbery, non-tender, matted right cervical lymph node mass for 2 months, with night sweats and 8 kg weight loss. What is the best next diagnostic step?
HON-WBC-MCQ-20.a: Excisional biopsy of an entire abnormal lymph node
HON-WBC-MCQ-20.p: สงสัย lymphoma → excisional biopsy · ห้าม steroid ก่อน

HON-WBC-MCQ-21.s: A 21-year-old woman has a 2-cm exquisitely tender, warm submandibular lymph node that appeared 3 days after a dental abscess. What best explains why this node is painful while lymphomatous nodes are typically painless?
HON-WBC-MCQ-21.a: Rapid inflammatory enlargement stretching the innervated nodal capsule
HON-WBC-MCQ-21.p: เจ็บ = โตเร็วจากการอักเสบ · ไม่เจ็บ = โตช้า

HON-WBC-MCQ-22.s: A 30-year-old man has several matted, firm-to-fluctuant posterior cervical nodes for 6 weeks, mild evening fever, and a chronic draining sinus over one node. Which pathological process best explains these features?
HON-WBC-MCQ-22.p: ต่อมคอเป็นพวง นิ่ม มีรูหนอง = TB

HON-WBC-MCQ-23.s: A 64-year-old man has early satiety, epigastric discomfort and 9 kg weight loss. A hard, fixed 2-cm node is palpable just above the medial end of the left clavicle. Which anatomical fact best explains the location of this node?
HON-WBC-MCQ-23.a: The thoracic duct carries lymph from the abdomen and empties into the left venous angle near this node
HON-WBC-MCQ-23.p: Supraclavicular ซ้ายแข็ง + อาการทางเดินอาหาร = Virchow node

HON-WBC-MCQ-24.s: A 29-year-old man has a painless, hard right testicular mass. Which lymph node group is the expected first site of lymphatic spread?
HON-WBC-MCQ-24.a: Para-aortic (retroperitoneal) nodes at the level of the renal hilum
HON-WBC-MCQ-24.p: อัณฑะ → para-aortic · ถุงอัณฑะ → ขาหนีบ

HON-WBC-MCQ-25.s: A 58-year-old woman has slowly enlarging, painless generalised lymphadenopathy for 3 years; biopsy shows grade 1–2 follicular lymphoma with t(14;18). Her 60-year-old neighbour has a 6-week history of a rapidly growing neck mass diagnosed as DLBCL. Why is the neighbour's lymphoma more likely to be cured with chemotherapy?
HON-WBC-MCQ-25.a: A higher proportion of DLBCL cells are actively dividing and therefore sensitive to cytotoxic drugs
HON-WBC-MCQ-25.p: Indolent ไม่หายขาด เพราะเซลล์ส่วนใหญ่ไม่แบ่งตัว

HON-WBC-MCQ-26.s: A 14-year-old boy has a right lower quadrant abdominal mass that has doubled in size over 10 days. Before any treatment: K 6.1 mmol/L, phosphate 7.8 mg/dL, uric acid 14 mg/dL, creatinine rising. Biopsy shows sheets of medium-sized cells with vacuolated cytoplasm and a 'starry sky' pattern. Which genetic event drives this tumour?
HON-WBC-MCQ-26.p: Burkitt = MYC t(8;14) · starry sky · TLS เอง

HON-WBC-MCQ-27.s: A 23-year-old woman with biopsy-proven classical Hodgkin lymphoma reports several symptoms. Which one, by itself, qualifies her disease for the 'B' designation?
HON-WBC-MCQ-27.a: Unexplained loss of 12% of body weight over the past 5 months
HON-WBC-MCQ-27.p: B = ไข้ > 38 · เหงื่อกลางคืน · น้ำหนักลด > 10%/6 เดือน

HON-WBC-MCQ-28.s: A 30-year-old man with Hodgkin lymphoma has involved cervical and mediastinal lymph nodes and an involved spleen. There is no liver, lung or bone marrow involvement. What is his Ann Arbor stage?
HON-WBC-MCQ-28.p: ม้ามนับเป็นระบบน้ำเหลือง · สองด้านของกะบังลม = III

HON-WBC-MCQ-29.s: A 68-year-old man with known CLL (lymphocytes 48,000/µL) has haemoglobin that fell from 12.5 to 7.9 g/dL over 2 weeks, with jaundice and dark urine. Reticulocytes 9%, indirect bilirubin and LDH raised, haptoglobin undetectable, direct antiglobulin test positive for IgG. What is the mechanism of his anaemia?
HON-WBC-MCQ-29.a: Autoimmune haemolysis from dysregulated immunity producing antibodies against red cells
HON-WBC-MCQ-29.p: CLL + ซีดเร็ว + retic สูง + DAT+ = AIHA (ทำลาย ไม่ใช่สร้างน้อย)

HON-WBC-MCQ-30.s: A 19-year-old man with Burkitt lymphoma starts chemotherapy. On day 2: K 6.4 mmol/L, phosphate 6.8 mg/dL, Ca 6.9 mg/dL, uric acid 12.6 mg/dL, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (baseline 0.8), urine output 0.3 mL/kg/h for 8 hours. He is already on allopurinol. Which additional drug most rapidly lowers his existing uric acid, and what must be checked?
HON-WBC-MCQ-30.p: TLS ที่เป็นแล้ว → rasburicase (ตรวจ G6PD) · allopurinol แค่กันใหม่

HON-WBC-MCQ-31.s: A 22-year-old woman has 3 weeks of facial swelling worse on bending, distended neck veins and dilated veins over the upper chest. She has no stridor, is alert, and SpO2 is 97%. CT shows a 9-cm anterior mediastinal mass and an enlarged left supraclavicular node. What is the most appropriate next step?
HON-WBC-MCQ-31.a: Obtain tissue first (biopsy of the supraclavicular node), with supportive care, before giving corticosteroids
HON-WBC-MCQ-31.p: SVC ไม่คุกคามชีวิต → ชิ้นเนื้อก่อน steroid

HON-WBC-MCQ-32.s: A 17-year-old boy has a large anterior mediastinal mass with SVC obstruction, together with pallor, fever and petechiae. CBC: haemoglobin 7.2 g/dL, WBC 92,000/µL with many blasts, platelets 19,000/µL. Which diagnosis best fits?
HON-WBC-MCQ-32.p: ก้อน mediastinum + BM failure + blast ในชายวัยรุ่น = T-ALL

HON-ONC-MCQ-01.s: A 52-year-old farmer from north-eastern Thailand who regularly eats raw fermented fish presents with painless jaundice and a hilar biliary mass. Which aetiological factor is most strongly associated with this cancer in this region?
HON-ONC-MCQ-01.p: ปลาดิบ + อีสาน + ก้อนที่ขั้วตับ = cholangiocarcinoma จากพยาธิใบไม้ตับ

MOCK-027.s: An epidemiological study examines global incidence of primary liver malignancies. Which of the following viral agents is recognized as the leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide?

HON-ONC-MCQ-02.s: A 58-year-old man has a completely resected stage III colon adenocarcinoma (3 of 14 nodes positive). What is the main purpose of offering him oxaliplatin plus fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy now?
HON-ONC-MCQ-02.a: To eradicate micrometastatic disease and improve disease-free and overall survival
HON-ONC-MCQ-02.p: Adjuvant = กำจัด micrometastasis หลังผ่าตัด

MOCK-026.s: Following complete resection of stage II colon cancer, a patient asks about the primary objective of adjuvant chemotherapy. Which of the following is the correct explanation?
MOCK-026.a: To eradicate microscopic residual metastatic disease and reduce the risk of disease recurrence

MOCK-024.s: A 60-year-old man presents with hematochezia and circumferential mass in the sigmoid colon. Biopsy yields adenocarcinoma. Which of the following staging investigations is necessary prior to definitive management?
MOCK-024.a: Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis

HON-ONC-MCQ-03.s: A 70-year-old woman with metastatic gastric cancer cares for herself but cannot work, and is up and about for more than half of her waking hours. What is her approximate ECOG performance status?
HON-ONC-MCQ-03.p: ECOG 2: ดูแลตัวเองได้ ทำงานไม่ได้ ลุก > 50%

HON-ONC-MCQ-04.s: Which of the following tumours is classically highly radiosensitive?
HON-ONC-MCQ-04.p: ไวรังสี: seminoma lymphoma SCC

HON-ONC-MCQ-05.s: A tumour carries a loss-of-function mutation in TP53. Which normal cellular response to DNA damage is most directly lost?
HON-ONC-MCQ-05.a: Arrest at the G1 checkpoint to allow DNA repair, or apoptosis if repair fails
HON-ONC-MCQ-05.p: p53 = ผู้พิทักษ์ genome ที่ G1 checkpoint

HON-ONC-MCQ-06.s: Which of the following is an original hallmark of cancer described by Hanahan and Weinberg?

HON-ONC-MCQ-07.s: Which chemotherapeutic agent acts specifically in the M phase by disrupting microtubules?

HON-ONC-MCQ-08.s: A 28-year-old man receiving bleomycin, etoposide and cisplatin (BEP) for testicular germ cell tumour develops progressive dyspnoea and dry cough with bibasal crackles and a restrictive defect. Which drug is most likely responsible?

HON-ONC-MCQ-09.s: A patient with metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma is being considered for cetuximab. Which biomarker result is required before using it?
HON-ONC-MCQ-09.p: Anti-EGFR mAb ใช้เฉพาะ RAS wild-type

HON-ONC-MCQ-10.s: A 62-year-old woman on bevacizumab for metastatic colon cancer is reviewed before her next cycle. Which adverse effect should be routinely monitored for this drug?
HON-ONC-MCQ-10.p: Anti-VEGF → ความดันสูง + proteinuria

HON-ONC-MCQ-11.s: A 55-year-old non-smoking Thai woman has metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with an EGFR exon 19 deletion. Which class of first-line therapy is most appropriate?

HON-ONC-MCQ-12.s: A 60-year-old man receiving pembrolizumab for NSCLC develops 7 watery stools per day above baseline with abdominal cramps (grade 3 colitis). Infection has been excluded. What is the most appropriate management?
HON-ONC-MCQ-12.a: Withhold pembrolizumab and start IV methylprednisolone 1–2 mg/kg/day
HON-ONC-MCQ-12.p: irAE grade 3 → หยุด ICI + methylpred 1–2 มก./กก.

HON-ONC-MCQ-13.s: Which statement correctly contrasts CTLA-4 and PD-1?
HON-ONC-MCQ-13.a: CTLA-4 regulates early T-cell activation (priming) in lymphoid tissue, whereas PD-1 inhibits effector T-cell activity in peripheral tissues and tumours

HON-ONC-MCQ-14.s: A 62-year-old postmenopausal woman has a 1.5 cm invasive ductal carcinoma, ER 90%, PgR 60%, HER2 negative, sentinel nodes negative, treated with breast-conserving surgery and radiotherapy. What is the most appropriate adjuvant systemic therapy?

HON-ONC-MCQ-15.s: A 38-year-old woman has invasive breast cancer, HER2 IHC 3+, with 2 positive axillary nodes. In addition to chemotherapy, which adjuvant targeted therapy is indicated and for how long?
HON-ONC-MCQ-15.p: HER2 3+/FISH+ → trastuzumab 1 ปี + เฝ้า LVEF

HON-ONC-MCQ-16.s: A 35-year-old woman's mother had breast cancer at 40 and her maternal aunt had ovarian cancer. Which is the most appropriate next step?
HON-ONC-MCQ-16.a: Refer for genetic counselling and BRCA1/2 testing
HON-ONC-MCQ-16.p: เต้านม < 45 + รังไข่ในครอบครัว → BRCA testing

HON-ONC-MCQ-17.s: A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman, 4 years after treatment for ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, presents with back pain. Imaging shows multiple bone metastases only; liver and lungs are clear. She is well. What is the preferred first-line systemic approach?
HON-ONC-MCQ-17.a: Endocrine therapy (an aromatase inhibitor, currently combined with a CDK4/6 inhibitor) plus a bone-modifying agent
HON-ONC-MCQ-17.p: HR+ แพร่ไปกระดูก ไม่มี visceral crisis → endocrine (+ CDK4/6i)

MOCK-025.s: A 50-year-old woman undergoes mastectomy for invasive ductal breast carcinoma (2.2 cm, margins negative, 0/12 axillary nodes, ER+, PR+, HER2-). Which of the following systemic adjuvant therapies is indicated?
MOCK-025.a: Adjuvant endocrine therapy (e.g., Tamoxifen or Aromatase Inhibitor)

MOCK-038.s: A 65-year-old man with metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases presents for palliative management. Which pharmacologic class reduces skeletal-related events?

HON-ONC-MCQ-18.s: A 64-year-old man had a curative resection for stage III colon cancer. His preoperative CEA was 18 ng/mL and fell to normal after surgery. What is the main role of measuring CEA during follow-up?
HON-ONC-MCQ-18.a: To detect recurrence early during surveillance
HON-ONC-MCQ-18.p: Marker ที่สูงก่อนรักษา → ใช้ติดตามการกลับเป็นซ้ำ

HON-ONC-MCQ-19.s: A 30-year-old woman with pelvic pain and fever has a tender adnexal mass and CA-125 of 160 U/mL. Which statement is most accurate?
HON-ONC-MCQ-19.a: CA-125 can be raised by pelvic inflammatory disease, endometriosis and menstruation, so it is non-specific in premenopausal women
HON-ONC-MCQ-19.p: CA-125 สูงเท็จใน PID endometriosis ก่อนหมดประจำเดือน

HON-ONC-MCQ-20.s: A 52-year-old woman asks about colorectal cancer screening. She has no symptoms and no family history. Which approach is appropriate in the Thai national programme?
HON-ONC-MCQ-20.a: Annual faecal immunochemical test (FIT), with colonoscopy if positive
HON-ONC-MCQ-20.p: คัดกรองลำไส้ใหญ่ไทย: FIT 50–70 → บวก → colonoscopy

MOCK-033.s: A 68-year-old man with a 30 pack-year smoking history undergoes screening for lung cancer. Which of the following modalities is recommended by international clinical guidelines?
MOCK-033.a: Annual low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) of the chest

HON-ONC-MCQ-21.s: A 63-year-old smoker has a central lung mass, confusion and serum sodium 118 mmol/L with euvolaemia and inappropriately concentrated urine. Biopsy is pending. Which histology is most likely?
HON-ONC-MCQ-21.p: SCLC = กลางปอด + SIADH/ACTH/LEMS

HON-ONC-MCQ-22.s: A 66-year-old man presents with fatigue and iron-deficiency anaemia (Hb 8.9 g/dL, ferritin 6 ng/mL). He denies GI symptoms. Which investigation is most important?
HON-ONC-MCQ-22.p: ชายสูงอายุขาดเหล็ก → ส่องกล้องบน + ล่าง

HON-ONC-MCQ-23.s: A patient has newly diagnosed metastatic colorectal cancer with multiple liver metastases. Tumour testing shows mismatch-repair deficiency (dMMR/MSI-high). What is the preferred first-line systemic therapy?
HON-ONC-MCQ-23.p: mCRC MSI-H/dMMR → pembrolizumab ก่อน

MOCK-022.s: A 62-year-old male with a 40 pack-year smoking history presents with progressive dysphagia, initially to solid foods and now to liquids, over the past 3 months, accompanied by an 8-kg weight loss. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic procedure?
MOCK-022.a: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with tissue biopsy

MOCK-023.s: A 58-year-old heavy smoker presents with a central lung mass. Serum lab shows Sodium 118 mEq/L, consistent with SIADH. Biopsy confirms small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC). Which of the following is the primary definitive treatment strategy?

MOCK-032.s: A 60-year-old man presents with early satiety, epigastric discomfort, weight loss, and a palpable firm left supraclavicular lymph node (Virchow’s node). Which of the following is the diagnostic test of choice?
MOCK-032.a: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with mucosal biopsy

MOCK-029.s: A 64-year-old former shipyard worker presents with progressive dyspnea, chest pain, and weight loss. Chest CT reveals nodular pleural thickening and pleural effusion. Biopsy confirms malignant mesothelioma. Exposure to which substance is the primary etiologic factor?

HON-ONC-MCQ-24.s: A 24-year-old man has a painless, firm right testicular mass. AFP and β-hCG are raised. What is the correct first step after scrotal ultrasound?
HON-ONC-MCQ-24.p: ก้อนอัณฑะ → inguinal orchiectomy ห้ามผ่านถุงอัณฑะ

HON-ONC-MCQ-25.s: A 72-year-old man has worsening low back pain, PSA 210 ng/mL and multiple sclerotic (osteoblastic) lesions on bone scan. What is the backbone of systemic treatment?
HON-ONC-MCQ-25.a: Androgen deprivation therapy (with an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor)
HON-ONC-MCQ-25.p: Prostate แพร่กระจาย → ADT + ARPI

MOCK-034.s: A 45-year-old woman presents with persistent abdominal bloating and a solid, fixed adnexal mass on ultrasound with serum CA-125 elevated at 450 U/mL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

MOCK-036.s: A 52-year-old man presents with gross painless hematuria, right flank pain, a palpable abdominal mass, and polycythemia (Hb 18.5 g/dL). CT shows hypervascular renal mass. Which of the following is the diagnosis?

MOCK-037.s: A pathology report of fine-needle aspiration from a thyroid nodule describes psammoma bodies, ground-glass nuclei (Orphan Annie eyes), and nuclear grooves. Which thyroid malignancy is indicated?

MOCK-021.s: A 65-year-old man presents with a slow-growing, pearly papule with central ulceration and telangiectasias on his right cheek. Skin biopsy confirms basal cell carcinoma. Which of the following is the primary localized treatment of choice?

MOCK-028.s: A 55-year-old woman with treated right breast carcinoma 3 years ago presents with progressive headache and motor aphasia. Brain MRI reveals a single ring-enhancing lesion at the left frontal cortex with vasogenic edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

HON-ONC-MCQ-26.s: Ten days after chemotherapy for breast cancer, a woman has a temperature of 38.6 °C, BP 118/70 mmHg and ANC 200/µL. No focus is found. After blood cultures, what is the most appropriate next step?
HON-ONC-MCQ-26.a: Start IV anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam (e.g. cefepime or piperacillin–tazobactam) within 1 hour
HON-ONC-MCQ-26.p: FN → antipseudomonal β-lactam ภายใน 1 ชม.

HON-ONC-MCQ-27.s: Two days after starting chemotherapy for bulky Burkitt lymphoma, a patient has K 6.4 mmol/L, phosphate 8.2 mg/dL, uric acid 14 mg/dL, Ca 6.8 mg/dL and rising creatinine. G6PD status is normal. What is the best management?
HON-ONC-MCQ-27.a: Aggressive IV hydration, rasburicase, treatment of hyperkalaemia and early nephrology input
HON-ONC-MCQ-27.p: TLS ที่เกิดแล้ว → สารน้ำ + rasburicase + แก้ K

HON-ONC-MCQ-28.s: A 66-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer has 2 weeks of worsening thoracic back pain, worse lying down, and today new leg weakness and numbness below the umbilicus. What should be done first?
HON-ONC-MCQ-28.a: High-dose dexamethasone immediately, then urgent whole-spine MRI
HON-ONC-MCQ-28.p: Cord compression: dexamethasone → MRI ทั้งแนวด่วน

HON-ONC-MCQ-29.s: A 70-year-old woman with lung squamous cell carcinoma is confused and dehydrated. Calcium is 14.2 mg/dL, PTH is suppressed and PTHrP is raised. Which initial treatment is most appropriate?
HON-ONC-MCQ-29.a: IV normal saline followed by IV zoledronic acid
HON-ONC-MCQ-29.p: Hypercalcemia of malignancy: NSS → zoledronic acid

MOCK-031.s: A 68-year-old man presents with massive right pleural effusion. Cytological examination reveals malignant cells. Which of the following is the primary mechanism of pleural effusion accumulation in this patient?
MOCK-031.a: Tumor invasion of pleural lymphatics leading to impaired lymphatic drainage

HON-ANM-MCQ-90.s: A 35-year-old woman has had fatigue and mild scleral icterus for 10 days. She is alert; BP 116/70 mmHg, HR 94/min, no chest pain. Hb 7.0 g/dL, Hct 21%, MCV 99 fL, WBC and platelet counts are normal. Her Hb was 12.6 g/dL four months ago. Reticulocyte count is 8%. Which interpretation and next step is most appropriate?
HON-ANM-MCQ-90.a: Corrected reticulocyte about 3.7%; hyperproliferative marrow, so look for blood loss and send hemolysis markers, a blood smear and a DAT
HON-ANM-MCQ-90.p: Corrected retic = %retic × Hct/45 · ≥ 2% = เสียเลือด/แตก · < 2% = ผลิตไม่พอ

HON-ANM-MCQ-91.s: A 74-year-old man with known coronary artery disease presents with 2 days of exertional chest tightness and dizziness. HR 118/min, BP 96/60 mmHg with an orthostatic drop. ECG shows new ST depression in V4–V6. Hb 6.4 g/dL, MCV 74 fL. He has no overt bleeding. What is the best approach?
HON-ANM-MCQ-91.a: Stabilize first: draw diagnostic samples, transfuse packed red cells, treat the ischemia, and run the anemia work-up in parallel
HON-ANM-MCQ-91.p: Warning sign = stabilize first, run algorithms in parallel — เจาะเลือดเก็บก่อนให้เลือด

HON-ANM-MCQ-92.s: A 26-year-old Thai woman has a premarital blood test. She is asymptomatic and has normal menses. Hb 10.8 g/dL, MCV 64 fL, MCH 20 pg, RBC 5.7 × 10^6/µL, RDW 13.6%, WBC and platelets normal. Ferritin 82 ng/mL and CRP are normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
HON-ANM-MCQ-92.p: MCV ต่ำ ferritin ปกติ RBC สูง → Hb analysis ไม่ใช่ยาเหล็ก

HON-ANM-MCQ-93.s: A 22-year-old Thai man develops dark (cola-coloured) urine and jaundice 2 days after starting primaquine for Plasmodium vivax malaria. Hb 7.8 g/dL (baseline 14.5), MCV 94 fL, reticulocyte 7%, indirect bilirubin 4.1 mg/dL, LDH 980 U/L, haptoglobin undetectable, DAT negative. The smear shows bite cells, eccentrocytes and ghost cells. A quantitative G6PD assay sent today is within the normal range. What is the best interpretation?
HON-ANM-MCQ-93.a: The G6PD result is likely falsely normal because older enzyme-deficient cells have lysed; repeat the assay about 2–3 months after recovery
HON-ANM-MCQ-93.p: Bite/ghost cell + ยา oxidant = G6PD · ตรวจตอนแตกอาจปกติเทียม

HON-ANM-MCQ-94.s: A 45-year-old man has 3 weeks of progressive fatigue, gum bleeding and a fever of 38.6 °C. He is hemodynamically stable. Examination shows pallor and scattered petechiae, without hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy. Hb 7.2 g/dL, MCV 92 fL, WBC 1,600/µL (ANC 400/µL), platelets 14,000/µL, corrected reticulocyte 0.3%. B12, folate and liver function are normal. Besides blood cultures and empirical antibiotics, which investigation is most important to establish the diagnosis?
HON-ANM-MCQ-94.a: Bone marrow aspiration and trephine biopsy
HON-ANM-MCQ-94.p: Subacute + pancytopenia + retic < 2% → bone marrow study

HON-ANM-MCQ-01.s: A 30-year-old woman presents with 3 weeks of fatigue. Hb 8.0 g/dL, Hct 25%, MCV 86 fL, reticulocyte count 6%. There is no recent bleeding. Which interpretation of her reticulocyte response is most accurate?
HON-ANM-MCQ-01.a: Reticulocyte production index about 1.7, indicating an inadequate marrow response for this degree of anemia
HON-ANM-MCQ-01.p: Retic% → × Hct/45 → ÷ maturation time (Hct 25 = 2 วัน) · RPI < 2 = โรงงานตอบสนองไม่พอ

HON-ANM-MCQ-02.s: A 4-year-old girl has Hb 9.5 g/dL, MCV 64 fL and MCH 19 pg. Her erythroblasts have normal DNA synthesis. Which mechanism best explains why her circulating red cells are small?
HON-ANM-MCQ-02.a: Slow accumulation of cytoplasmic hemoglobin lets erythroblasts undergo extra divisions before reaching the hemoglobin level that stops division
HON-ANM-MCQ-02.p: Micro = Hb มาช้า แบ่งเกิน · macro megaloblastic = DNA มาช้า แบ่งน้อย

HON-ANM-MCQ-03.s: A 61-year-old man with stage 4 chronic kidney disease has Hb 8.6 g/dL, MCV 88 fL, reticulocyte production index 0.5, ferritin 320 ng/mL and transferrin saturation 31%. He is started on an oral drug that raises his Hb over 8 weeks without being an erythropoietin analog. By which mechanism does this drug work?
HON-ANM-MCQ-03.a: It inhibits prolyl hydroxylase so HIF-α escapes VHL-mediated degradation, increasing endogenous EPO and iron availability
HON-ANM-MCQ-03.p: O2 → PHD → HIF-α ถูกทำลาย · ขาด O2 (หรือยา HIF-PHI) → HIF-2α → EPO

HON-ANM-MCQ-04.s: A 63-year-old man reports 2 months of exertional fatigue. He has no visible bleeding and takes no medication. Hb 9.1 g/dL, MCV 71 fL, RDW 18.5%, platelets 480,000/µL, ferritin 7 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 6%. Abdominal examination is normal. What is the most appropriate next step?
HON-ANM-MCQ-04.a: Arrange bidirectional endoscopy (gastroscopy and colonoscopy) and start iron replacement
HON-ANM-MCQ-04.p: IDA ในชาย/หญิงหมดประจำเดือน = เลือดออกทางเดินอาหารจนกว่าจะพิสูจน์ว่าไม่ใช่

HON-ANM-MCQ-05.s: A 25-year-old woman with heavy menstrual bleeding and IDA (Hb 9.8 g/dL, ferritin 6 ng/mL) was prescribed ferrous sulfate 200 mg three times daily. She stopped after 1 week because of nausea and constipation. She is switched to a single 200 mg tablet every other morning. What is the physiological rationale for this regimen?
HON-ANM-MCQ-05.a: A dose of oral iron raises serum hepcidin for about 24 hours, which degrades ferroportin and reduces absorption of the next dose; spacing doses improves fractional absorption
HON-ANM-MCQ-05.p: เหล็กมื้อเดียว → hepcidin สูง ~24 ชม. → วันละครั้ง/วันเว้นวันดูดซึมดีกว่าวันละหลายมื้อ

HON-ANM-MCQ-06.s: A 19-year-old female regular blood donor feels well. Hb 12.9 g/dL, MCV 87 fL, RDW 13.2%, serum ferritin 10 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 24%, CRP normal. Which stage of iron deficiency best describes her?
HON-ANM-MCQ-06.a: Iron depletion: storage iron is exhausted while iron supply to erythropoiesis is still adequate
HON-ANM-MCQ-06.p: Ferritin ตกก่อน (ระยะคลังหมด) → TSAT ตก → Hb ตก → MCV ตก

HON-ANM-MCQ-07.s: A 47-year-old woman with active rheumatoid arthritis has Hb 9.8 g/dL, MCV 83 fL, reticulocyte production index 0.8, serum iron 35 µg/dL, TIBC 220 µg/dL (low), transferrin saturation 16%, ferritin 280 ng/mL, soluble transferrin receptor normal, CRP 45 mg/L. Which mechanism is mainly responsible for her low serum iron?
HON-ANM-MCQ-07.a: IL-6–induced hepcidin causing internalization and degradation of ferroportin on macrophages and enterocytes
HON-ANM-MCQ-07.p: ACD = hepcidin ปิด ferroportin → ferritin สูงแต่ serum iron ต่ำ · TIBC ต่ำ

HON-ANM-MCQ-08.s: A 58-year-old man with rheumatoid arthritis has taken naproxen daily for years. Hb 8.9 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, RDW 17%, serum iron 22 µg/dL, TIBC 310 µg/dL, transferrin saturation 7%, ferritin 72 ng/mL, CRP 30 mg/L, soluble transferrin receptor raised (sTfR/log ferritin index 3.2). Which interpretation is most appropriate?
HON-ANM-MCQ-08.a: Anemia of inflammation with coexisting absolute iron deficiency; replace iron and look for a gastrointestinal bleeding source
HON-ANM-MCQ-08.p: อักเสบอยู่: ferritin 30–100 + TSAT < 20% หรือ sTfR/log ferritin > 2 = มี IDA ร่วม

HON-ANM-MCQ-09.s: A 52-year-old woman with long-standing active rheumatoid arthritis has anemia of inflammation (Hb 9.6 g/dL, ferritin 310 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 14%). Three months of oral ferrous sulfate produced no change. After she starts tocilizumab, her Hb rises to 12.1 g/dL within 8 weeks without iron. Which explanation is best?
HON-ANM-MCQ-09.a: Blocking the IL-6 receptor reduces STAT3-driven hepcidin transcription, restoring ferroportin so iron is released from macrophages and absorbed from the gut
HON-ANM-MCQ-09.p: รักษา ACD = ลดการอักเสบ → ลด hepcidin · oral iron มักไม่ได้ผลเพราะ hepcidin ปิดลำไส้

HON-ANM-MCQ-10.s: A 41-year-old man has been taking isoniazid for latent tuberculosis for 5 months without any vitamin supplement. He reports fatigue and tingling in his feet. Hb 9.0 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, RDW 19%, serum iron 210 µg/dL, transferrin saturation 68%, ferritin 640 ng/mL. Hb typing is normal. Bone marrow shows many ringed sideroblasts. Which enzyme step is primarily impaired?
HON-ANM-MCQ-10.p: INH → B6 ↓ → ALAS2 ทำงานไม่ได้ → sideroblastic anemia + neuropathy · ป้องกันด้วย B6

HON-ANM-MCQ-11.s: A 54-year-old woman had Roux-en-Y gastric bypass 6 years ago and takes high-dose zinc supplements for hair loss. She has progressive gait unsteadiness and numb feet. Hb 8.7 g/dL, MCV 99 fL, ANC 900/µL, platelets 160,000/µL. Serum B12 and folate are normal. Bone marrow shows ringed sideroblasts and cytoplasmic vacuoles in myeloid and erythroid precursors. Which test is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?
HON-ANM-MCQ-11.p: Zinc เกิน/หลัง bypass → copper ↓ → ซีด + neutropenia + myeloneuropathy + ringed sideroblast เลียนแบบ MDS

HON-ANM-MCQ-12.s: A 22-year-old man has lifelong mild anemia that never improved with oral iron. His maternal uncle had a similar problem and died of heart failure. Hb 9.4 g/dL, MCV 66 fL, RDW 21%, ferritin 910 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 78%, HbA2 2.6% and no abnormal hemoglobin on HPLC. Smear shows dimorphic red cells with Pappenheimer bodies. What is the most likely diagnosis and the first mechanism-directed treatment?
HON-ANM-MCQ-12.a: X-linked sideroblastic anemia from ALAS2 mutation; a trial of pyridoxine plus management of iron overload
HON-ANM-MCQ-12.p: Microcytic + TSAT สูง + ชายที่มีญาติฝั่งแม่ = นึกถึง ALAS2 → ลอง pyridoxine

HON-ANM-MCQ-19.s: A 3-year-old boy lives beside a small car-battery recycling shop. He has 2 weeks of abdominal pain, constipation and irritability but is alert with a normal neurologic examination. Hb 9.6 g/dL, MCV 70 fL; smear shows coarse basophilic stippling. Venous blood lead level is 52 µg/dL. Which management is most appropriate?
HON-ANM-MCQ-19.a: Remove him from the exposure source and start oral succimer
HON-ANM-MCQ-19.p: เด็ก BLL ≥ 45 → succimer · ≥ 70 หรือ encephalopathy → BAL + CaNa₂EDTA · เอาออกจากแหล่งก่อนเสมอ

HON-ANM-MCQ-13.s: A Thai couple attends their first antenatal visit at 9 weeks. Both have MCV about 68 fL and normal ferritin. Hemoglobin typing in both is A2A with HbA2 2.4%. PCR shows that each partner is heterozygous for the --SEA deletion (--SEA/αα). Which statement about this pregnancy is correct?
HON-ANM-MCQ-13.a: The fetus has a 25% risk of Hb Bart's hydrops fetalis, so prenatal diagnosis should be offered
HON-ANM-MCQ-13.p: α⁰ แบบ cis (--SEA) × α⁰ แบบ cis = ลูก 25% Hb Bart's · Hb typing ปกติไม่ตัด α-thal

HON-ANM-MCQ-14.s: A 26-year-old Thai woman with known HbH-Constant Spring disease presents with fever from pyelonephritis. Her usual Hb is 8.0 g/dL; now it is 5.4 g/dL with dark urine, jaundice and reticulocytes 12%. A brilliant cresyl blue preparation shows many cells with evenly distributed 'golf-ball' inclusions. What is the main mechanism of her anemia?
HON-ANM-MCQ-14.a: Unstable β4 tetramers precipitate under oxidant stress, damaging the membrane and causing splenic removal plus some intravascular hemolysis
HON-ANM-MCQ-14.p: HbH = β4 ไม่เสถียร → ตกตะกอนเมื่อเจอ oxidant → hemolytic crisis ตอนมีไข้

HON-ANM-MCQ-15.s: At 28 weeks of gestation, ultrasound of a fetus of a Thai couple who both carry α⁰-thalassemia shows cardiomegaly, ascites, skin edema and a thick placenta. Cordocentesis shows Hb 5 g/dL composed mainly of Hb Bart's with no HbA or HbF. Which mechanism best explains the fetal hydrops?
HON-ANM-MCQ-15.a: γ4 tetramers lack cooperativity and the Bohr effect, so they have a very high oxygen affinity and do not release oxygen to tissues, causing hypoxic high-output cardiac failure
HON-ANM-MCQ-15.p: Hb Bart's (γ4) ปล่อย O2 ไม่ได้ → ขาด O2 → high-output heart failure → hydrops

HON-ANM-MCQ-16.s: A 15-year-old boy from northeastern Thailand has HbE/β⁰-thalassemia. His Hb has stayed at 7.5–8.0 g/dL and he has received only 3 transfusions in his life. He has hepatosplenomegaly. Ferritin 1,450 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 85%, liver iron concentration 9 mg Fe/g dry weight. What is the main mechanism of his iron overload?
HON-ANM-MCQ-16.a: Ineffective erythropoiesis releases erythroferrone, which suppresses hepatic hepcidin and increases intestinal iron absorption
HON-ANM-MCQ-16.p: NTDT: ineffective erythropoiesis → ERFE → hepcidin ↓ → ดูดซึมเหล็กเพิ่ม → ต้องตรวจเหล็กเกินแม้ไม่ค่อยให้เลือด

HON-ANM-MCQ-17.s: A 27-year-old Thai woman at 12 weeks of gestation has Hb 9.9 g/dL, MCV 63 fL, RBC 5.4 × 10⁶/µL, RDW 16%, ferritin 8 ng/mL. Hb typing (HPLC) shows A2A with HbA2 3.3% and no HbE. Her husband is a known β-thalassemia carrier. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
HON-ANM-MCQ-17.a: Coexisting iron deficiency can lower HbA2 and mask β-thalassemia trait, so she needs iron replacement and β-globin DNA testing promptly given her husband's status
HON-ANM-MCQ-17.p: IDA กด HbA2 → β-thal trait ซ่อนได้ · Mentzer เป็นแค่ตัวชี้ทาง ไม่ใช่การวินิจฉัย

HON-ANM-MCQ-18.s: A 2-year-old boy with β⁰/β⁰-thalassemia (no HbA, HbF 97%) has Hb 6.2 g/dL, poor growth, frontal bossing and splenomegaly. He is starting a regular transfusion program. Which plan best reflects the mechanism-based goal of therapy?
HON-ANM-MCQ-18.a: Keep the pre-transfusion Hb at about 9.5–10.5 g/dL to suppress ineffective erythropoiesis and marrow expansion, and start iron chelation once ferritin exceeds about 1,000 ng/mL or after about 10–20 transfusions
HON-ANM-MCQ-18.p: TDT: Hb ก่อนให้ 9.5–10.5 เพื่อกดไขกระดูก · chelation เมื่อ ferritin > 1,000 หรือ 10–20 ยูนิต

HON-ANM-MCQ-20.s: A 68-year-old woman with vitiligo and treated Hashimoto thyroiditis presents with 4 months of fatigue, tingling feet and unsteadiness that is worse in the dark. Romberg sign is positive. Hb 7.8 g/dL, MCV 118 fL, WBC 3,200/µL, platelets 98,000/µL, reticulocytes 0.5%. LDH 2,450 U/L, indirect bilirubin 2.4 mg/dL, haptoglobin < 10 mg/dL. The smear shows macro-ovalocytes and neutrophils with 6–7 nuclear lobes. Which mechanism best explains the markedly elevated LDH?
HON-ANM-MCQ-20.a: Apoptosis of megaloblastic erythroid precursors within the bone marrow
HON-ANM-MCQ-20.p: LDH หลักพัน + retic ต่ำ + MCV สูง = intramedullary hemolysis ของ megaloblast ไม่ใช่ TTP

HON-ANM-MCQ-21.s: A 55-year-old man who has taken metformin for 9 years has macrocytic anemia (Hb 10.9 g/dL, MCV 109 fL) and reduced vibration sense in both toes. Serum vitamin B12 is 240 pg/mL (reference > 200) and serum folate is normal. Which pair of results would best confirm tissue vitamin B12 deficiency?
HON-ANM-MCQ-21.a: Elevated methylmalonic acid and elevated homocysteine
HON-ANM-MCQ-21.p: B12 ขาด: MMA ↑ + Hcy ↑ · folate ขาด: Hcy ↑ อย่างเดียว · MMA สูงปลอมในไตวาย

HON-ANM-MCQ-22.s: A 74-year-old man with pernicious anemia (Hb 5.9 g/dL, MCV 121 fL, serum potassium 4.0 mmol/L) is started on intramuscular hydroxocobalamin 1 mg. Forty-eight hours later he reports leg weakness and palpitations; ECG shows flattened T waves and prominent U waves. Which mechanism best explains this complication?
HON-ANM-MCQ-22.a: Uptake of potassium into rapidly proliferating new erythroid precursors
HON-ANM-MCQ-22.p: เริ่ม B12 ในรายซีดมาก → ตรวจ K⁺ วันที่ 1–3 และระวังขาดเหล็กตามมา

HON-ANM-MCQ-23.s: A 63-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis has been taking methotrexate 20 mg weekly without any folate supplement. She was recently given trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole for a urinary tract infection. She now has painful oral ulcers, Hb 8.4 g/dL, MCV 108 fL, WBC 1,900/µL and platelets 62,000/µL. Methotrexate is stopped. Which agent most directly restores her cells' thymidylate synthesis?
HON-ANM-MCQ-23.p: DHFR ถูกบล็อก (MTX, pyrimethamine) → ให้ leucovorin ที่ข้าม DHFR

HON-ANM-MCQ-24.s: A 29-year-old woman at 30 weeks of a twin pregnancy has fatigue and a sore tongue. Hb 8.6 g/dL, MCV 112 fL, reticulocytes 0.6%, hypersegmented neutrophils on smear. Neurological examination including vibration and position sense is normal. Serum folate is low, homocysteine is elevated and methylmalonic acid is normal. Which statement best explains why she has no subacute combined degeneration?
HON-ANM-MCQ-24.a: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase does not require folate, so methylmalonyl-CoA is still converted to succinyl-CoA
HON-ANM-MCQ-24.p: Mutase ใช้ B12 อย่างเดียว → MMA ปกติใน folate ขาด → ไม่มี SCD

HON-ANM-MCQ-25.s: A 71-year-old man with macrocytic anemia (Hb 8.1 g/dL, MCV 117 fL) and mild numbness of the feet is started on folic acid 5 mg daily while vitamin B12 results are pending. Six weeks later his hemoglobin is 11.8 g/dL, but he now has a broad-based gait, a positive Romberg sign and extensor plantar responses. Serum B12 returns at 90 pg/mL. Which mechanism best explains this course?
HON-ANM-MCQ-25.a: Folic acid is reduced by DHFR to tetrahydrofolate, bypassing the B12-dependent methionine synthase step and restoring DNA synthesis, while the methylmalonyl-CoA mutase defect persists
HON-ANM-MCQ-25.p: Folate เดี่ยวแก้เลือดแต่ไม่แก้ myelin → ตัด B12 ก่อนเสมอ

HON-ANM-MCQ-26.s: A 22-year-old man developed acute hepatitis 10 weeks ago; tests for hepatitis A, B, C and E were negative and his liver enzymes normalised. He now has gum bleeding and fever. There is no lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly. ANC 0.15 × 10⁹/L, platelets 8 × 10⁹/L, absolute reticulocytes 10 × 10⁹/L, MCV 96 fL. Trephine biopsy shows 5% cellularity with fat replacement and no abnormal cells. Chromosome breakage testing is normal. His brother is a full HLA match. What is the best classification and definitive treatment?
HON-ANM-MCQ-26.a: Very severe aplastic anemia; allogeneic stem cell transplantation from the HLA-matched sibling
HON-ANM-MCQ-26.p: Very severe AA = ANC < 0.2 · อายุน้อย + sibling donor → HSCT

HON-ANM-MCQ-27.s: A 35-year-old woman is diagnosed with severe aplastic anemia. Flow cytometry shows a 6% granulocyte population lacking CD59 and FLAER binding. She responds to horse antithymocyte globulin plus cyclosporine. Which mechanism best explains both her marrow failure and the presence of the CD59-negative population?
HON-ANM-MCQ-27.a: Cytotoxic T cells secreting IFN-γ and TNF-α induce Fas-mediated apoptosis of stem cells, while GPI-deficient stem cells escape the immune attack and expand
HON-ANM-MCQ-27.p: PNH clone ใน AA = ร่องรอยของ immune escape ไม่ใช่สาเหตุของ aplasia

HON-ANM-MCQ-28.s: A 62-year-old farmer is referred for pancytopenia: Hb 7.9 g/dL, WBC 2,100/µL, platelets 41,000/µL. Which additional finding most strongly argues against a diagnosis of aplastic anemia?
HON-ANM-MCQ-28.a: Spleen palpable 6 cm below the costal margin
HON-ANM-MCQ-28.p: Pancytopenia + ม้ามโต = มองหาโรคอื่นก่อน AA

HON-ANM-MCQ-29.s: A 58-year-old man with diabetic nephropathy (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m², not on dialysis) has fatigue. Hb 8.9 g/dL, MCV 88 fL, reticulocytes 0.6%, ferritin 320 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 14%, CRP 12 mg/L. B12 and folate are normal and stool occult blood is negative. What is the most appropriate next step?
HON-ANM-MCQ-29.a: Give iron (oral trial or intravenous) before or together with starting an ESA
HON-ANM-MCQ-29.p: CKD: เติมเหล็กก่อน ESA เมื่อ TSAT ≤ 30% และ ferritin ≤ 500

HON-ANM-MCQ-30.s: A 66-year-old woman on maintenance hemodialysis is switched from injectable epoetin to oral daprodustat. Which mechanism explains how this drug raises her hemoglobin?
HON-ANM-MCQ-30.a: It inhibits prolyl hydroxylase so that HIF-α escapes VHL-mediated degradation, increasing endogenous EPO and lowering hepcidin
HON-ANM-MCQ-30.p: HIF-PH inhibitor = หลอกไตว่าขาด O₂ → EPO ตัวเอง ↑ + hepcidin ↓

HON-ANM-MCQ-31.s: A 49-year-old man on hemodialysis for 3 years had a stable Hb of 10.8 g/dL on epoetin. Over 2 months his Hb fell to 8.7 g/dL despite doubling the epoetin dose. Reticulocytes 1.0%, MCV 82 fL, ferritin 90 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 12%, CRP normal, PTH mildly elevated and stable, Kt/V adequate. What is the most likely cause of his ESA hyporesponsiveness?
HON-ANM-MCQ-31.a: Absolute iron deficiency from blood loss
HON-ANM-MCQ-31.p: ESA ดื้อ → ดู ferritin/TSAT ก่อน · PRCA = retic เกือบศูนย์ + ferritin สูง

HON-ANM-MCQ-32.s: A 52-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis (Child–Pugh C, MELD 27) has deepening jaundice. His spleen is palpable 5 cm below the costal margin. Hb has fallen from 10.0 to 6.8 g/dL over 3 weeks without bleeding. Reticulocytes 9%, LDH 520 U/L, direct antiglobulin test negative. The smear shows many dense red cells with irregular, unevenly spaced spiky projections. Which mechanism best explains his anemia?
HON-ANM-MCQ-32.a: Free-cholesterol-rich lipoproteins load the red cell membrane with cholesterol in excess of phospholipid, producing rigid acanthocytes that are destroyed in the enlarged spleen
HON-ANM-MCQ-32.p: Cholesterol > phospholipid + ม้ามโต = spur cell · cholesterol = phospholipid = target cell

HON-ANM-MCQ-33.s: A 47-year-old man drinks about 10 standard drinks daily. He is asymptomatic. Hb 12.6 g/dL, MCV 106 fL, WBC 6,400/µL, platelets 110,000/µL, reticulocytes 1.1%. GGT 210 U/L. Serum B12 and red-cell folate are normal and TSH is normal. The smear shows round macrocytes without hypersegmented neutrophils. Which is the most likely explanation and expected course?
HON-ANM-MCQ-33.a: Direct toxicity of ethanol on erythroid precursors and their membranes; MCV normalises over about 2–4 months of abstinence
HON-ANM-MCQ-33.p: MCV 100–110 + GGT สูง + round macrocyte = สุรา · หยุดดื่ม 2–4 เดือนกลับปกติ

HON-ANM-MCQ-34.s: A 44-year-old woman has fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation and weight gain. Hb 10.6 g/dL, MCV 96 fL, reticulocytes 0.5%, ferritin 85 ng/mL, B12 and folate normal, LDH and bilirubin normal. TSH is 48 mU/L with low free T4. Which mechanism best explains her anemia?
HON-ANM-MCQ-34.a: Reduced tissue oxygen demand lowering erythropoietin production, together with loss of the direct stimulatory effect of thyroid hormone on erythroid progenitors
HON-ANM-MCQ-34.p: Hypothyroid = ซีดแบบ demand ลด → EPO ลด · normocytic retic ต่ำ

HON-ANM-MCQ-40.s: An 8-year-old boy has intermittent jaundice and splenomegaly. His father underwent splenectomy as a teenager. Hb 9.8 g/dL, MCV 82 fL, MCHC 37.5 g/dL, reticulocytes 9%, indirect bilirubin 3.1 mg/dL, direct antiglobulin test negative. The smear shows many small dense cells lacking central pallor. Which mechanism best explains the shape of these cells?
HON-ANM-MCQ-40.a: Defective vertical linkage between the lipid bilayer and the spectrin skeleton with loss of membrane as microvesicles
HON-ANM-MCQ-40.p: HS = vertical defect → microvesicle → SA:V ↓ → spherocyte (DAT ลบ)

HON-ANM-MCQ-41.s: A 6-year-old girl with known hereditary spherocytosis (baseline Hb 10 g/dL, reticulocytes 8%) had fever, coryza and malaise 6 days ago. She is now very pale and tachycardic. Hb 4.6 g/dL, reticulocytes 0.2%, WBC and platelets normal, indirect bilirubin lower than her usual level, spleen size unchanged. What is the most likely cause?
HON-ANM-MCQ-41.a: Parvovirus B19 infection of erythroid progenitors
HON-ANM-MCQ-41.p: ซีดฮวบ + retic ~0 ในโรค hemolysis เรื้อรัง = parvovirus B19

HON-ANM-MCQ-42.s: A 7-year-old boy with severe hereditary spherocytosis requires transfusion every 6–8 weeks and is scheduled for elective laparoscopic total splenectomy. Which statement is most appropriate?
HON-ANM-MCQ-42.a: Give pneumococcal, Hib and meningococcal vaccines at least 2 weeks before surgery; spherocytes persist but red-cell survival improves
HON-ANM-MCQ-42.p: Splenectomy ใน HS: spherocyte ยังอยู่ แต่ RBC อายุยืน · วัคซีนก่อน 2 สัปดาห์

HON-ANM-MCQ-43.s: A 24-year-old Thai man is treated with chloroquine and primaquine for Plasmodium vivax malaria. On day 3 he develops dark cola-colored urine and back pain. Hb falls from 14 to 8.9 g/dL; LDH is markedly elevated, haptoglobin undetectable, DAT negative, and the smear shows bite and blister cells. Deficient production of which molecule in his red cells is the primary problem?
HON-ANM-MCQ-43.p: G6PD ↓ → NADPH ↓ → GSH ↓ → Heinz body/bite cell

HON-ANM-MCQ-44.s: A 30-year-old Thai man develops dark urine and jaundice 2 days after starting co-trimoxazole for pneumonia. On day 6 his Hb is 7.8 g/dL, reticulocytes 12%, DAT negative, and the smear shows bite cells. A quantitative G6PD assay sent that day returns at the lower limit of normal. What is the most appropriate next step regarding the diagnosis?
HON-ANM-MCQ-44.a: Repeat the quantitative G6PD assay about 2–3 months after recovery
HON-ANM-MCQ-44.p: G6PD ตรวจขณะแตก/retic สูง → ปกติเทียม → ตรวจซ้ำ 2–3 เดือน

HON-ANM-MCQ-45.s: A 45-year-old Thai man with newly diagnosed Burkitt lymphoma is about to start chemotherapy. Uric acid is 11 mg/dL and creatinine is rising. He has a documented history of G6PD deficiency. Which urate-lowering approach must be avoided, and why?
HON-ANM-MCQ-45.a: Rasburicase — it converts uric acid to allantoin and generates hydrogen peroxide
HON-ANM-MCQ-45.p: G6PD พร่อง: ห้าม rasburicase (สร้าง H₂O₂) · methylene blue ใช้ไม่ได้

HON-ANM-MCQ-46.s: A 19-year-old man has had chronic hemolytic anemia since infancy and required exchange transfusion as a neonate. He plays football without dyspnea. Hb 7.4 g/dL, MCV 96 fL, MCHC 33 g/dL, reticulocytes 8%, indirect bilirubin 2.8 mg/dL, DAT negative, EMA binding and osmotic fragility normal. The smear shows occasional echinocytes without spherocytes or bite cells. His parents are hematologically normal. Which mechanism best explains why he tolerates this degree of anemia?
HON-ANM-MCQ-46.a: Accumulation of 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate proximal to the enzyme block, lowering hemoglobin oxygen affinity
HON-ANM-MCQ-46.p: PK def: สารคั่งต้นน้ำ → 2,3-BPG ↑ → right shift → ทนซีดดี

HON-ANM-MCQ-47.s: A 12-year-old girl with pyruvate kinase deficiency (compound heterozygous PKLR variants) required transfusions every 5 weeks and underwent splenectomy. Three months later she has not needed transfusion; Hb is 9.3 g/dL (previously 7.0 g/dL before transfusions), but reticulocytes have risen from 12% before surgery to 48%. Bilirubin is unchanged, platelets 610,000/µL, and the smear shows Howell-Jolly bodies and prominent echinocytes. What is the best interpretation?
HON-ANM-MCQ-47.a: An expected finding because PK-deficient reticulocytes are no longer trapped and destroyed in the hypoxic spleen
HON-ANM-MCQ-47.p: PK def หลังตัดม้าม: retic พุ่ง 40–70% = คาดได้ (retic เคยถูกม้ามกิน)

HON-ANM-MCQ-48.s: A 28-year-old man with pyruvate kinase deficiency, compound heterozygous for two missense PKLR variants, has Hb 8.2 g/dL, reticulocytes 10%, and ferritin 1,150 ng/mL despite only occasional transfusions. He is started on mitapivat 5 mg twice daily with planned titration. Which statement best describes this drug?
HON-ANM-MCQ-48.a: It allosterically activates the mutant red-cell PK tetramer, raising ATP and lowering 2,3-BPG, and should not be stopped abruptly
HON-ANM-MCQ-48.p: Mitapivat: PK activator → ATP ↑ 2,3-BPG ↓ · missense ≥ 1 allele · ห้ามหยุดทันที

HON-ANM-MCQ-50.s: A 9-year-old boy with homozygous HbSS disease, whose family recently moved to Thailand from Nigeria, has had five hospital admissions for vaso-occlusive pain crises and one episode of acute chest syndrome in the past year. His hemoglobin is 7.6 g/dL, MCV 84 fL, reticulocytes 12%, and HbF 6%. He is started on hydroxyurea, escalated to 25 mg/kg/day. Six months later his crises have markedly decreased, his MCV is 104 fL and HbF is 21%. Which mechanism best explains the main clinical benefit of this drug?
HON-ANM-MCQ-50.a: Increasing γ-globin synthesis so that HbF, which does not copolymerize with deoxy-HbS, dilutes HbS and prolongs the delay time to polymerization
HON-ANM-MCQ-50.p: Hydroxyurea → HbF ↑ (MCV ↑ ใช้ดู adherence) · ปรับขนาดถึง ≤ 35 mg/kg/วัน โดยคุม ANC ≥ 2,000

HON-ANM-MCQ-51.s: A 7-year-old girl with HbSS disease is brought in with 2 days of profound fatigue and pallor. One week earlier she had a low-grade fever and her younger brother now has bright red cheeks and a lacy rash. Her baseline hemoglobin is 8.0 g/dL. Today: Hb 3.9 g/dL, MCV 86 fL, reticulocytes 0.2%, WBC 9,800/µL, platelets 310,000/µL. The spleen is not palpable; the smear shows sickle cells and Howell–Jolly bodies but no polychromasia. Which mechanism best explains her sudden fall in hemoglobin?
HON-ANM-MCQ-51.a: Lytic infection of erythroid progenitors entering through the P antigen, halting red cell production while red cell survival remains short
HON-ANM-MCQ-51.p: Hb ตก + retic ~0 = parvovirus B19 · Hb ตก + ม้ามโต + retic สูง = sequestration

HON-ANM-MCQ-52.s: A 26-year-old man with HbSS disease has few pain crises but develops a recurrent painful erection lasting 5 hours, a chronic ulcer over the medial malleolus, and progressive exertional dyspnea. Echocardiography shows an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 48 mmHg with tricuspid regurgitant velocity 3.1 m/s. Labs: Hb 6.8 g/dL, reticulocytes 15%, LDH 1,150 U/L, indirect bilirubin 4.1 mg/dL, haptoglobin undetectable. Which mechanism best links his hemolysis to these complications?
HON-ANM-MCQ-52.a: Consumption of nitric oxide by cell-free plasma hemoglobin together with arginase-mediated depletion of L-arginine
HON-ANM-MCQ-52.p: LDH สูง + PH/priapism/leg ulcer = hemolysis–NO axis · VOC/ACS/AVN = viscosity–vaso-occlusion axis

HON-ANM-MCQ-53.s: A 34-year-old Thai man presents with 3 weeks of abdominal distension and right upper quadrant pain. Doppler ultrasound shows occlusion of the hepatic veins with ascites. He has noticed intermittently dark urine. Hb 8.4 g/dL, MCV 98 fL, reticulocytes 4.5%, WBC 3,100/µL, platelets 92,000/µL, LDH 1,860 U/L, haptoglobin < 10 mg/dL, direct antiglobulin test negative. Urinalysis shows dipstick blood 3+ with 0–1 RBC/HPF. Which test is most appropriate to establish the underlying diagnosis?
HON-ANM-MCQ-53.a: Flow cytometry for FLAER and CD24 on granulocytes and CD59 on red cells
HON-ANM-MCQ-53.p: Budd–Chiari + hemolysis DAT ลบ + cytopenia → flow FLAER (ไม่ใช่ Ham test)

HON-ANM-MCQ-54.s: A 29-year-old woman is evaluated for fatigue, episodic dysphagia, and reddish-brown urine that is most noticeable on waking. Hb 7.9 g/dL, reticulocytes 6%, LDH 2,300 U/L, indirect bilirubin 2.6 mg/dL, haptoglobin undetectable, DAT negative. Urine hemosiderin is positive. Flow cytometry shows 68% of granulocytes lack GPI-anchored proteins. Which molecular event most directly causes lysis of her red cells?
HON-ANM-MCQ-54.a: Failure to inhibit polymerization of C9 on C5b-8, so that the membrane attack complex forms on cells lacking CD59
HON-ANM-MCQ-54.p: CD59 (MIRL) หาย → MAC ประกอบได้ = ขั้นที่ทำให้ PNH RBC แตก

HON-ANM-MCQ-55.s: A 41-year-old man with PNH has transfusion-dependent hemolysis (LDH 2,900 U/L) and a prior cerebral venous sinus thrombosis. The hematologist plans to start ravulizumab. He has not received any vaccines in adulthood. Which step is most important before the first dose?
HON-ANM-MCQ-55.a: Give meningococcal vaccines (MenACWY and MenB) at least 2 weeks beforehand, or cover with antibiotic prophylaxis until 2 weeks after vaccination
HON-ANM-MCQ-55.p: Anti-C5 = ไม่มี MAC = เสี่ยง Neisseria → วัคซีน ACWY + B ≥ 2 สัปดาห์ก่อนเริ่มยา

HON-ANM-MCQ-60.s: A 29-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus presents with 10 days of fatigue and yellow eyes. The spleen tip is palpable. Hb 6.9 g/dL, MCV 99 fL, MCHC 37.5 g/dL, reticulocytes 11%, LDH 690 U/L, indirect bilirubin 3.4 mg/dL, haptoglobin < 10 mg/dL. Urinalysis shows no hemoglobin. The smear shows many small, dense, round red cells without central pallor and polychromasia. Direct antiglobulin test: anti-IgG positive, anti-C3d negative. Which process best explains the red cell destruction?
HON-ANM-MCQ-60.a: Fcγ receptor–mediated partial phagocytosis by splenic macrophages that converts IgG-coated cells into spherocytes
HON-ANM-MCQ-60.p: Spherocyte + DAT IgG บวก = ม้ามกัดเยื่อ RBC ทีละคำผ่าน FcγR

HON-ANM-MCQ-61.s: A 58-year-old man with newly diagnosed warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia has Hb 4.6 g/dL, heart rate 128/min, chest tightness and new ST depression on ECG. Intravenous methylprednisolone has been started. The blood bank reports that his serum reacts with every donor unit tested and with all panel cells; autoadsorption to exclude alloantibodies will take several hours. He has never been transfused or had surgery. What is the most appropriate next step regarding transfusion?
HON-ANM-MCQ-61.a: Transfuse ABO/RhD-matched, least-incompatible red cells slowly with close monitoring now
HON-ANM-MCQ-61.p: Warm AIHA ที่ซีดจนอันตราย: ให้ least-incompatible ABO/RhD-matched blood ได้ — อย่ารอ crossmatch

HON-ANM-MCQ-62.s: A 67-year-old man with chronic lymphocytic leukemia developed warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (DAT IgG+). He responded to prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day, but hemolysis recurred twice whenever the dose was tapered below 15 mg/day. He takes folic acid. HBsAg and anti-HBc are negative. Which is the most appropriate next therapy?
HON-ANM-MCQ-62.p: Warm AIHA ที่ดื้อหรือพึ่ง steroid → rituximab (เช็ก HBV ก่อน)

HON-ANM-MCQ-63.s: A 72-year-old woman reports purple, numb fingertips and ear tips every time she enters an air-conditioned room. Automated CBC at room temperature: RBC 1.62 × 10^6/µL, Hb 9.6 g/dL, Hct 21%, MCV 130 fL, MCHC 45.7 g/dL. After the sample is incubated at 37 °C for 30 minutes and rerun: RBC 2.95 × 10^6/µL, Hb 9.6 g/dL, Hct 28.6%, MCV 97 fL, MCHC 33.6 g/dL. Which best explains the first set of results?
HON-ANM-MCQ-63.a: IgM-mediated red cell clumping that the analyzer counts as single large cells
HON-ANM-MCQ-63.p: MCV สูง + MCHC สูงเกินจริง + ดีขึ้นเมื่ออุ่น 37 °C = cold agglutinin

HON-ANM-MCQ-64.s: A 21-year-old college student has had a dry cough, low-grade fever and headache for 2 weeks. Chest radiograph shows patchy bilateral interstitial infiltrates. He now has fatigue and mild jaundice. Hb 8.8 g/dL, reticulocytes 7%, LDH 520 U/L, haptoglobin undetectable. The smear shows red cell clumps that disperse when the slide is warmed. Which direct antiglobulin test result is most likely?
HON-ANM-MCQ-64.p: Mycoplasma → anti-I IgM → DAT C3d อย่างเดียว

HON-ANM-MCQ-65.s: A 70-year-old man with primary cold agglutinin disease (monoclonal IgM-kappa, DAT C3d positive, IgG negative) remains transfusion-dependent despite strict cold avoidance. A trial of high-dose prednisolone was ineffective. He is offered a monoclonal antibody that rapidly reduces both extravascular hemolysis in the liver and intravascular hemolysis. Which target best achieves this?
HON-ANM-MCQ-65.a: C1s of the classical complement pathway
HON-ANM-MCQ-65.p: CAD: ปิด C1s = ตัดทั้ง C3b (ตับ) และ MAC · ปิด C5 ได้แค่ครึ่งเดียว

HON-ANM-MCQ-66.s: A 54-year-old diabetic rice farmer is admitted with fever, hypotension and multiple liver and splenic abscesses; blood cultures grow Burkholderia pseudomallei. On day 2 he oozes from venipuncture and central line sites. Platelets 36 × 10^9/L (180 on admission), PT 21 s (control 12 s), aPTT 54 s (control 30 s), fibrinogen 0.8 g/L, D-dimer markedly elevated. The smear shows occasional schistocytes. Which event initiated this coagulopathy?
HON-ANM-MCQ-66.a: Cytokine-induced tissue factor expression on monocytes and endothelium generating thrombin systemically
HON-ANM-MCQ-66.p: Sepsis → cytokine → TF บน monocyte/endothelium = จุดชนวนของ DIC

HON-ANM-MCQ-67.s: A 63-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma has had three episodes of superficial thrombophlebitis in different limbs over 6 weeks and now has a right femoral deep vein thrombosis. He has no bleeding. Platelets 118 × 10^9/L, PT 12.8 s (control 12 s), aPTT 31 s, fibrinogen 4.6 g/L, D-dimer markedly elevated. Which statement best describes his condition and management?
HON-ANM-MCQ-67.a: Chronic compensated DIC; start low-molecular-weight heparin
HON-ANM-MCQ-67.p: Chronic DIC: PT/fibrinogen ปกติ + D-dimer สูง + ลิ่มเลือดย้ายที่ → LMWH

HON-ANM-MCQ-68.s: A 31-year-old woman at 35 weeks' gestation has a placental abruption with fetal demise. While awaiting delivery she has brisk vaginal bleeding and oozing from IV sites. Platelets 62 × 10^9/L, PT 19 s (control 12 s), aPTT 48 s, fibrinogen 0.7 g/L, D-dimer markedly elevated. She has received 4 units of fresh frozen plasma; repeat fibrinogen is 0.9 g/L and bleeding continues. In addition to expediting delivery, which is the most appropriate next blood product?
HON-ANM-MCQ-68.p: DIC ที่เลือดออก + fibrinogen < 1.5 g/L หลัง FFP → cryoprecipitate/fibrinogen concentrate

HON-ANM-MCQ-69.s: A 36-year-old woman presents with 2 days of headache, intermittent word-finding difficulty and petechiae on her legs. Temperature 37.2 °C. Hb 7.4 g/dL, reticulocytes 6.8%, platelets 11 × 10^9/L, many schistocytes, LDH 1,840 U/L, haptoglobin undetectable, DAT negative, PT 12.4 s, aPTT 30 s, fibrinogen 3.1 g/L, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL, troponin mildly elevated. Which molecular defect best explains her presentation?
HON-ANM-MCQ-69.a: Autoantibody-mediated loss of the protease that cleaves von Willebrand factor multimers
HON-ANM-MCQ-69.p: MAHA + plt < 30 + coagulation ปกติ + สมองเด่น = TTP (ADAMTS13 autoantibody)

HON-ANM-MCQ-70.s: A 41-year-old man has microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, platelets 9 × 10^9/L, LDH 2,100 U/L, normal PT/aPTT, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL and transient left arm weakness. His PLASMIC score is 7. A sample for ADAMTS13 activity has been drawn; the result will take 3 days. The team plans to insert a central venous catheter for plasma exchange. Which is the most appropriate plan?
HON-ANM-MCQ-70.a: Start daily plasma exchange with corticosteroids and caplacizumab now, without prophylactic platelet transfusion
HON-ANM-MCQ-70.p: PLASMIC สูง → TPE + steroid + caplacizumab ทันที ไม่รอผล · ไม่ให้เกล็ดเลือดป้องกัน

HON-ANM-MCQ-71.s: A patient with immune TTP receiving daily plasma exchange and corticosteroids is started on caplacizumab. Within 3 days the platelet count rises above 150 × 10^9/L, although ADAMTS13 activity is still < 5% and the anti-ADAMTS13 antibody remains detectable. He develops gum bleeding. Which mechanism explains both the rapid platelet recovery and the bleeding?
HON-ANM-MCQ-71.a: Blockade of the von Willebrand factor A1 domain, preventing binding to platelet glycoprotein Ib
HON-ANM-MCQ-71.p: Caplacizumab = anti-vWF A1 → หยุดลิ่มเร็ว แต่ antibody ยังอยู่ และเสี่ยงเลือดออกเยื่อบุ

HON-ANM-MCQ-72.s: A 4-year-old boy had abdominal cramps and bloody diarrhea without high fever 7 days after a family barbecue; the diarrhea is now improving. Today he is pale, puffy around the eyes and has passed little urine. Hb 7.1 g/dL, platelets 48 × 10^9/L, schistocytes on smear, LDH 1,250 U/L, DAT negative, creatinine 3.4 mg/dL, PT/aPTT normal. Stool PCR is positive for stx2. Through which mechanism does the toxin injure his glomeruli?
HON-ANM-MCQ-72.a: Binding of globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) and removal of an adenine from 28S ribosomal RNA, halting protein synthesis
HON-ANM-MCQ-72.p: Shiga toxin: B จับ Gb3 · A ตัด 28S rRNA (60S) → หยุดสร้างโปรตีน

HON-ANM-MCQ-73.s: A 6-year-old girl has had bloody diarrhea for 2 days after visiting a petting farm. She is afebrile and mildly dehydrated. Stool testing is positive for Shiga toxin; E. coli O157:H7 is isolated. Hb 12.2 g/dL, platelets 220 × 10^9/L, creatinine normal. Which management is most appropriate?
HON-ANM-MCQ-73.a: Intravenous isotonic fluids with daily CBC, smear and creatinine monitoring; avoid antibiotics and antimotility agents
HON-ANM-MCQ-73.p: STEC ยังไม่เกิด HUS: สารน้ำ + เฝ้าระวัง · ห้าม antibiotic และยาหยุดถ่าย

HON-ANM-MCQ-74.s: A 27-year-old woman develops oliguria 4 days after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. BP 168/102 mmHg. Hb 7.6 g/dL, platelets 74 × 10^9/L, schistocytes 4%, LDH 980 U/L, haptoglobin undetectable, DAT negative, creatinine 4.8 mg/dL, PT/aPTT normal, liver enzymes normal. ADAMTS13 activity 64%. Stool Shiga toxin PCR is negative. Serum C3 is low and C4 is normal. Laboratory abnormalities have worsened despite delivery 4 days ago. Which is the most appropriate treatment, together with which precaution?
HON-ANM-MCQ-74.a: Eculizumab, with meningococcal vaccination or antibiotic prophylaxis
HON-ANM-MCQ-74.p: TMA + AKI + ADAMTS13 > 10% + Stx ลบ → aHUS → eculizumab + วัคซีน meningococcus

HON-ANM-MCQ-75.s: A 24-year-old motorcyclist arrives 25 minutes after a crash with a closed midshaft femur fracture and a large thigh hematoma. HR 124/min, BP 104/86 mmHg, cool clammy skin, capillary refill 4 seconds. No IV fluid has been given yet. The point-of-care Hb is 14.1 g/dL (his baseline 14.5 g/dL). Which statement best explains this hemoglobin value?
HON-ANM-MCQ-75.a: Blood is lost as whole blood, so concentration is unchanged until interstitial fluid and administered fluids expand plasma volume over hours
HON-ANM-MCQ-75.p: Hb แรกรับปกติไม่ได้ตัดการเสียเลือดเฉียบพลัน — ดู HR, pulse pressure, perfusion

HON-ANM-MCQ-76.s: A 70-kg man with a stab wound to the abdomen is anxious and confused. HR 132/min, BP 84/62 mmHg, RR 34/min, urine output 10 mL over the last hour after bladder catheterization, base deficit −8 mmol/L. He takes no medications. Approximately how much blood has he lost?
HON-ANM-MCQ-76.p: SBP เริ่มตก = class III (30–40%, 1.5–2 L) — ความดันปกติไม่ได้แปลว่าเสียเลือดน้อย

HON-ANM-MCQ-77.s: A 52-year-old man with melena from a duodenal ulcer underwent successful endoscopic hemostasis 12 hours ago. He has no history of cardiovascular disease. He received 2 L of crystalloid and 1 unit of red cells. Now HR 88/min, BP 122/76 mmHg, no further melena, no chest pain or dyspnea. Hb is 7.6 g/dL (8.9 g/dL on admission). What is the most appropriate approach to red cell transfusion?
HON-ANM-MCQ-77.a: Withhold transfusion; transfuse if Hb falls below 7 g/dL or he becomes unstable or symptomatic
HON-ANM-MCQ-77.p: เลือดหยุด hemodynamics คงที่ → ให้เลือดเมื่อ Hb < 7 (โรคหัวใจ < 8)

HON-PBS-MCQ-01.s: A 34-year-old man has a routine pre-employment CBC. He has no bruising or bleeding and takes no medications. Hb 14.6 g/dL, WBC 7,200/µL, platelet count 38,000/µL (EDTA sample). On low-power (10x) scanning of the blood smear, large clumps of platelets are seen along the feathered edge; individual platelets in the monolayer appear normal in size. What is the most appropriate next step?
HON-PBS-MCQ-01.a: Repeat the platelet count from a sodium citrate (or heparin) tube and correct for dilution
HON-PBS-MCQ-01.p: เกล็ดเลือดต่ำโดยไม่มีอาการ → ดู feathered edge หา clump → นับซ้ำในหลอด citrate

HON-PBS-MCQ-02.s: A medical student examines a well-stained blood smear from a healthy volunteer whose CBC is entirely normal (MCV 88 fL, MCHC 33 g/dL). Near the very thin tail of the smear, he finds many round red cells that lack central pallor and appear distorted, and he proposes reporting 'spherocytes 3+'. Which is the best response?
HON-PBS-MCQ-02.a: Re-evaluate red cell morphology in the monolayer, where cells barely touch without overlapping and normally show central pallor
HON-PBS-MCQ-02.p: Spherocyte ที่เจอเฉพาะ feathered edge = artifact จนกว่าจะเห็นใน monolayer

HON-PBS-MCQ-03.s: A Wright-Giemsa-stained smear from an afebrile outpatient shows numerous dark blue-black granules of varying size lying on top of red cells and also scattered in the background between cells. When the fine focus is moved up and down, the granules appear refractile and sharpen in a different plane from the red cells. The CBC is normal. What is the most likely explanation and the appropriate action?
HON-PBS-MCQ-03.a: Stain precipitate; prepare and stain a fresh smear with filtered stain before interpreting
HON-PBS-MCQ-03.p: เม็ดสีที่อยู่ทั้งในและนอกเซลล์ และเรืองวาวคนละระนาบ = stain precipitate

HON-PBS-MCQ-04.s: A hematology resident reviews several smears and estimates the proportion of red cells showing each abnormality in the monolayer. According to the ICSH 2015 grading recommendations, which of the following reports is correct?
HON-PBS-MCQ-04.a: Target cells in 15% of red cells reported as '2+ (moderate)'
HON-PBS-MCQ-04.p: ICSH: ขนาด/สี 11–20% = 2+ · รูปร่างทั่วไป 5–20% = 2+ · schistocyte 1–2% = 2+

HON-PBS-MCQ-05.s: A 38-year-old woman with heavy menstrual periods reports fatigue. Hb 8.6 g/dL, MCV 64 fL, MCH 19 pg, RBC count 3.9 × 10⁶/µL, RDW 19.5%, platelet count 520,000/µL. The smear shows hypochromic microcytic red cells with marked anisocytosis, many elongated pencil-shaped cells and a few target cells. No basophilic stippling, spherocytes or polychromasia are seen. White cell morphology is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-05.p: เล็ก + จาง + RDW สูง + pencil cell + RBC count ต่ำ = IDA จนกว่าจะพิสูจน์ว่าไม่ใช่

HON-PBS-MCQ-06.s: A 45-year-old man with chronic occult gastrointestinal blood loss has microcytic, hypochromic anemia. His blood smear shows numerous elongated, cigar-shaped red cells with hypochromia, oriented randomly across the monolayer. Which mechanism best explains these elongated cells?
HON-PBS-MCQ-06.a: Iron deficiency weakens the membrane cytoskeleton, so cells become permanently elongated by mechanical stress during repeated microvascular transit
HON-PBS-MCQ-06.p: Pencil cell สีจาง = IDA · elliptocyte สีปกติ > 25% = HE · เซลล์ยาวเรียงขนาน = artifact

HON-PBS-MCQ-07.s: A 29-year-old woman with iron deficiency anemia (Hb 8.2 g/dL, MCV 66 fL, ferritin 4 ng/mL) started oral ferrous sulfate 10 days ago. A repeat smear now shows, in addition to the microcytic hypochromic cells, a distinct population of larger, normochromic cells and several larger bluish-grey cells without central pallor. What is the best interpretation?
HON-PBS-MCQ-07.a: An expected reticulocyte response to iron, producing a dimorphic picture of new well-hemoglobinized cells alongside the old microcytic cells
HON-PBS-MCQ-07.p: IDA + polychromasia = เลือดออกใหม่ หรือกำลังตอบสนองต่อเหล็ก

HON-PBS-MCQ-08.s: A 52-year-old woman with active rheumatoid arthritis and long-term NSAID use has Hb 9.0 g/dL, MCV 70 fL and RDW 18%. Her smear shows hypochromic microcytic cells with anisocytosis and some pencil cells. CRP is 45 mg/L. Ferritin 85 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 7%, and soluble transferrin receptor is elevated. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
HON-PBS-MCQ-08.a: True iron deficiency coexisting with inflammation; ferritin is falsely reassuring and the elevated sTfR supports iron deficiency
HON-PBS-MCQ-08.p: อักเสบอยู่ + ferritin 'ปกติ' + TSAT ต่ำ + sTfR สูง = ยังขาดเหล็กได้

HON-PBS-MCQ-09.s: A 24-year-old Thai woman at her first antenatal visit has Hb 11.2 g/dL, MCV 66 fL, MCH 21 pg, RBC count 6.0 × 10⁶/µL and RDW 13.8%. Her smear shows uniformly small, mildly hypochromic red cells with a few target cells; there are no pencil cells, spherocytes or polychromasia. Ferritin is 62 ng/mL. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
HON-PBS-MCQ-09.a: Hemoglobin analysis (HPLC or capillary electrophoresis) for HbA2/Hb E, with DNA testing for α-thalassemia 1 as indicated
HON-PBS-MCQ-09.p: Microcytosis + RBC count สูง + RDW ปกติ + ferritin ปกติ → Hb typing ± PCR α-thal 1

HON-PBS-MCQ-10.s: A 30-year-old Thai man has mild jaundice and splenomegaly. Hb 8.5 g/dL, MCV 60 fL, reticulocytes 5%. The smear shows moderate hypochromia, microcytosis and anisocytosis, with target cells, teardrop cells, schistocytes, occasional spherocytes and polychromasia. After incubation of his red cells with brilliant cresyl blue, many cells contain numerous evenly distributed blue inclusions giving a 'golf ball' appearance. What do these inclusions consist of?
HON-PBS-MCQ-10.a: Precipitated tetramers of excess β-globin chains (Hb H, β4)
HON-PBS-MCQ-10.p: Golf ball ใน BCB = Hb H (β4) — ไวใน Hb H disease ไม่ไวใน α-thal trait

HON-PBS-MCQ-11.s: A 19-year-old man with β-thalassemia/Hb E disease underwent splenectomy 1 year ago for hypersplenism. His Hb is 7.5 g/dL, WBC 18,000/µL (uncorrected analyzer count), platelet count 920,000/µL. The smear shows marked numbers of nucleated red cells (180 per 100 WBC), many red cells containing a single round dark purple inclusion, target cells and teardrop cells. What best explains these findings?
HON-PBS-MCQ-11.a: Loss of splenic filtration (removal of nucleated cells and nuclear remnants) and loss of the splenic platelet pool
HON-PBS-MCQ-11.p: ไม่มีม้าม = NRBC มาก + Howell-Jolly + platelet สูง · อย่าลืมแก้ WBC เมื่อ NRBC มาก

HON-PBS-MCQ-12.s: A 30-year-old Thai woman undergoes premarital screening. Hb 12.6 g/dL, MCV 79 fL, MCH 26 pg, RBC count 4.9 × 10⁶/µL. The smear shows mild hypochromia, a few target cells and basophilic stippling in some red cells; there are no spherocytes or polychromasia. Hemoglobin analysis shows Hb A with HbA2 2.6%, no Hb E, and a small Hb Constant Spring fraction of about 1%. Ferritin is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-12.a: Hb Constant Spring trait (or α-thalassemia 2/Hb CS)
HON-PBS-MCQ-12.p: Hb ปกติ + MCV เกือบปกติ + basophilic stippling + แถบ Hb CS เล็ก ๆ = Hb CS trait

HON-PBS-MCQ-13.s: A 26-year-old man from northeastern Thailand is found incidentally to have Hb 12.8 g/dL, MCV 66 fL and RBC count 6.1 × 10⁶/µL. His smear shows numerous target cells with mild microcytosis, no spherocytes and no polychromasia. Hemoglobin analysis shows about 90% Hb E. Which molecular mechanism explains why this variant produces a mild thalassemic (microcytic) phenotype?
HON-PBS-MCQ-13.a: The codon 26 (GAG→AAG) mutation activates a cryptic splice site, reducing correctly spliced βE mRNA and β-chain output
HON-PBS-MCQ-13.p: Hb E = cryptic splice site → β⁺-thal อ่อน ๆ → microcytosis + target cell เด่น

HON-PBS-MCQ-14.s: A 68-year-old woman presents with 3 months of fatigue and tingling of both feet. Hb 7.8 g/dL, MCV 118 fL, WBC 3,100/µL, platelet count 95,000/µL, reticulocytes 0.5%, LDH 2,400 U/L. The smear shows macrocytic red cells with many large oval, well-hemoglobinized cells, teardrop cells and occasional schistocytes, and a neutrophil with six nuclear lobes. What is the most appropriate next step?
HON-PBS-MCQ-14.a: Measure serum vitamin B12 and folate (with methylmalonic acid if B12 is borderline) before starting treatment
HON-PBS-MCQ-14.p: Megaloblastic smear → ตรวจ B12/folate ก่อนรักษา · อาการทางประสาท = คิดถึง B12

HON-PBS-MCQ-15.s: A 55-year-old man with chronic alcohol use and poor diet has an MCV of 108 fL. While performing a 100-cell differential on his smear, a technologist records the nuclear lobes of the neutrophils. Which finding meets the criterion for neutrophil hypersegmentation?
HON-PBS-MCQ-15.a: A single neutrophil with six lobes
HON-PBS-MCQ-15.p: 6 lobes ตัวเดียวพอ หรือ 5 lobes > 5% = hypersegmented

HON-PBS-MCQ-16.s: Two patients have an MCV of 112 fL. Patient A, who has chronic liver disease, has round macrocytes and target cells. Patient B, who has pernicious anemia, has large oval, fully hemoglobinized red cells (macro-ovalocytes). Which mechanism best explains the red cells of patient B?
HON-PBS-MCQ-16.a: Impaired DNA synthesis causes nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony; cytoplasmic maturation continues while cell divisions are skipped, producing large, fully hemoglobinized cells
HON-PBS-MCQ-16.p: Macro-ovalocyte = DNA ช้า cytoplasm ไม่รอ · round macrocyte = ไขมันในเยื่อเพิ่ม

HON-PBS-MCQ-17.s: A 22-year-old man presents with gum bleeding and petechiae for 2 weeks. He has no lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly. Hb 7.2 g/dL, MCV 99 fL, WBC 1,500/µL (neutrophils 20%, lymphocytes 78%), platelet count 9,000/µL, reticulocytes 0.2%. The smear shows normochromic red cells with occasional round macrocytes, no polychromasia, no nucleated red cells, no teardrop cells, no blasts and no dysplastic features. Vitamin B12 and folate are normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
HON-PBS-MCQ-17.a: Bone marrow aspiration and trephine biopsy to assess cellularity
HON-PBS-MCQ-17.p: Pancytopenia + smear 'ว่าง' ไม่มี blast/dysplasia/NRBC → trephine biopsy + PNH flow

HON-PBS-MCQ-18.s: A 60-year-old woman has pancytopenia (Hb 8.0 g/dL, WBC 2,400/µL, platelet count 40,000/µL). Aplastic anemia is being considered. Which additional finding on her blood smear would most strongly argue against aplastic anemia and point toward marrow infiltration or fibrosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-18.a: Nucleated red cells and immature myeloid cells together with teardrop cells
HON-PBS-MCQ-18.p: Pancytopenia + NRBC + teardrop + immature myeloid = myelophthisis/fibrosis ไม่ใช่ aplastic

HON-PBS-MCQ-19.s: A 35-year-old woman with newly diagnosed severe aplastic anemia has WBC 1,600/µL with 70% lymphocytes and 25% neutrophils. A student suggests that the lymphocyte predominance indicates a lymphoproliferative disorder. Which statement best explains the lymphocyte predominance?
HON-PBS-MCQ-19.a: Neutrophils have a short circulating lifespan and depend on continuous marrow production, whereas many lymphocytes are long-lived and recirculate; the percentage of lymphocytes rises although their absolute count is usually low
HON-PBS-MCQ-19.p: อ่าน differential เป็นค่าสัมบูรณ์ — relative lymphocytosis มักแปลว่า neutropenia

HON-PBS-MCQ-20.s: A 16-year-old boy has recurrent mild jaundice and splenomegaly. His father underwent splenectomy for 'anemia' in his twenties. Hb 10.2 g/dL, MCV 84 fL, MCHC 37.5 g/dL, reticulocytes 8%. The smear (read in the monolayer) shows many uniform, round, dense red cells lacking central pallor, with polychromasia and no agglutination. The direct antiglobulin test is negative. Which test best confirms the most likely diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-20.p: Spherocyte + DAT ลบ + MCHC > 36 + ประวัติครอบครัว → EMA binding test

HON-PBS-MCQ-21.s: A peripheral smear from a patient with an ankyrin gene mutation shows numerous small, dense, perfectly round red cells without central pallor. Which mechanism best explains this red cell shape?
HON-PBS-MCQ-21.a: Membrane vesiculation with loss of surface area relative to volume
HON-PBS-MCQ-21.p: HS: เยื่อหลุดเป็น vesicle → SA:V ลด → ทรงกลม

HON-PBS-MCQ-22.s: A 30-year-old woman from southern Thailand is found to have an abnormal smear during a pre-employment check-up. She is asymptomatic with Hb 12.8 g/dL. The smear shows many broad, egg-shaped macro-ovalocytes whose central pallor is a narrow slit; some cells have a transverse bar of hemoglobin dividing the pallor into two slits, resembling the Greek letter theta. White cells and platelets are normal. Which molecular defect is most likely?
HON-PBS-MCQ-22.p: Theta cell + stomatocytic ovalocyte = SAO (band 3, SLC4A1 27-bp deletion)

HON-PBS-MCQ-23.s: A 40-year-old man with a normal CBC (Hb 14.6 g/dL, MCV 88 fL, MCHC 33 g/dL, normal reticulocytes) has a smear report of 'elliptocytes'. On review, the oval cells are confined to one area near the feathered edge, and all of them are aligned parallel with their long axes pointing in the same direction. In the well-spread monolayer the red cells are normal discocytes. What is the best interpretation?
HON-PBS-MCQ-23.a: Artifact of smear preparation; no hemolysis work-up is needed
HON-PBS-MCQ-23.p: Elliptocyte ขนานกันทิศเดียว = artifact · HE จริงวางหลายทิศทั่วสไลด์

HON-PBS-MCQ-24.s: A 70-year-old man presents with fatigue and jaundice. Hb 6.9 g/dL, WBC 48,000/µL with 85% small mature-appearing lymphocytes, platelets 190,000/µL, reticulocytes 11%. The smear shows numerous smudge cells, many small dense round red cells of variable size lacking central pallor, polychromasia and occasional nucleated red cells; there is no red cell clumping. Which result of monospecific direct antiglobulin testing is most likely?
HON-PBS-MCQ-24.a: IgG positive, with or without C3d
HON-PBS-MCQ-24.p: CLL + microspherocyte → warm AIHA → monospecific DAT IgG+

HON-PBS-MCQ-25.s: A 68-year-old woman reports bluish discoloration of her fingertips and ears in cool weather. The automated CBC shows Hb 9.8 g/dL, RBC count 1.6 × 10^6/µL, MCV 128 fL and MCHC 44 g/dL. The smear shows irregular three-dimensional grape-like clusters of red cells throughout the film, with few spherocytes. What is the most appropriate next step to obtain accurate red cell indices?
HON-PBS-MCQ-25.a: Warm the sample to 37 °C and re-run the analysis
HON-PBS-MCQ-25.p: MCHC > 40 + ก้อน RBC → cold agglutinin → อุ่น 37 °C แล้วรันใหม่

HON-PBS-MCQ-26.s: A 66-year-old man has back pain, anemia (Hb 9.1 g/dL), serum calcium 11.8 mg/dL and total protein 10.2 g/dL with albumin 3.0 g/dL. In the thin monolayer area of his smear, many red cells are arranged in linear stacks resembling piles of coins. The stacks disperse when the patient's plasma is replaced with saline. Which mechanism best explains this finding?
HON-PBS-MCQ-26.a: High plasma proteins reducing repulsion between red cells
HON-PBS-MCQ-26.p: Rouleaux = แถวเหรียญจากโปรตีนพลาสมาสูง (myeloma) · หายด้วย saline · agglutination หายด้วยอุ่น 37 °C

HON-PBS-MCQ-27.s: A 24-year-old woman presents with fatigue, jaundice and petechiae on her legs. Hb 7.2 g/dL, reticulocytes 9%, WBC 7,800/µL, platelets 14,000/µL. The smear shows many microspherocytes of varying size with polychromasia, very few platelets with some large forms, and no schistocytes or red cell clumps. DAT is positive for IgG. PT and aPTT are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-27.p: AIHA (DAT+) + ITP = Evans syndrome · ต้องไม่มี schistocyte

HON-PBS-MCQ-28.s: A 6-year-old Thai boy develops pallor and dark cola-colored urine two days after chewing mothballs. Hb 6.5 g/dL, reticulocytes 4%, DAT negative. The smear shows red cells with semicircular 'bitten-out' defects, cells in which hemoglobin is pushed to one side leaving a clear membrane pouch, a few pale empty membrane shells, and polychromasia. Platelets are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-28.p: Oxidant + ปัสสาวะสีโค้ก + bite/blister/ghost cell + DAT ลบ = G6PD

HON-PBS-MCQ-29.s: A 25-year-old man develops acute hemolysis after starting primaquine. The Wright-stained smear shows bite and blister cells, but no intracellular inclusions are visible. The clinician wants to demonstrate the denatured hemoglobin inclusions responsible for these changes. Which stain should be requested?
HON-PBS-MCQ-29.a: Supravital stain (crystal violet or new methylene blue)
HON-PBS-MCQ-29.p: Heinz body ต้อง supravital stain · Wright เห็นแค่ bite/blister cell

HON-PBS-MCQ-30.s: During acute hemolysis in a G6PD-deficient patient, the smear shows many red cells with a smooth semicircular defect at one edge. Which mechanism best explains the formation of these cells?
HON-PBS-MCQ-30.a: Splenic macrophages pitting denatured-hemoglobin inclusions from the membrane
HON-PBS-MCQ-30.p: Bite cell = splenic pitting ของ Heinz body

HON-PBS-MCQ-31.s: A 9-year-old Thai boy is admitted with dengue infection and develops dark urine and a fall in Hb from 12.5 to 7.4 g/dL. On day 5 of hemolysis, reticulocytes are 10% and the smear shows blister cells, bite cells and marked polychromasia. DAT is negative. A quantitative G6PD assay sent that day is reported within the normal range. How should this result be interpreted?
HON-PBS-MCQ-31.a: Possibly falsely normal; repeat the assay 2–3 months after recovery
HON-PBS-MCQ-31.p: ตรวจ G6PD ตอน retic สูงหรือหลังให้เลือด → ปกติเทียม → ตรวจซ้ำ 2–3 เดือน

HON-PBS-MCQ-32.s: A 32-year-old woman presents with fever, confusion and petechiae. Hb 7.0 g/dL, platelets 11,000/µL, creatinine 1.3 mg/dL, LDH 1,450 U/L, haptoglobin undetectable, DAT negative.
