PT, aPTT and fibrinogen are normal. The smear shows 6% schistocytes including helmet cells and triangles, microspherocytes, polychromasia and very few platelets. Which test is most specific for the most likely diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-32.p: MAHA + เกล็ดเลือดต่ำ + coag ปกติ + อาการทางระบบประสาท → ADAMTS13

HON-PBS-MCQ-33.s: A 58-year-old man with Escherichia coli septic shock develops oozing from venipuncture sites. Platelets 38,000/µL, PT 24 s (control 12), aPTT 58 s (control 30), fibrinogen 85 mg/dL, D-dimer markedly elevated. The smear shows 3% schistocytes and polychromasia. Compared with thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, which feature best explains why his PT and aPTT are prolonged?
HON-PBS-MCQ-33.a: Systemic coagulation activation consuming clotting factors, with fibrinolysis
HON-PBS-MCQ-33.p: Schistocyte + PT/aPTT ยาว + fibrinogen ต่ำ = DIC · coag ปกติ = TMA

HON-PBS-MCQ-34.s: A 45-year-old woman with known immune thrombocytopenia has a platelet count of 42,000/µL. Hb 13.1 g/dL, LDH and haptoglobin are normal. On review of the smear, the technologist counts 1,000 red cells in the monolayer and finds 2 fragmented cells (0.2%); most oil-immersion fields contain no fragments. Large platelets are present. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
HON-PBS-MCQ-34.a: The fragment count is below the significant threshold and does not support MAHA
HON-PBS-MCQ-34.p: Schistocyte < 1% และไม่มี hemolysis → ไม่ใช่ MAHA

HON-PBS-MCQ-35.s: A 4-year-old girl develops bloody diarrhea followed 5 days later by oliguria. Hb 6.8 g/dL, platelets 35,000/µL, creatinine 3.4 mg/dL, DAT negative, PT/aPTT normal. The smear shows helmet cells, triangular red cell fragments, microspherocytes and polychromasia. Which mechanism best explains the red cell fragments?
HON-PBS-MCQ-35.a: Shearing of red cells by microthrombi in injured small vessels
HON-PBS-MCQ-35.p: Schistocyte = RBC ถูกตัดโดยลิ่มเล็กในหลอดเลือดฝอย (fibrin ใน DIC · platelet thrombi ใน TMA)

HON-PBS-MCQ-36.s: A 19-year-old university student has fever, severe sore throat with tonsillar exudate, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy and a palpable spleen for 8 days. WBC 15,200/µL with 62% lymphocytes; Hb and platelets are normal. The smear shows many large lymphocytes that vary considerably from cell to cell, with abundant blue cytoplasm that is deeper blue at the edges and wraps around adjacent red cells; nucleoli are indistinct. What is the most likely diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-36.a: Infectious mononucleosis due to Epstein–Barr virus
HON-PBS-MCQ-36.p: Pleomorphic large lymphocyte + skirt + ไข้ เจ็บคอ ม้ามโต = EBV IM

HON-PBS-MCQ-37.s: A 7-year-old child has fever and lymphocytosis. The smear contains many large mononuclear cells. Which additional smear feature most strongly favors reactive (variant) lymphocytes rather than leukemic blasts?
HON-PBS-MCQ-37.a: Heterogeneous cells whose abundant cytoplasm is indented by adjacent red cells
HON-PBS-MCQ-37.p: Reactive = หลากหน้าตา + skirt · blast = หน้าตาเดียว + ดัน RBC ออก + nucleoli ชัด

HON-PBS-MCQ-38.s: A 22-year-old man in Bangkok has had high fever, headache, retro-orbital pain and myalgia for 5 days. Today he feels weak; tourniquet test is positive. WBC 2,900/µL, platelets 48,000/µL, hematocrit 49% (baseline 41%). The smear shows 18% large lymphocytes with abundant blue cytoplasm, variable nuclear shapes and scalloping around red cells; no blasts are seen. Which test is most appropriate to confirm the cause of these smear findings?
HON-PBS-MCQ-38.a: Dengue NS1 antigen and dengue IgM
HON-PBS-MCQ-38.p: Variant lymphocyte + WBC ต่ำ เกล็ดเลือดต่ำ Hct ขึ้น → dengue → NS1/IgM

HON-PBS-MCQ-39.s: In a patient recovering from acute cytomegalovirus infection, many lymphocytes on the smear are enlarged with abundant, intensely basophilic (deep blue) cytoplasm. Which cellular change best accounts for the deep blue color of the cytoplasm?
HON-PBS-MCQ-39.a: Abundant ribosomal RNA in antigen-activated lymphocytes
HON-PBS-MCQ-39.p: ไซโทพลาซึมฟ้าเข้ม = RNA/ribosome มากจากเซลล์ที่ถูกกระตุ้น

HON-PBS-MCQ-40.s: A 58-year-old man presents with 3 weeks of fatigue and gum bleeding. CBC: Hb 7.6 g/dL, WBC 34,000/µL, platelets 22,000/µL. The peripheral smear shows normochromic normocytic red cells and numerous large blasts (about 2–3 times the size of a red cell) with fine, lacy chromatin, 2–4 prominent nucleoli, and a moderate amount of grayish-blue cytoplasm containing a few granules. Several blasts contain a thin, pink-red, rod-shaped cytoplasmic inclusion. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-40.p: Auer rod = myeloid เสมอ → AML (ไม่มีใน ALL)

HON-PBS-MCQ-41.s: A 32-year-old woman presents with gum bleeding and large ecchymoses. CBC: Hb 8.1 g/dL, WBC 2,800/µL, platelets 18,000/µL. The smear shows many abnormal cells with bilobed or kidney-shaped nuclei and cytoplasm densely packed with coarse purple-red granules; a few cells contain bundles of rod-shaped inclusions. Fragmented red cells are present. PT is 19 s (control 12 s), fibrinogen is 85 mg/dL, and D-dimer is markedly elevated. Bone marrow cytogenetics will take several days. What is the most appropriate next step?
HON-PBS-MCQ-41.a: Start all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) immediately together with platelet, cryoprecipitate and plasma support
HON-PBS-MCQ-41.p: สงสัย APL จาก smear + coagulopathy → ATRA ทันที ไม่รอผลยืนยัน

HON-PBS-MCQ-42.s: A 40-year-old man with newly diagnosed leukemia has a smear showing hypergranular abnormal promyelocytes, occasional cells with bundles of Auer rods, and scattered schistocytes. Flow cytometry: CD13+, CD33+, CD117+, MPO+, HLA-DR−, CD34−. Fibrinogen is very low and fibrin degradation products are very high, out of proportion to the degree of thrombocytopenia. Which mechanism best explains his bleeding tendency?
HON-PBS-MCQ-42.a: Release of tissue factor from leukemic granules plus annexin II–mediated plasmin generation causing consumptive coagulopathy with hyperfibrinolysis
HON-PBS-MCQ-42.p: APL bleeding = tissue factor (DIC) + annexin II (hyperfibrinolysis) → fibrinogen ต่ำมาก

HON-PBS-MCQ-43.s: A 4-year-old boy has 2 weeks of bone pain, pallor, and petechiae. CBC: Hb 6.9 g/dL, WBC 18,000/µL, platelets 25,000/µL. The smear shows many small to medium-sized blasts, mostly uniform, with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, scanty sky-blue agranular cytoplasm, indistinct nucleoli, and no Auer rods. Which test result would best confirm the most likely diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-43.a: Flow cytometry showing blasts positive for CD10, CD19, CD22, CD79a and TdT
HON-PBS-MCQ-43.p: Lymphoblast จาก smear ต้องยืนยันด้วย flow: B-ALL = CD10/CD19/CD22/CD79a + TdT

HON-PBS-MCQ-44.s: A 9-year-old boy presents with a rapidly enlarging abdominal mass. Serum LDH and uric acid are markedly elevated. The peripheral smear shows large, uniform blasts with distinct nucleoli and intensely deep-blue cytoplasm containing prominent, clear, punched-out vacuoles. Which genetic abnormality is most likely present in these cells?
HON-PBS-MCQ-44.a: t(8;14) involving MYC and the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus
HON-PBS-MCQ-44.p: Blast cytoplasm น้ำเงินเข้มมี vacuole = L3/Burkitt = MYC t(8;14) → ระวัง TLS

HON-PBS-MCQ-45.s: A 45-year-old man has early satiety and a spleen palpable 10 cm below the costal margin. CBC: Hb 10.5 g/dL, WBC 186,000/µL, platelets 640,000/µL. The smear shows granulocytes at every stage of maturation with myelocytes more numerous than metamyelocytes, blasts 2%, basophils 7%, eosinophils 5%, and giant hypogranular platelets. There is no toxic granulation. Which test is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-45.a: BCR::ABL1 detection by RT-PCR or FISH
HON-PBS-MCQ-45.p: CML ยืนยันด้วย BCR::ABL1 (RT-PCR/FISH) — smear แค่ชี้ทาง

HON-PBS-MCQ-46.s: A 70-year-old woman with severe community-acquired pneumonia has WBC 52,000/µL and platelets 380,000/µL. The smear shows mostly segmented neutrophils and bands, with some metamyelocytes and rare myelocytes. Neutrophils contain coarse dark cytoplasmic granules, pale-blue cytoplasmic inclusions near the edge of the cell, and small vacuoles. Basophils and eosinophils are not increased and no blasts are seen. What is the most likely explanation of the leukocytosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-46.p: Leukemoid: ระยะท้ายเด่น + toxic granulation/Döhle body · ไม่มี basophilia

HON-PBS-MCQ-47.s: While performing a differential count on a smear from a patient with chronic myeloid leukemia, a student sees a cell with a round to oval nucleus, condensed chromatin, and no visible nucleoli. The cytoplasm is moderately abundant, less basophilic than a blast, and filled with fine pinkish specific (secondary) granules. The nucleus shows no indentation. Which maturation stage is this cell?
HON-PBS-MCQ-47.p: ไม่มี nucleoli + specific granule + นิวเคลียสกลม = myelocyte

HON-PBS-MCQ-48.s: A 68-year-old man has an incidental finding on a routine CBC: WBC 42,000/µL with 88% lymphocytes, Hb 13.2 g/dL, platelets 190,000/µL. A CBC 4 months ago showed a similar lymphocytosis. He has small, painless cervical lymph nodes. The smear shows a uniform population of small lymphocytes with scant cytoplasm and coarsely clumped, block-like chromatin, together with many smudge cells. Which is the most appropriate next investigation to establish the diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-48.a: Flow cytometry of peripheral blood for CD5, CD19, CD20, CD23 and kappa/lambda light chains
HON-PBS-MCQ-48.p: สงสัย CLL → flow cytometry ของเลือด (CD5+/CD19+/CD23+ + light chain restriction)

HON-PBS-MCQ-49.s: A 72-year-old woman with known CLL (WBC 60,000/µL, previously Hb 12.8 g/dL) presents with 2 weeks of fatigue and dark urine. Hb is now 7.9 g/dL, MCV 102 fL, reticulocytes 9%, platelets 160,000/µL, LDH and indirect bilirubin are elevated. The smear shows numerous small lymphocytes, smudge cells, many spherocytes, and marked polychromasia. Which test is most important to perform next?
HON-PBS-MCQ-49.p: CLL + spherocyte + retic สูง → DAT (warm AIHA) ก่อนคิดว่าไขกระดูกถูกเบียด

HON-PBS-MCQ-50.s: A medical student reviewing the blood smear of a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukemia notices many irregular, purple, net-like nuclear remnants without any surrounding cytoplasm, scattered among intact small lymphocytes. Which statement best explains these structures?
HON-PBS-MCQ-50.a: They are leukemic lymphocytes that are mechanically fragile and rupture while the smear is being spread
HON-PBS-MCQ-50.p: Smudge cell = เซลล์ CLL เปราะ (vimentin น้อย) แตกตอนไถสไลด์ — artifact

HON-PBS-MCQ-51.s: A 66-year-old man with progressive low back pain and weight loss has Hb 8.4 g/dL, WBC 6,800/µL, platelets 62,000/µL, and a markedly elevated serum alkaline phosphatase. The smear shows numerous teardrop-shaped red cells, nucleated red cells, polychromasia, occasional myelocytes and metamyelocytes, and some giant platelets. Bone marrow aspiration yields no aspirate (dry tap). What is the most appropriate next diagnostic step?
HON-PBS-MCQ-51.a: Bone marrow trephine biopsy with reticulin stain and immunohistochemistry
HON-PBS-MCQ-51.p: Leukoerythroblastic + dry tap → trephine biopsy + reticulin + IHC

HON-PBS-MCQ-52.s: A 58-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer has anemia and thrombocytopenia. Her smear shows many red cells with a single elongated, tapered tail, together with nucleated red cells and immature granulocytes. Which mechanism best explains the formation of the tapered red cells?
HON-PBS-MCQ-52.a: Deformation of red cells squeezed through fibrotic, distorted marrow and through extramedullary hematopoietic sites such as the spleen
HON-PBS-MCQ-52.p: Teardrop = RBC ถูกบีบผ่านไขกระดูกที่เป็นพังผืด/ม้ามที่สร้างเลือดแทน

HON-PBS-MCQ-53.s: Five patients each have immature white cells on their peripheral smear. Which combination of smear findings most strongly suggests replacement of the bone marrow (myelophthisis) rather than a reactive or other neoplastic process?
HON-PBS-MCQ-53.a: Teardrop cells, nucleated red cells, myelocytes and metamyelocytes, with thrombocytopenia and giant platelets
HON-PBS-MCQ-53.p: Teardrop + NRBC + myelocyte + เกล็ดเลือดต่ำตัวใหญ่ = myelophthisis

HON-PBS-MCQ-54.s: A 71-year-old man presents with back pain and fatigue. Hb 8.6 g/dL (normocytic), calcium 12.1 mg/dL, creatinine 2.4 mg/dL, total protein 10.2 g/dL with albumin 3.0 g/dL, ESR 120 mm/h. In the thin monolayer area of the smear, the red cells are arranged in long linear stacks resembling piles of coins, and the background between cells appears hazy blue. Which mechanism best explains the red cell arrangement?
HON-PBS-MCQ-54.a: High concentration of monoclonal protein neutralizing the negative surface charge (zeta potential) that normally keeps red cells apart
HON-PBS-MCQ-54.p: Rouleaux = paraprotein ลบล้าง zeta potential → ESR สูง · อ่านใน monolayer

HON-PBS-MCQ-55.s: A 68-year-old woman has a CBC run on a cold winter morning showing an RBC count of 1.9 × 10^6/µL, Hb 10.8 g/dL, MCV 130 fL, and MCHC 44 g/dL. Her smear shows red cells forming irregular, three-dimensional grape-like clumps of varying size rather than linear stacks. When the sample is warmed to 37 °C and rerun, the RBC count and MCHC normalize. Which is the most likely explanation of the smear finding?
HON-PBS-MCQ-55.a: Red cell agglutination due to a cold agglutinin
HON-PBS-MCQ-55.p: Rouleaux = แถวเส้นตรง สลายด้วย saline · agglutination = ก้อนไม่เป็นระเบียบ หายเมื่ออุ่น (cold)

HON-PBS-MCQ-56.s: A 55-year-old man presents with fatigue, bone pain and acute kidney injury. CBC: Hb 7.8 g/dL, WBC 15,000/µL, platelets 48,000/µL. The smear shows prominent rouleaux and many circulating cells with eccentric round nuclei, clock-face chromatin, deep-blue cytoplasm and a perinuclear clear zone; some have a high N:C ratio with prominent nucleoli. These cells make up 28% of the differential count. Serum immunofixation shows IgG-kappa monoclonal protein. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
HON-PBS-MCQ-56.p: PCL = plasma cell ในเลือด > 5% หรือ > 2,000/µL · plasmablastic = aggressive

HON-PBS-MCQ-57.s: A 26-year-old woman has 1 week of petechiae on her legs and gum bleeding. CBC: Hb 12.9 g/dL, WBC 7,200/µL with a normal differential, platelets 11,000/µL. The smear shows normochromic normocytic red cells, no schistocytes, normal white cells, and very few platelets, most of which are large or giant; no platelet clumps are seen at the feathered edge. PT and aPTT are normal. Which mechanism best explains both the low count and the large platelet size?
HON-PBS-MCQ-57.a: Autoantibody-coated platelets cleared by splenic macrophages, with compensatory marrow release of young, larger platelets
HON-PBS-MCQ-57.p: ITP = antibody + ม้ามทำลาย → เกล็ดเลือดน้อยแต่ตัวใหญ่ (เกล็ดเลือดใหม่)

HON-PBS-MCQ-58.s: A 50-year-old man has a pre-operative CBC showing platelets 38,000/µL. He has no history of bleeding, no petechiae, and normal coagulation tests. Hb and WBC are normal. On the smear, platelets in the monolayer area are scarce, but large clumps of platelets are present at the feathered edge. What is the most appropriate next step?
HON-PBS-MCQ-58.a: Repeat the platelet count using a sodium citrate (or heparin) anticoagulated sample
HON-PBS-MCQ-58.p: เกล็ดเลือดต่ำแต่ไม่มีเลือดออก + ก้อนที่ feathered edge → ตรวจซ้ำด้วย citrate

HON-PBS-MCQ-59.s: A 6-year-old girl from rural northeastern Thailand presents with multiple bruises on her legs for 5 days, without trauma. She is otherwise well, with no hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy. CBC: Hb 11.8 g/dL, WBC 11,500/µL with 34% eosinophils, platelets 285,000/µL. PT and aPTT are normal. The smear shows normal red cells, morphologically normal eosinophils, and many pale gray platelets lacking the usual purple granules. Which is the most appropriate next step?
HON-PBS-MCQ-59.p: จ้ำเลือด + eosinophilia + เกล็ดเลือดปกติแต่ซีด/เทา = APDE → ตรวจอุจจาระหาพยาธิ

HON-PBS-MCQ-60.s: Two children present with easy bruising. Child A has platelets 9,000/µL with large platelets and a normal differential. Child B has platelets 310,000/µL, eosinophils 28%, and pale-staining gray platelets on the smear; platelet aggregation studies are abnormal. Which mechanism best explains the bleeding in Child B?
HON-PBS-MCQ-60.a: Acquired loss of platelet alpha and dense granules impairing secretion and aggregation
HON-PBS-MCQ-60.p: ITP = ปัญหาจำนวน · APDE = ปัญหาการทำงาน (granule หาย เกล็ดเลือดเทา)

HON-PBS-MCQ-70.s: A 58-year-old man has fatigue and bluish fingertips in cold weather, two weeks after a Mycoplasma pneumonia. The automated CBC reports Hb 8.9 g/dL, RBC 1.6 x 10^6/uL, MCV 118 fL, MCHC 42 g/dL. The peripheral smear prepared at room temperature shows many irregular, three-dimensional grape-like clusters of red cells rather than linear stacks; spherocytes are few. Which is the most appropriate next step?
HON-PBS-MCQ-70.a: Warm the specimen to 37 °C, repeat the CBC, and perform a monospecific DAT
HON-PBS-MCQ-70.p: MCHC > 40 g/dL + ก้อน RBC บน smear = cold agglutinin จนกว่าจะพิสูจน์ว่าไม่ใช่ → อุ่น 37 °C แล้วนับใหม่ + DAT (C3d)

HON-PBS-MCQ-71.s: A 24-year-old man presents with gum bleeding and fatigue for 3 weeks. CBC: Hb 7.2 g/dL, MCV 99 fL, WBC 1,800/uL (ANC 400/uL), platelets 12,000/uL; corrected reticulocyte count 0.2%. The smear shows normochromic red cells with a few round macrocytes, no polychromasia, no nucleated red cells, no teardrop cells, no schistocytes, few platelets, and mainly small mature lymphocytes; no blasts or dysplastic neutrophils are seen. Which diagnosis is most consistent with this smear?
HON-PBS-MCQ-71.p: Pancytopenia + smear "ว่าง" (ไม่มี polychromasia, NRBC, blast, dysplasia) + relative lymphocytosis = คิดถึง aplastic anemia → ยืนยันด้วย bone marrow biopsy

HON-PBS-MCQ-72.s: A 9-year-old girl has had fever for 5 days with myalgia. CBC: WBC 6,500/uL with 22% "atypical lymphocytes", platelets 45,000/uL, Hct 46%. The smear shows large lymphoid cells of varying size and shape; their abundant cytoplasm is deep blue at the edges and scallops around adjacent red cells, and the chromatin is coarse and smudged. Which smear feature most strongly favors a reactive process over acute leukemia?
HON-PBS-MCQ-72.a: Heterogeneity of the lymphoid cells within the same field (pleomorphism)
HON-PBS-MCQ-72.p: Reactive = หลากหลาย (pleomorphic) · Blast = เหมือนกันหมด (monomorphic) — ดูภาพรวมของทั้งประชากรเซลล์ ไม่ใช่เซลล์เดียว

DERM-D1-MCQ-01.s: A 25-year-old woman has a 2-day history of intensely itchy, pink, raised, flat-topped lesions 1–4 cm in size on the trunk and arms. Several lesions have a pale centre. She notices that each lesion disappears within a few hours while new ones appear elsewhere. There is no scale, crust, or vesicle. Which term best describes the primary lesion?
DERM-D1-MCQ-01.p: นูน + หายใน < 24 ชม. + ย้ายที่ = wheal

DERM-D1-MCQ-02.s: A 30-year-old man has a 3-cm, flat, non-palpable, sharply demarcated area of complete depigmentation on the dorsum of his left hand. There is no scale or change in skin texture, and sensation is normal. Which term best describes this primary lesion?
DERM-D1-MCQ-02.p: แบน > 1 cm = patch · แบน < 1 cm = macule

DERM-D1-MCQ-03.s: A 78-year-old bedridden woman has several tense, dome-shaped blisters 2–3 cm in diameter filled with clear fluid on the lower legs and trunk. Which term best describes these primary lesions, and at what level is the split most likely to be?
DERM-D1-MCQ-03.p: ตุ่มน้ำ > 1 cm = bulla · ตึง = แยกลึก (subepidermal)

DERM-D1-MCQ-04.s: A 45-year-old man with pemphigus vulgaris has several moist, red, shallow, denuded areas on the trunk where blisters had been. The base is glistening and does not extend into the dermis. When they heal, what is expected and what is the correct term for these lesions?
DERM-D1-MCQ-04.p: Erosion ไม่เป็นแผลเป็น · ulcer เป็นแผลเป็น

DERM-D1-MCQ-05.s: A 40-year-old man has itchy, flat-topped, violaceous papules on the wrists. On the flank, identical papules are arranged in a straight line exactly along a recent scratch mark. Which phenomenon is shown, and in which disease is it characteristic?
DERM-D1-MCQ-05.p: รอยโรคเดิมขึ้นตามรอยข่วน = Koebner (LP, psoriasis, vitiligo)

DERM-D1-MCQ-06.s: Three days after wearing new rubber boots, a 35-year-old man develops intensely itchy erythema on the dorsa of both feet with tiny clustered vesicles, oozing, and yellowish crusts. A skin biopsy is taken. Which histological finding is most characteristic of this stage?

DERM-D1-MCQ-07.s: Which of the following is classified as an exogenous eczema in the lecture?

DERM-D1-MCQ-08.s: A 48-year-old construction worker has a 2-year history of thick, dry, lichenified, fissured plaques on both palms that itch intensely. KOH examination is negative. Which topical regimen is most appropriate initially?
DERM-D1-MCQ-08.a: Clobetasol propionate 0.05% ointment twice daily for 2–3 weeks plus a greasy emollient
DERM-D1-MCQ-08.p: ผื่นหนาแห้งที่ฝ่ามือ = steroid แรง + ointment

DERM-D1-MCQ-09.s: A 32-year-old woman with atopic dermatitis has recurrent eczema of both upper eyelids. She has used a medium-potency steroid cream intermittently for a year and now has mild skin thinning. Which is the most appropriate long-term topical treatment?
DERM-D1-MCQ-09.a: Tacrolimus ointment twice daily, then twice weekly for maintenance
DERM-D1-MCQ-09.p: เปลือกตา/หน้า ระยะยาว = TCI

DERM-D1-MCQ-10.s: A 26-year-old man develops acute contact dermatitis on the forearm with weeping vesicles and serous exudate. Which initial local measure is most appropriate?
DERM-D1-MCQ-10.a: Cool saline wet compresses for 15–20 minutes followed by a mid-potency steroid cream
DERM-D1-MCQ-10.p: Acute ซึม = wet compress → cream

DERM-D1-MCQ-11.s: A 7-year-old boy has had a recurrent itchy rash since infancy. Examination shows lichenified, excoriated eczematous plaques in both antecubital and popliteal fossae. He has asthma, and his mother has allergic rhinitis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
DERM-D1-MCQ-11.p: ข้อพับ + เรื้อรัง + atopy = AD

DERM-D1-MCQ-12.s: A 5-year-old girl with known atopic dermatitis develops fever and a sudden painful eruption of clustered, monomorphic, punched-out erosions with haemorrhagic crusts over her eczematous cheeks and neck over 2 days. What is the most appropriate management?
DERM-D1-MCQ-12.p: AD + แผลตื้นกลมเป็นกลุ่ม + ไข้ = eczema herpeticum → acyclovir

DERM-D1-MCQ-13.s: A 9-year-old boy with atopic dermatitis has several ill-defined, slightly scaly, hypopigmented patches 1–2 cm on both cheeks that became more noticeable after a beach holiday. Sensation over the patches is normal and KOH is negative. What is the most appropriate treatment?
DERM-D1-MCQ-13.a: Low-potency topical corticosteroid, emollient and sunscreen
DERM-D1-MCQ-13.p: Pityriasis alba = steroid อ่อน + sunscreen · เช็คชาทุกผื่นซีด

DERM-D1-MCQ-14.s: A 68-year-old man with Parkinson disease has erythematous patches with greasy, yellowish scales on the scalp, eyebrows, glabella, and nasolabial folds. The rash worsens in winter and is mildly itchy. Which treatment is most appropriate?
DERM-D1-MCQ-14.a: Ketoconazole 2% shampoo and cream plus a short course of low-potency topical corticosteroid
DERM-D1-MCQ-14.p: Seb derm = antifungal + steroid อ่อน

DERM-D1-MCQ-15.s: A previously healthy 27-year-old man presents with a 1-month history of an extensive, severe eruption of greasy, scaly erythematous plaques on the face, scalp, chest and groin that has not responded to topical treatment. He also has oral thrush. Which investigation is most important next?
DERM-D1-MCQ-15.p: Seb derm รุนแรง + thrush ในคนหนุ่ม → ตรวจ HIV

DERM-D1-MCQ-16.s: A 70-year-old woman with long-standing varicose veins has itchy, scaly, erythematous plaques around both ankles and lower calves, with yellow-brown pigmentation, hair loss and shiny skin. Both legs are equally affected, are not warm, and she is afebrile. What is the most appropriate management?
DERM-D1-MCQ-16.a: Compression stockings with a mid-potency topical steroid and emollient
DERM-D1-MCQ-16.p: Stasis = compression + steroid + emollient · อย่าใช้ยาปฏิชีวนะทา

DERM-D1-MCQ-17.s: An 82-year-old man complains of itchy shins every winter. Examination shows dry skin on both anterior shins with a network of fine red fissures separating plates of scale, resembling cracked porcelain. He bathes twice daily with hot water and antibacterial soap. What is the best initial treatment?
DERM-D1-MCQ-17.a: Lukewarm short baths, mild soap substitute, liberal emollient after bathing and a mid-potency steroid ointment for a short period
DERM-D1-MCQ-17.p: Xerotic eczema = emollient + เลิกน้ำร้อน/สบู่แรง ± steroid ointment

DERM-D1-MCQ-18.s: A 66-year-old man has developed generalized dry, scaly, itchy skin over the past 4 months, despite regular emollient use. He has lost 6 kg, has night sweats, and is not taking any new medications. What is the most important next step?
DERM-D1-MCQ-18.a: Evaluate for lymphoma (CBC, lymph node examination, imaging as indicated)
DERM-D1-MCQ-18.p: Xerosis ทั้งตัว + B symptoms → หา lymphoma

DERM-D1-MCQ-19.s: A 45-year-old woman has a single, thick, hyperpigmented, scaly plaque with exaggerated skin markings on the nape of her neck. She admits rubbing it constantly when stressed at work. KOH is negative. Which management is most appropriate?
DERM-D1-MCQ-19.a: Potent topical corticosteroid under occlusion plus measures to stop rubbing (covering, habit reversal, sedating antihistamine at night)
DERM-D1-MCQ-19.p: LSC = steroid แรงทาปิด + หยุดถู

DERM-D1-MCQ-20.s: A 58-year-old man has a 1-year history of generalized itch and multiple firm, dome-shaped, hyperkeratotic, excoriated nodules 0.5–2 cm on the extensor arms and legs. He has no personal history of atopy. Which approach is most appropriate besides symptomatic treatment?
DERM-D1-MCQ-20.a: Screen for systemic causes of pruritus: CBC, renal and liver function, thyroid function, glucose, and HIV/hepatitis serology
DERM-D1-MCQ-20.p: Prurigo nodularis → หาสาเหตุคันทั้งตัว

DERM-D1-MCQ-21.s: A 22-year-old medical student with allergic rhinitis has recurrent episodes of intensely itchy, clear, deep-seated 1–2 mm vesicles along the sides of the fingers and on the palms, worse during exam periods and hot weather. KOH from the palm is negative. What is the most appropriate treatment?
DERM-D1-MCQ-21.a: Potent topical corticosteroid (e.g., clobetasol) for a short course with emollients and irritant avoidance

DERM-D1-MCQ-22.s: A 60-year-old man admitted with pneumonia has had high fever and profuse sweating for 3 days while lying supine. The nurse notices hundreds of tiny, clear, fragile, dew-drop-like vesicles on his back and chest without surrounding erythema or itch. What is the most appropriate management?
DERM-D1-MCQ-22.a: Reassure, keep the skin cool and dry, and change damp clothing — it resolves without specific treatment
DERM-D1-MCQ-22.p: ตุ่มใสหยดน้ำค้างไม่แดงหลังเหงื่อออก = miliaria crystallina → ทำให้เย็น

MOCK-060.s: 30yo man presents with intensely pruritic, deep-seated 'tapioca-like' vesicles along lateral fingers and palms recurrently during warm weather/stress. Diagnosis?

DERM-D1-MCQ-23.s: A 30-year-old man has a recurrent, itchy, scaly, hyperpigmented rectangular plaque just below the umbilicus. It flares 1–2 days after he wears a particular belt. Which mechanism and confirmatory test are correct?
DERM-D1-MCQ-23.a: Type IV (T-cell–mediated) hypersensitivity to nickel; patch test
DERM-D1-MCQ-23.p: ผื่นรูปวัตถุ + ขึ้นช้า 1–3 วัน = ACD → patch test

DERM-D1-MCQ-24.s: A 34-year-old hairdresser has had dry, fissured, scaly dermatitis of the backs of both hands and finger webs for 2 years. She washes hair many times daily without gloves. Her dermatitis improves on holidays. Despite gloves and emollients for 2 months, it persists. What is the most appropriate next step?
DERM-D1-MCQ-24.a: Patch testing to exclude coexisting allergic contact dermatitis
DERM-D1-MCQ-24.p: ICD เรื้อรังที่มือ → patch test ตัด ACD

MOCK-059.s: Nurse develops dry scaly erythematous patches and fissures on hands after frequent alcohol hand rub use. No lesions elsewhere. Diagnosis?

DERM-D1-MCQ-25.s: A 35-year-old woman develops generalized wheals and lip swelling 1 hour after taking ibuprofen for headache. She had a similar reaction to aspirin last year but tolerates paracetamol. Which mechanism best explains her reaction?
DERM-D1-MCQ-25.a: Cyclooxygenase-1 inhibition shifting arachidonic acid metabolism toward leukotrienes and activating mast cells, without specific IgE
DERM-D1-MCQ-25.p: ลมพิษกับ NSAID หลายตัว = COX-1 → leukotriene (non-allergic)

DERM-D1-MCQ-26.s: A 62-year-old man taking enalapril for 4 years presents with marked swelling of the lower lip and tongue that developed over several hours. There are no wheals and no itch. Blood pressure 138/84 mmHg, SpO2 97%, no stridor. What is the most important step in management?
DERM-D1-MCQ-26.a: Stop enalapril permanently and observe the airway closely
DERM-D1-MCQ-26.p: Angioedema ไม่มีลมพิษ + ACEi = bradykinin → หยุด ACEi

DERM-D1-MCQ-27.s: A 40-year-old woman has had recurrent itchy wheals almost daily for 4 months without an identifiable trigger. Which statement is correct?
DERM-D1-MCQ-27.a: This is chronic urticaria (≥ 6 weeks); most cases have no identifiable external cause
DERM-D1-MCQ-27.p: Chronic urticaria = ≥ 6 สัปดาห์ ส่วนใหญ่ idiopathic

DERM-D1-MCQ-28.s: A 29-year-old woman with chronic spontaneous urticaria for 5 months has persistent daily wheals despite taking cetirizine 10 mg once daily regularly for 4 weeks. There is no angioedema. According to the EAACI/GA²LEN/EuroGuiDerm/APAAACI 2022 guideline, what is the next step?
DERM-D1-MCQ-28.a: Increase cetirizine up to 4 times the standard dose (e.g., 10 mg up to four times daily)
DERM-D1-MCQ-28.p: sgAH ไม่คุม → เพิ่มถึง 4 เท่าก่อน

DERM-D1-MCQ-29.s: Ten minutes after eating shrimp, a 24-year-old man develops generalized wheals, swelling of the lips and tongue, hoarseness, wheeze, and a blood pressure of 78/40 mmHg. What is the most appropriate first drug and route?
DERM-D1-MCQ-29.a: Adrenaline (epinephrine) 1 mg/mL, 0.5 mg intramuscularly into the anterolateral thigh
DERM-D1-MCQ-29.p: Anaphylaxis = adrenaline 0.5 mg IM ต้นขา

DERM-D1-MCQ-30.s: A 24-year-old man presents with a 2-week history of a non-itchy rash. Examination shows scattered, symmetric, reddish-brown papules with fine scale on the trunk, and similar papules with a peripheral collarette of scale on both palms and soles. He has generalized, non-tender lymphadenopathy and recalls a painless penile sore 2 months ago that healed spontaneously. Which pair of tests is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?
DERM-D1-MCQ-30.a: A non-treponemal test (RPR/VDRL) and a treponemal test (TPHA/TPPA)
DERM-D1-MCQ-30.p: ผื่นฝ่ามือฝ่าเท้า + LN ทั่วตัว + แผลไม่เจ็บมาก่อน = secondary syphilis → RPR + TPHA

DERM-D1-MCQ-31.s: A 28-year-old man has a single, painless, clean-based, 1-cm penile ulcer with a firm, indurated (button-like) edge that appeared 10 days ago. He has bilateral, firm, non-tender inguinal lymph nodes. RPR is non-reactive. Which statement is correct?
DERM-D1-MCQ-31.a: RPR may be negative in early primary syphilis; confirm by darkfield/PCR and treat presumptively with benzathine penicillin
DERM-D1-MCQ-31.p: Chancre + RPR ลบ ≠ ไม่เป็นโรค (primary sens ~86%)

DERM-D1-MCQ-32.s: Four hours after receiving benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM for secondary syphilis, a 26-year-old woman (not pregnant) develops fever of 38.9 °C, chills, myalgia and a transient worsening of her rash. Blood pressure is 118/70 mmHg and there is no wheeze or urticaria. What is the most appropriate management?
DERM-D1-MCQ-32.a: Reassure, give antipyretics, and continue follow-up — this is the Jarisch–Herxheimer reaction
DERM-D1-MCQ-32.p: ไข้หลังฉีด BPG ใน 24 ชม. = Jarisch–Herxheimer → ยาลดไข้ ไม่ใช่แพ้ยา

DERM-D1-MCQ-33.s: A 32-year-old HIV-negative man was treated with a single dose of benzathine penicillin G for secondary syphilis when his RPR titre was 1:64. At 12 months his RPR is 1:32 and TPHA remains reactive. He has no neurological or ocular symptoms. What is the correct interpretation?
DERM-D1-MCQ-33.a: Inadequate serologic response — evaluate for reinfection, treatment failure or neurosyphilis (including CSF examination as indicated) and retreat
DERM-D1-MCQ-33.p: ติดตาม RPR: ต้องลด ≥ 4 เท่าใน 6–12 เดือน

DERM-D1-MCQ-34.s: A 25-year-old woman at 16 weeks of pregnancy is diagnosed with secondary syphilis. She reports a history of generalized urticaria and wheeze after amoxicillin. What is the most appropriate treatment?
DERM-D1-MCQ-34.a: Penicillin desensitization followed by benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM
DERM-D1-MCQ-34.p: ตั้งครรภ์ + แพ้ penicillin → desensitize แล้วให้ BPG

MOCK-008.s: A 30-year-old individual is diagnosed with early latent syphilis. The patient reports having had a single sexual partner within the past 60 days. The partner is currently asymptomatic and nonreactive on RPR screening. Which of the following is the most appropriate management for the sexual partner?
MOCK-008.a: Administer Benzathine Penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose immediately

DERM-D1-MCQ-35.s: A 30-year-old man returning from abroad has two painful, soft, 1.5-cm genital ulcers with ragged, undermined edges and a purulent grey base. He also has a unilateral, tender, fluctuant inguinal lymph node. Gram stain of the exudate shows Gram-negative coccobacilli in parallel chains. What is the most appropriate treatment?
DERM-D1-MCQ-35.a: Azithromycin 1 g orally once (or ceftriaxone 250 mg IM once) and needle aspiration of the fluctuant node
DERM-D1-MCQ-35.p: แผลเจ็บ นุ่ม เซาะใต้ + bubo เจ็บ = chancroid → azithro/ceftriaxone ครั้งเดียว

DERM-D1-MCQ-36.s: A 23-year-old man has a 3-day history of dysuria and profuse creamy purulent urethral discharge. Gram stain shows Gram-negative intracellular diplococci within neutrophils. Chlamydia testing is pending. According to current CDC (2021) recommendations, what is the most appropriate treatment?
DERM-D1-MCQ-36.a: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once plus doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days
DERM-D1-MCQ-36.p: GC ปัจจุบัน = ceftriaxone 500 mg IM ± doxycycline 7 วัน

DERM-D1-MCQ-37.s: A 27-year-old man has a 2-week history of a painful, unilateral swelling in the left groin. He recalls a small painless genital papule 4 weeks earlier that healed within days. Examination shows matted inguinal and femoral lymph nodes separated by the inguinal ligament, with overlying violaceous skin. Which organism and treatment are most appropriate?
DERM-D1-MCQ-37.a: Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1–L3; doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for at least 3 weeks
DERM-D1-MCQ-37.p: Groove sign + แผลแรกไม่เจ็บ = LGV → doxycycline ≥ 21 วัน

MOCK-016.s: A 19-year-old female presents with acute right knee pain, swelling, and fever. Physical examination reveals a warm, swollen right knee and two small necrotic pustules on an erythematous base on her forearm. Synovial fluid shows WBC 45,000/µL. Which of the following is the most likely pathogen?

DERM-D1-MCQ-38.s: A 35-year-old Thai farmer has three hypopigmented, dry, hairless patches with well-defined raised edges on the forearm and thigh. Sensation to light touch and temperature is absent within the patches. No peripheral nerve is enlarged or tender, and there is no motor or sensory deficit outside the patches. Slit-skin smear is negative. According to the WHO 2018 guideline, what is the treatment?
DERM-D1-MCQ-38.a: Rifampicin, dapsone and clofazimine for 6 months
DERM-D1-MCQ-38.p: WHO 2018: PB = R + D + C 6 เดือน · MB = 12 เดือน

DERM-D1-MCQ-39.s: A 40-year-old man with borderline tuberculoid leprosy started multidrug therapy 2 months ago. He now has redness and swelling of his existing skin patches, new pain along the ulnar nerve, and new weakness of the small muscles of the hand. He is afebrile. What is the most appropriate management?
DERM-D1-MCQ-39.a: Start oral prednisolone and continue multidrug therapy
DERM-D1-MCQ-39.p: Type 1 reaction = ผื่นเดิมบวม + neuritis → prednisolone + ให้ MDT ต่อ

DERM-D1-MCQ-40.s: A 45-year-old man presents with diffuse infiltration and thickening of the face and ear lobes, loss of the lateral eyebrows, and numerous symmetric, ill-defined papules and nodules on the trunk and limbs. Sensation over the lesions is largely preserved. Which finding is expected?
DERM-D1-MCQ-40.a: Slit-skin smear showing numerous acid-fast bacilli in clumps (globi)
DERM-D1-MCQ-40.p: LL = หน้าสิงโต คิ้วร่วง ผื่นสมมาตรมาก ไม่ชาระยะแรก · smear globi

DERM-D1-MCQ-41.s: A 22-year-old woman develops, over 24 hours, multiple round, raised lesions on the palms, backs of the hands and forearms, each with a dusky central blister, a pale oedematous ring and an outer red ring. She had a cold sore on the lip 10 days ago. There is mild lip erosion only, and she takes no medications. Which statement is correct?
DERM-D1-MCQ-41.a: This is erythema multiforme triggered by HSV; it does not progress to TEN, and recurrent cases can be prevented with antiviral prophylaxis
DERM-D1-MCQ-41.p: Typical target ปลายมือเท้า หลัง HSV = EM ไม่กลายเป็น TEN

DERM-D1-MCQ-42.s: A 30-year-old Thai man started carbamazepine for trigeminal neuralgia 16 days ago. He presents with fever, sore throat, burning eyes, painful oral and genital erosions, and dusky red, irregular macules with flat atypical targets on the trunk that are coalescing. Epidermal detachment involves about 20% of the body surface area and Nikolsky sign is positive. Which statement is most accurate?
DERM-D1-MCQ-42.a: This is SJS–TEN overlap; stop carbamazepine immediately, admit to an ICU/burn unit with ophthalmology input — HLA-B1502 screening before starting the drug could have prevented it
DERM-D1-MCQ-42.p: ยาใหม่ 4–28 วัน + dusky macule + เยื่อบุ + ลอก 10–30% = SJS–TEN overlap → หยุดยา

DERM-D1-MCQ-43.s: A 52-year-old man with TEN has, on day 1: heart rate 128/min, BSA detached 35%, serum urea 12 mmol/L, glucose 16 mmol/L, bicarbonate 22 mmol/L, and no history of cancer. What is his SCORTEN score?
DERM-D1-MCQ-43.p: SCORTEN: อายุ HR มะเร็ง BSA urea HCO3 glucose — ≥ 5 ตาย ~90%

DERM-D1-MCQ-44.s: A 32-year-old woman has a 1-week history of fever, bilateral ankle arthritis, and several tender, warm, red nodules 2–4 cm on both shins. Chest radiograph shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. Which statement is correct?
DERM-D1-MCQ-44.a: Löfgren syndrome (acute sarcoidosis); usually self-limited — rest and NSAIDs
DERM-D1-MCQ-44.p: EN + bilateral hilar LN + ข้อเท้าอักเสบ = Löfgren — NSAID

DERM-D1-MCQ-45.s: Why do erythema nodosum lesions typically resolve without ulceration or scarring, unlike erythema induratum?
DERM-D1-MCQ-45.a: Inflammation is confined to the fibrous septa of the subcutaneous fat without vasculitis or fat necrosis
DERM-D1-MCQ-45.p: EN = septal ไม่มี vasculitis → ไม่แตก

MOCK-058.s: 28yo woman taking OCPs presents with painful red subcutaneous nodules on anterior lower legs. Biopsy reveals septal panniculitis without vasculitis. Diagnosis?

DE-SI-MCQ-01.s: A 54-year-old man has a tender erythematous plaque on the shin. Which single bedside feature most reliably tells you the infection involves the deep dermis and subcutaneous fat rather than the upper dermis?
DE-SI-MCQ-01.a: An ill-defined border that fades gradually into normal skin
DE-SI-MCQ-01.p: คำถามแรกข้างเตียงคือ “ขอบคมหรือเบลอ” ไม่ใช่ “มีไข้หรือไม่”

DE-SI-MCQ-02.s: A diabetic patient develops a skin infection on the forearm with no history of trauma, and blood cultures grow the same organism. By the lecture's classification, this is best described as which pattern?
DE-SI-MCQ-02.a: Inside out — endogenous or haematogenous source
DE-SI-MCQ-02.p: ติดเชื้อผิวหนังที่ไม่มีทางเข้า ให้สงสัย inside out แล้วตามหา source

DE-SI-MCQ-03.s: A 6-year-old has several lesions around the mouth: thin-walled blisters that ruptured leaving erosions rimmed by honey-coloured crust. Which mechanism explains the blister?
DE-SI-MCQ-03.a: A staphylococcal exotoxin splitting desmosomal connections within the epidermis
DE-SI-MCQ-03.p: bullous impetigo = exotoxin แยกชั้น epidermis · อย่าสับสนกับ pemphigoid

DE-SI-MCQ-04.s: Which feature best distinguishes ecthyma from ordinary impetigo?
DE-SI-MCQ-04.a: It heals with scarring because the lesion extends below the epidermis
DE-SI-MCQ-04.p: ecthyma = ulcer + สะเก็ดหนา + ขาส่วนล่าง + เป็นแผลเป็น

DE-SI-MCQ-05.s: A 62-year-old woman has a bright red, tender, swollen plaque on the cheek with a sharply demarcated, palpably raised edge, plus fever and chills that began within hours. Which is the most likely diagnosis and its usual organism?
DE-SI-MCQ-05.p: ขอบคม + ยกขึ้น + ใบหน้า + ไข้เร็ว = erysipelas → penicillin

DE-SI-MCQ-06.s: A patient with a small infected wound on the dorsum of the hand now has tender red streaks running up the forearm toward the axilla, with fever. What does this finding indicate and what must be included in management?
DE-SI-MCQ-06.a: Lymphangitis — antibiotics plus treatment of the original wound
DE-SI-MCQ-06.p: เห็นเส้นแดงลากไปต่อมน้ำเหลือง = รักษาทั้งยาและแผลต้นทาง

DE-SI-MCQ-07.s: Which combination is the classic risk-factor triad for bacterial cellulitis given in the lecture?
DE-SI-MCQ-07.a: Skin barrier disruption, oedema, and venous insufficiency
DE-SI-MCQ-07.p: ผิวแตก + ขาบวม + venous insufficiency = ชุดเสี่ยงของ cellulitis แบคทีเรีย

DE-SI-MCQ-08.s: A 45-year-old aquarium hobbyist has a 3-week history of painful red-brown nodules on the dorsum of the right hand that have not responded to two courses of oral cephalexin. Which investigation is most likely to establish the diagnosis?
DE-SI-MCQ-08.a: Skin biopsy for acid-fast staining and mycobacterial culture
DE-SI-MCQ-08.p: ตู้ปลา + มือ + ดื้อยา = M. marinum → biopsy + AFB + culture

DE-SI-MCQ-09.s: Compared with bacterial cellulitis, which set of features best characterises tuberculous cellulitis in the lecture's table?
DE-SI-MCQ-09.a: Chronic course over weeks to months, usually afebrile, violaceous plaques that may form sinus tracts
DE-SI-MCQ-09.p: TB cellulitis: เรื้อรัง ไม่มีไข้ ม่วงคล้ำ และมี sinus tract

DE-SI-MCQ-10.s: A 29-year-old man has a 4 cm tender erythematous lump on the buttock with a soft, fluctuant centre. What is the single most important step in management?
DE-SI-MCQ-10.p: คลำได้นุ่มตรงกลาง = กรีดระบาย ยาเป็นของเสริม

DE-SI-MCQ-11.s: A 51-year-old woman with poorly controlled diabetes has three painful deep nodules on the shin over six weeks. They are firm, not fluctuant, and one has begun to drain serous fluid. Which next step fits the lecture's approach?
DE-SI-MCQ-11.a: Skin biopsy with culture and special stains for fungi and mycobacteria
DE-SI-MCQ-11.p: ก้อนลึกไม่ fluctuant + เรื้อรัง = biopsy อย่ากรีดและอย่าให้สเตียรอยด์

DE-SI-MCQ-12.s: Three days after using a poorly chlorinated hot tub, a woman develops itchy follicular pustules on the trunk and thighs, sparing areas covered tightly by her swimsuit edges. Which organism is most likely?
DE-SI-MCQ-12.p: แช่อ่างน้ำอุ่น + ตุ่มหนองตามรูขุมขน = Pseudomonas

DE-SI-MCQ-13.s: A furuncle on the thigh has become a 5 cm mass with several draining points. Which term and which management apply?
DE-SI-MCQ-13.a: Carbuncle — drainage of all loculations plus oral antibiotics
DE-SI-MCQ-13.p: หลายหัว = carbuncle = ระบายทุกช่อง + ยากิน

DE-SI-MCQ-14.s: A 58-year-old man with diabetes has 12 hours of rapidly worsening leg pain. He rates the pain 10/10, yet the overlying skin shows only mild erythema and slight swelling. He is febrile with a blood pressure of 92/54 mmHg. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
DE-SI-MCQ-14.a: Urgent surgical consultation for operative exploration
DE-SI-MCQ-14.p: ปวดไม่สมดุลกับผิว + สัญญาณชีพแย่ = โทรหาศัลยกรรม อย่าโทรหาห้องเอกซเรย์

DE-SI-MCQ-15.s: Which statement about the two types of necrotizing fasciitis is correct?
DE-SI-MCQ-15.a: Type I is polymicrobial, whereas Type II is due to Streptococcus pyogenes or MRSA
DE-SI-MCQ-15.p: Type I polymicrobial · Type II strep หรือ MRSA · ทั้งคู่ต้องเข้าห้องผ่าตัด

DE-SI-MCQ-16.s: A man who works in a tannery has a 1 cm ulcer with a black central eschar on the forearm, surrounded by marked oedema. Strikingly, the lesion is not painful. Which organism is most likely?
DE-SI-MCQ-16.p: แผลสะเก็ดดำที่ไม่เจ็บ + บวมมาก + สัมผัสสัตว์ = anthrax

DE-SI-MCQ-17.s: A 34-year-old man has well-defined reddish-brown patches with fine scale in both groins. Under a Wood lamp the patches fluoresce coral-red. Which treatment is appropriate?
DE-SI-MCQ-17.a: Topical clindamycin solution or oral erythromycin if widespread
DE-SI-MCQ-17.p: ซอกพับ + coral-red = แบคทีเรีย ให้ยาต้านแบคทีเรีย อย่าให้ยาฆ่าเชื้อรา

DE-SI-MCQ-18.s: A man complains of malodorous feet. On the weight-bearing areas of both soles there are multiple small crater-like depressions in the stratum corneum, with no erythema or scaling between the toes. Which organism and which first measure?
DE-SI-MCQ-18.a: Micrococcus sedentarius — keep the feet dry and treat hyperhidrosis
DE-SI-MCQ-18.p: หลุมที่ฝ่าเท้า + เหม็น + ไม่อักเสบ = pitted keratolysis → ทำให้แห้งก่อน

DE-SI-MCQ-19.s: An examination question describes: “diffuse erythematous oedematous plaques with ill-defined borders on the left shin, warm and tender, with fever.” Which diagnosis do these morphology terms point to?
DE-SI-MCQ-19.p: ill-defined + oedematous plaque = cellulitis แทบทุกครั้ง

DE-SI-MCQ-20.s: Which description should make you think of a surgical emergency rather than a simple skin infection?
DE-SI-MCQ-20.a: Hemorrhagic bullae with skin necrosis and crepitus
DE-SI-MCQ-20.p: เห็นคำว่า necrosis หรือ crepitus = หยุดคิดเรื่องยาแล้วโทรหาศัลยกรรม

DE-SI-MCQ-21.s: A 10-year-old has a painful keratotic lesion on the sole that hurts more when squeezed from the sides than when pressed directly, and shows tiny black dots on paring. Which HPV type is most characteristic, and what do the black dots represent?
DE-SI-MCQ-21.p: ฝ่าเท้า = HPV 1 · จุดดำ = หลอดเลือดอุดตัน ไม่ใช่เมลานิน

DE-SI-MCQ-22.s: Which histopathological finding is the hallmark of HPV infection?
DE-SI-MCQ-22.p: koilocyte = HPV · multinucleated giant cell = herpes · อย่าสลับกัน

DE-SI-MCQ-23.s: A healthy 9-year-old has two small common warts on a finger that do not bother him. His mother asks whether treatment is necessary. What does the lecture support?
DE-SI-MCQ-23.a: Observation is reasonable because warts in children are often self-limiting
DE-SI-MCQ-23.p: เด็ก หูดไม่กวน = สังเกตอาการได้ ไม่ต้องรีบจี้

DE-SI-MCQ-24.s: A 70-year-old man with chronic kidney disease receives intravenous acyclovir for severe herpes infection. Two days later he develops tremor and visual hallucinations, and his creatinine has risen. Which two measures directly address the mechanisms involved?
DE-SI-MCQ-24.a: Adequate hydration with infusion over more than one hour, and dose adjustment for renal function
DE-SI-MCQ-24.p: acyclovir IV: ให้น้ำพอ หยดช้ากว่า 1 ชม. และปรับขนาดตามไต

DE-SI-MCQ-25.s: A 25-year-old nurse develops painful grouped vesicles on the pulp of her index finger about a week after caring for a patient with oral ulcers. What is the diagnosis?
DE-SI-MCQ-25.p: ตุ่มน้ำเป็นกลุ่มที่ปลายนิ้วในบุคลากรการแพทย์ = herpetic whitlow

DE-SI-MCQ-26.s: A 68-year-old man has a painful unilateral vesicular rash over the right forehead and upper eyelid. There are also vesicles on the tip of his nose. Besides starting an antiviral, what is the single most important next step?
DE-SI-MCQ-26.p: ตุ่มที่ปลายจมูก = Hutchinson's sign = ส่งจักษุแพทย์ด่วน

DE-SI-MCQ-27.s: A 59-year-old woman has right facial droop that spares no part of the face, plus ear pain, vertigo, and vesicles in the right ear canal. Which treatment combination does the lecture recommend?
DE-SI-MCQ-27.a: Antiviral plus prednisone 60 mg daily for 5–7 days then taper
DE-SI-MCQ-27.p: หน้าเบี้ยว + ตุ่มในหู = Ramsay Hunt → ยาต้านไวรัส + prednisone ไม่ใช่อย่างใดอย่างเดียว

DE-SI-MCQ-28.s: Which feature of the varicella rash is most useful for distinguishing it from other vesicular eruptions?
DE-SI-MCQ-28.a: Lesions appear in crops and are at different stages at the same time
DE-SI-MCQ-28.p: สุกใส = หลายระยะพร้อมกัน · งูสวัด = dermatome เดียว

CARDIO-01-01-1.s: A 55-year-old man collapses in a shopping mall. He does not respond to shouting or tapping, has only occasional gasping breaths, and no carotid pulse is felt within 10 seconds. Help has been called and someone has gone to get an AED. What is the most appropriate next step?
CARDIO-01-01-1.p: Gasping ไม่ใช่การหายใจ — ไม่มี pulse ให้กดอกทันที

CARDIO-01-01-2.s: During adult CPR without an advanced airway, which combination best describes high-quality chest compressions?

CARDIO-01-01-3.s: A 60-year-old woman in cardiac arrest is receiving bystander CPR. An AED is attached and advises a shock. A shock is delivered. What should be done immediately afterwards?
CARDIO-01-01-3.a: Resume chest compressions for 2 minutes before reanalysing the rhythm
CARDIO-01-01-3.p: Shock → กดต่อทันที 2 นาที → ค่อยดู rhythm

CARDIO-01-02-1.s: A man with uncontrolled hypertension presents in cardiac arrest. CPR is in progress and he has already received three doses of adrenaline 1 mg IV. The monitor still shows pulseless ventricular tachycardia. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-01-02-1.p: เห็น VF/pVT เมื่อไร ต้อง shock ก่อนยาเสมอ

CARDIO-01-02-2.s: A 30-year-old farmer is struck by lightning. He is unresponsive and pulseless. CPR is started and the monitor shows asystole confirmed in two leads. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-01-02-2.a: Epinephrine 1 mg IV as soon as possible with continued CPR
CARDIO-01-02-2.p: Asystole/PEA → epinephrine ASAP + CPR ไม่ shock

CARDIO-01-02-3.s: A 58-year-old man has a cardiac arrest from acute myocardial infarction. During chest compressions the monitor shows an organised narrow-complex rhythm at 70/min, but no pulse can be palpated. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-01-02-3.p: EKG ดูดีแต่ไม่มี pulse = PEA → epinephrine

CARDIO-01-02-4.s: A 64-year-old woman in VF arrest has received three shocks with CPR, and one dose of epinephrine 1 mg IV. The rhythm remains VF after the third shock. Which antiarrhythmic regimen is most appropriate now?

CARDIO-01-03-1.s: A patient presents with palpitation without syncope, chest pain or dyspnea. BP 100/80 mmHg, pulse 160/min. EKG shows a regular narrow-QRS tachycardia with no visible P waves. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-01-03-1.p: Stable SVT เริ่มที่ vagal maneuver เสมอ

CARDIO-01-03-2.s: A man presents with palpitation and no chest pain. BT 37°C, BP 130/80 mmHg, pulse 150/min, RR 20/min. Physical examination is normal. EKG shows a regular narrow-complex tachycardia without visible P waves. Vagal maneuvers have failed. What is the first-line medication?

CARDIO-01-03-3.s: A 25-year-old woman has palpitation and near-syncope. BP 80/50 mmHg, HR 180/min. EKG shows a regular narrow-complex tachycardia. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-01-03-3.p: Unstable + มี pulse = synchronized cardioversion · ไม่มี pulse = defibrillation

CARDIO-01-03-4.s: A 60-year-old woman with DM, HT and dyslipidemia has chest tightness this morning. BT 37°C, BP 70/40 mmHg, PR 150/min, RR 28/min. She is drowsy with crepitation in both lungs and SpO2 88%. EKG shows a tachyarrhythmia with a pulse. After oxygen by mask with bag at 10 L/min, what is the most appropriate next step?
CARDIO-01-03-4.p: Tachy + shock + pulmonary edema → ไฟฟ้า ไม่ใช่ยา

CARDIO-01-03-5.s: A 28-year-old man has palpitation for 1 hour. BP 124/78 mmHg and he is alert. EKG shows an irregularly irregular wide-complex tachycardia at 210/min with varying QRS morphology and slurred upstrokes at the start of the QRS complexes. Which drug is most appropriate?
CARDIO-01-03-5.p: AF + WPW: ห้าม ABCD (adenosine, BB, CCB, digoxin)

CARDIO-01-04-1.s: A woman presents with intermittent palpitation. She is alert with normal blood pressure. Pulse 122/min, irregular. EKG confirms atrial fibrillation with a narrow QRS. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-01-04-1.p: Rate control AF: BB/non-DHP CCB (amlodipine ใช้ไม่ได้)

CARDIO-01-04-2.s: An adult comes for an annual check-up and has no chest pain or palpitation. Examination shows a totally irregular rhythm with a diastolic murmur at the apex. EKG shows fibrillatory waves with no P waves; heart rate is 84/min. Echocardiogram shows moderate mitral stenosis. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-01-04-2.p: AF + MS → warfarin เสมอ (ห้าม DOAC)

CARDIO-01-04-3.s: A 58-year-old woman with DM and HT presents with palpitation and acute chest pain. BP 90/60 mmHg, pulse totally irregular at 180/min, varying intensity of S1, and a grade 3/6 pansystolic murmur at the apex. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-01-04-3.p: AF + hypotension/chest pain = cardioversion ไม่ใช่ rate control

CARDIO-01-04-4.s: A 70-year-old woman with hypertension and type 2 diabetes is found to have persistent non-valvular atrial fibrillation. Heart rate is controlled with bisoprolol. She has no history of stroke, heart failure or vascular disease, and her creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min. What is the most appropriate antithrombotic therapy?
CARDIO-01-04-4.p: นับ CHA2DS2-VASc แล้ว ≥ 2 ในหญิง → DOAC/warfarin ไม่ใช่ aspirin

CARDIO-01-04-5.s: A 45-year-old woman with rheumatic heart disease has atrial fibrillation. Echocardiogram shows severe mitral stenosis with a mitral valve area of 0.9 cm2. Which anticoagulant is most appropriate?

CARDIO-01-05-1.s: A 70-year-old man has had dizziness and episodes of syncope on and off for 3 months. BP 130/70 mmHg, HR 70/min with dropped beats, RR 18/min. EKG shows sinus rhythm with intermittent absence of P waves; the long P-P intervals are not multiples of the basic P-P interval. What is the diagnosis?
CARDIO-01-05-1.p: P หาย = ปัญหาที่ SA node · P อยู่แต่ QRS หาย = AV block

CARDIO-01-05-2.s: A 50-year-old man presents with dyspnea on exertion and fatigue. BT 37°C, BP 90/60 mmHg, PR 30/min, RR 16/min. He looks fatigued. EKG shows a bradyarrhythmia. What is the most appropriate initial management?
CARDIO-01-05-2.p: Symptomatic bradycardia: atropine ก่อน แล้วค่อย pacing/infusion

CARDIO-01-05-3.s: A 75-year-old woman reports intermittent lightheadedness. BP 128/74 mmHg, alert, no chest pain. EKG shows a constant PR interval of 0.18 s with occasional non-conducted P waves that occur without preceding PR prolongation. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-01-05-3.p: Mobitz II แม้ stable ก็ต้อง pacing

CARDIO-01-05-4.s: A 68-year-old man on no medications has a rhythm strip showing progressive lengthening of the PR interval over three beats, followed by a P wave that is not conducted, after which the cycle repeats. What is the diagnosis?
CARDIO-01-05-4.a: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz type I (Wenckebach)
CARDIO-01-05-4.p: Wenckebach = PR ยาวขึ้นจนหลุด

CARDIO-01-05-5.s: A 72-year-old man presents with confusion. BP 70/40 mmHg, HR 32/min. EKG shows complete AV dissociation with wide QRS escape complexes. He has received atropine 1 mg IV three times without response. What is the most appropriate next step?
CARDIO-01-05-5.p: CHB unstable: atropine ไม่ได้ผล → pacing ทันที

CARDIO-02-01-1.s: A 45-year-old man has an early diastolic, high-pitched blowing murmur heard best at the left third intercostal space near the sternal border, with a wide pulse pressure. Which valvular lesion is most likely?
CARDIO-02-01-1.p: Diastolic blowing ที่ Erb's point = AR

CARDIO-02-01-2.s: A 22-year-old woman has a systolic ejection murmur at the left second intercostal space that radiates to the back, with a widely split second heart sound. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-02-01-2.p: PS = L 2nd ICS + wide split S2 + ร้าวหลัง

CARDIO-02-01-3.s: A 35-year-old man with a history of injection drug use has a holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border that becomes louder during inspiration, with prominent v waves in the jugular venous pulse. Which lesion is most likely?
CARDIO-02-01-3.p: Right-sided murmur ดังขึ้นตอนหายใจเข้า — TR ใน IVDU

CARDIO-02-02-1.s: A 75-year-old woman has dyspnea on exertion for 1 year with a history of syncope, orthopnea and PND. BP 150/80 mmHg, PR 72/min, alert, no neck vein engorgement. The carotid pulse has a delayed peak, decreased amplitude and gradual decline. There is a systolic ejection murmur at the right upper parasternal border radiating to the neck with a sustained apical heave. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-02-02-1.p: SEM ร้าวคอ + pulsus parvus et tardus = AS

CARDIO-02-02-2.s: A 77-year-old man with HT, DLP and DM presents with syncope. Lungs are clear and there is a grade III systolic ejection murmur at the left upper parasternal border radiating to the neck. Otherwise the examination is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-02-02-2.p: ผู้สูงอายุเป็นลม + SEM ร้าวคอ = AS (cardiac syncope)

CARDIO-02-02-3.s: A 60-year-old man has central chest pain and dizziness for 1 month, worse when climbing stairs and relieved by rest. BP 100/80 mmHg, PR 88/min, low-volume pulse, grade III/VI systolic ejection murmur at the 2nd right intercostal space radiating to the carotid artery, clear lungs. Echocardiogram confirms severe calcific aortic stenosis. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-02-02-3.p: Severe AS มีอาการ = เปลี่ยนลิ้น

CARDIO-02-02-4.s: A 58-year-old man with well-controlled HT and DLP complains of dyspnea. He has a carotid bruit and a grade III systolic ejection murmur at the right and left upper parasternal borders. Neurological examination is normal and the rest of the examination is unremarkable. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-02-02-4.p: Bruit ที่คอ + SEM ที่ base ของหัวใจ = นึกถึง AS ที่ร้าวขึ้นคอก่อน

CARDIO-02-03-1.s: A 30-year-old woman has gradual-onset dyspnea on exertion for 1 month without chest pain, cough or fever. BT 37.2°C, BP 120/80 mmHg, PR 80/min totally irregular, RR 20/min. Lungs are clear. There is RV heave 1+, no LV heave, loud S1, normal S2 and a grade III/VI diastolic rumbling murmur. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-02-03-1.p: Loud S1 + diastolic rumble + AF ในหญิงอายุน้อย = rheumatic MS

CARDIO-02-03-2.s: A 40-year-old woman has dyspnea on exertion for 6 months. BT 37.4°C, BP 120/80 mmHg, RR 14/min, HR 76/min. The PMI is at the 6th intercostal space, midclavicular line, with a left parasternal heave and a grade III pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla. The jugular veins are flat. EKG shows sinus rhythm, LA enlargement and LVH. What is the most likely diagnosis?

CARDIO-02-03-3.s: A 50-year-old woman has progressive dyspnea on exertion. SpO2 96%. Examination shows an irregular pulse, loud P2, a grade III diastolic rumbling murmur at the apex, crepitation in both lungs and hepatomegaly. What is the most likely underlying cause?
CARDIO-02-03-3.p: MS ในผู้ใหญ่ไทย = rheumatic จนกว่าจะพิสูจน์ได้ว่าไม่ใช่

CARDIO-02-03-4.s: A 57-year-old woman has progressive dyspnea for 6 months. RR 27/min. Examination shows engorged jugular veins, a grade 2/6 pansystolic murmur radiating to the axilla, crackles at both lung bases and pitting edema of both legs. What is the most likely valvular diagnosis?
CARDIO-02-03-4.p: ร้าวไป axilla = ลิ้น mitral แม้จะมี right HF ร่วม

CARDIO-02-04-1.s: A 62-year-old man with long-standing COPD and pulmonary hypertension develops a new high-pitched early diastolic decrescendo murmur at the left second intercostal space. Which valvular lesion is most likely?
CARDIO-02-04-1.p: Pulmonary HT → PR (diastolic ที่ L 2nd ICS)

CARDIO-02-04-2.s: A 50-year-old woman with long-standing left-sided heart failure now has a holosystolic murmur at the left fourth intercostal space, elevated JVP with prominent v waves and a pulsatile liver. What is the most likely mechanism of the new murmur?
CARDIO-02-04-2.a: Functional tricuspid regurgitation from right ventricular dilation
CARDIO-02-04-2.p: TR ส่วนใหญ่เป็น functional จาก RV dilation

CARDIO-02-05-1.s: A 20-year-old woman had a transient loss of consciousness. Beforehand she felt lightheaded, nauseated and had blurred vision. She had a few myoclonic jerks and fully recovered within 30 seconds. There is no orthostatic hypotension, PR 80/min, RR 16/min and no neurological deficit. What is the most useful investigation?
CARDIO-02-05-1.p: Myoclonic jerk สั้น ๆ + ฟื้นเร็ว + prodrome vagal = vasovagal ไม่ใช่ seizure

CARDIO-02-05-2.s: An 82-year-old woman feels dizzy and briefly loses consciousness when she gets up at night to urinate. She has had poor oral intake for several days. Examination confirms orthostatic hypotension. What is the most likely cause?
CARDIO-02-05-2.p: ลุกยืนแล้ววูบ + orthostatic hypotension → หาสาเหตุ hypovolemia/ยา/autonomic

CARDIO-02-05-3.s: A 70-year-old woman has had recurrent syncope over 2 months, typically while lying in bed. Physical examination is unremarkable and the 12-lead EKG is normal. What is the most appropriate investigation?
CARDIO-02-05-3.p: Syncope ตอนนอน = arrhythmia จนกว่าจะพิสูจน์ได้ว่าไม่ใช่ → Holter

CARDIO-02-05-4.s: A 16-year-old student is brought by her mother because she faints repeatedly while standing in the morning school assembly, especially on hot days. Each episode is preceded by nausea, sweating and pallor, and she recovers fully within a minute. What is the most likely cause?
CARDIO-02-05-4.p: ยืนนาน ที่ร้อน + prodrome = vasovagal

CARDIO-02-05-5.s: A 55-year-old man has lightheadedness and near-syncope whenever he uses his left arm to paint a ceiling. Left radial pulse is weaker than the right, and BP is 150/90 mmHg in the right arm and 115/70 mmHg in the left arm. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-02-05-5.p: วูบตอนใช้แขน + BP แขนข้างนั้นต่ำ = subclavian steal

CARDIO-03-01-1.s: A 50-year-old man has headache and dizziness for 3 months. He has no underlying disease, does not drink or smoke, and a check-up earlier this year was normal. Weight 63 kg, height 165 cm. BP 150/95 mmHg, PR 80/min. PMI at the 5th ICS medial to the MCL, normal S1S2, no murmur, normal neurological examination. What is the most appropriate initial management?
CARDIO-03-01-1.a: Lifestyle modification and confirm with home or ambulatory BP monitoring
CARDIO-03-01-1.p: BP สูงครั้งแรก ไม่มี HMOD → ยืนยันนอก รพ. + LSM ก่อน

CARDIO-03-01-2.s: A 45-year-old woman has dizziness and headache. Her home BP readings are consistently above 150/95 mmHg. At the hospital two readings are 138/88 and 135/85 mmHg. She has no diabetes, no cardiovascular disease and no evidence of organ damage. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-03-01-2.a: Lifestyle modification with close home BP follow-up
CARDIO-03-01-2.p: Masked HT = office ปกติ บ้านสูง → LSM, ยาถ้า high risk/HMOD

CARDIO-03-01-3.s: A 60-year-old man on HCTZ and enalapril for HT has office BP around 140–150/90–100 mmHg. He complains of dizziness, especially on changing position. Supine BP is 150/100 mmHg and sitting BP is 140/100 mmHg. BMI 28 kg/m2. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-03-01-3.p: สงสัย orthostatic hypotension หรือ white-coat → HBPM/ABPM

CARDIO-03-02-1.s: A 45-year-old man with type 2 diabetes has BP 160/90 mmHg on repeated measurements. Physical examination is normal. Urinalysis shows protein 2+ and glucose 3+. Which antihypertensive drug should be included in his regimen?

CARDIO-03-02-2.s: A patient with both type 2 diabetes and COPD with frequent wheezing needs an antihypertensive drug. He has no proteinuria. Which drug is most suitable?

CARDIO-03-02-3.s: A 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and HT is taking enalapril 40 mg/day. BP is 150/100 mmHg, FBS 120 mg/dL, HbA1c 6.5%. Urine dipstick shows protein 2+. EKG shows LVH. Which medication should be added?
CARDIO-03-02-3.p: ACEI เต็มขนาดแล้ว → เพิ่ม CCB/thiazide ไม่ใช่เพิ่ม ARB

CARDIO-03-02-4.s: A patient with HT on enalapril 20 mg/day and amlodipine 10 mg/day presents with bilateral ankle edema. BP 120/80 mmHg. Pitting edema 1+ both feet. BUN 15 mg/dL, Cr 0.8 mg/dL. Urinalysis is normal. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-03-02-4.p: ขาบวมจาก amlodipine → ลด/หยุดยา ไม่ใช่ให้ diuretic

CARDIO-03-02-5.s: A 75-year-old woman with diabetes is started on enalapril 10 mg/day for BP 170/110 mmHg. Two weeks later her BP is 150/100 mmHg but serum creatinine has risen from 1.0 to 1.5 mg/dL. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-03-02-5.a: Discontinue enalapril and recheck creatinine in 1 week
CARDIO-03-02-5.p: ACEI/ARB: Cr ขึ้น > 30% → หยุดยา + หา RAS

CARDIO-03-03-1.s: A 60-year-old man with long-standing HT and coronary artery disease presents with recurrent sudden pulmonary edema. BP left arm 190/105 mmHg, right arm 185/100 mmHg. There is no murmur, an S4 gallop, crackles at both lung bases and an abdominal bruit. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-03-03-1.p: Flash pulmonary edema + abdominal bruit = RAS

CARDIO-03-03-2.s: A 70-year-old man is newly found to have HT and is started on enalapril. He returns with puffy eyelids, edema and pulmonary edema. BUN 20 mg/dL, Cr 4.1 mg/dL, urine specific gravity 1.010. What is the most appropriate investigation for the diagnosis?
CARDIO-03-03-2.a: Doppler ultrasound of the renal arteries
CARDIO-03-03-2.p: AKI หลังเริ่ม ACEI → Doppler US renal arteries

CARDIO-03-03-3.s: A 25-year-old woman has intermittent headache, lightheadedness and palpitation for 1 year. Her BP is high both sitting and supine. Examination shows tremor, sweating and pallor during an episode. What is the most appropriate initial investigation?
CARDIO-03-03-3.p: Headache + palpitation + sweating เป็นพัก ๆ = pheo → metanephrines

CARDIO-03-03-4.s: A 35-year-old man has headache for 1 month and today has weakness of all four limbs while fully conscious. BP 190/100 mmHg, PR 78/min. Proximal muscle power is grade II/V in all extremities. What is the most appropriate initial investigation?
CARDIO-03-03-4.p: HT + อ่อนแรงต้นแขนขา → เจาะ K (Conn)

CARDIO-03-03-5.s: A 20-year-old man has headache and vomiting for 5 days. BP 170/105 mmHg, PR 80/min. Fundoscopy shows retinal artery narrowing. Na 145, K 3.9, Cl 99, HCO3 30 mEq/L. Urinalysis shows albumin 3+ and RBC 10–20/HPF. What is the most likely cause of his hypertension?
CARDIO-03-03-5.p: HT อายุน้อย + proteinuria + hematuria = GN

CARDIO-03-04-1.s: A 45-year-old man has severe headache for 1 day and episodic palpitation 1–2 times a day for 1–2 months. He was previously prescribed antihypertensives for BP 200/120 mmHg but took them irregularly. Now BP 210/130 mmHg, PR 120/min, RR 22/min. Fundoscopy shows flame-shaped hemorrhages and early papilledema. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-03-04-1.p: Papilledema/retinal hemorrhage + BP สูงมาก = malignant HT → IV drug

CARDIO-03-04-2.s: A patient with CKD stage 4 presents with BP 220/110 mmHg and no other specific symptoms. Ophthalmoscopy shows hemorrhages, cotton-wool spots and papilledema. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-03-04-2.p: HT emergency + CKD → nicardipine (เลี่ยง nitroprusside)

CARDIO-03-04-3.s: A 50-year-old man with CKD stage IV and poorly controlled HT comes for a routine follow-up. He has no symptoms. BP 210/130 mmHg, PR 80/min, RR 18/min. He has an LV heave, S4 gallop, no murmur, clear lungs and 1+ pitting edema. Fundoscopy shows only arteriolar narrowing. What is the most appropriate initial management?
CARDIO-03-04-3.p: LVH/S4 ปอดใส = chronic ไม่ใช่ acute damage → urgency → oral

CARDIO-03-04-4.s: A 58-year-old woman with HT presents with BP 230/130 mmHg, severe headache, confusion and vomiting. CT brain shows no hemorrhage or infarct. What is the appropriate goal of blood pressure reduction in the first hour?
CARDIO-03-04-4.a: Reduce mean arterial pressure by no more than 25%
CARDIO-03-04-4.p: HT emergency: MAP ลด ≤ 25% ในชั่วโมงแรก ยกเว้น dissection

CARDIO-04-01-1.s: A 20-year-old man has low-grade fever, myalgia and chest pain for 1 day. The chest pain improves when he leans forward. Examination shows normal S1S2, no murmur, no cardiomegaly and a friction rub at the apex. What is the most appropriate management?

CARDIO-04-01-2.s: An 18-year-old woman has chest pain that improves when she leans forward. Lungs are clear and a friction rub is present. EKG shows ST elevation in all chest leads with PR segment depression. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-04-01-2.p: Diffuse STE + rub ในคนอายุน้อย = pericarditis ห้าม thrombolysis

CARDIO-04-01-3.s: A 50-year-old man has chronic cough and dyspnea for 1 month. BT 38.5°C, BP 100/60 mmHg, PR 80/min, RR 18/min. There is a pericardial friction rub and soft S1. Pericardial fluid is straw-coloured with WBC 2,000 cells/mm3 (N 30%, L 70%), ADA 100 U/L and no organisms on Gram stain. Besides specific treatment, which drug can prevent long-term complications?
CARDIO-04-01-3.p: TB pericarditis + steroid → กัน constrictive pericarditis

CARDIO-04-01-4.s: A 30-year-old man has dyspnea for 1 month. He has a past history of pulmonary tuberculosis. Examination shows neck vein engorgement that rises further on inspiration, clear and equal breath sounds, hepatomegaly and an early diastolic extra sound. EKG shows diffuse ST-T changes and low voltage. Echocardiogram shows a thickened pericardium without significant effusion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-04-01-4.p: Kussmaul + pericardial knock + เยื่อหุ้มหนา = constrictive

CARDIO-04-02-1.s: A 62-year-old woman with lung cancer has progressive dyspnea. BP 118/72 mmHg, no pulsus paradoxus. Chest X-ray shows an enlarged, globular heart with clear lung fields. EKG shows QRS amplitude of 4 mm in the limb leads and 8 mm in the precordial leads with alternating QRS heights. What is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?
CARDIO-04-02-1.p: สงสัย pericardial effusion → echo

CARDIO-04-02-2.s: A 45-year-old man on maintenance hemodialysis has a chest X-ray showing a markedly enlarged cardiac silhouette. Which combination of EKG findings best supports a large pericardial effusion?
CARDIO-04-02-2.a: Low QRS voltage with electrical alternans
CARDIO-04-02-2.p: Low voltage + electrical alternans = large effusion

CARDIO-04-03-1.s: A woman with breast cancer, post modified radical mastectomy and chemotherapy, has progressive dyspnea for 2 weeks. JVP is raised up to the angle of the mandible. While deflating the BP cuff, Korotkoff sounds are heard intermittently at 100 mmHg and clearly with every beat at 80 mmHg. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-04-03-1.p: Korotkoff เป็นช่วงแล้วต่อเนื่องห่างกัน > 10 mmHg = pulsus paradoxus

CARDIO-04-03-2.s: A 40-year-old woman has dyspnea on exertion. BP 90/60 mmHg, PR 110/min, RR 24/min, JVP 20 cmH2O. Lungs are clear with equal breath sounds and no adventitious sounds. Heart sounds are of low intensity and there is 1+ pitting edema. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-04-03-2.p: JVP สูง + ปอดใส + BP ต่ำ + เสียงหัวใจเบา = tamponade

CARDIO-04-03-3.s: A patient with stage IIIA breast cancer presents with dyspnea. BP 70/40 mmHg. Examination shows neck vein engorgement, equal breath sounds in both lungs, decreased S1S2 and no murmur. After initial resuscitation, what is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-04-03-3.p: Tamponade: pericardiocentesis คือการรักษา ยาเป็นแค่สะพาน

CARDIO-04-03-4.s: A 45-year-old man with lung cancer on chemotherapy has dizziness for 1 week. BT 36.5°C, BP 80/50 mmHg, RR 12/min. JVP is raised to the mid-cervical level, heart sounds are decreased and the lungs are clear. EKG shows generalized low voltage. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-04-03-4.p: Low voltage + JVP สูง + hypotension ในคนมะเร็ง = tamponade

CARDIO-04-04-1.s: A 60-year-old man develops severe chest pain radiating to the back while driving. He has HT and smokes, with GERD and COPD. BP 190/100 mmHg, PR 110/min, SpO2 98%. He is distressed; the left radial pulse is weaker than the right, JVP is flat, S1S2 normal, no murmur, breath sounds normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-04-04-1.p: Pulse/BP สองแขนต่างกัน = dissection จนกว่าพิสูจน์ได้ว่าไม่ใช่

CARDIO-04-04-2.s: A 70-year-old man has sudden chest pain radiating to the back. BP 170/100 mmHg. The pulse in the left arm and both legs is weak or absent. What is the most appropriate initial medication?
CARDIO-04-04-2.p: Dissection: BB ก่อนเสมอ

CARDIO-04-04-3.s: A 70-year-old man with DM and HT has chest pain radiating to the back 30 minutes before arrival. While waiting he develops right-sided weakness. BP right arm 130/60 mmHg, left arm 200/100 mmHg, HR 86/min. He has dysarthria, left facial palsy, right hemiplegia and a right Babinski sign. EKG shows sinus rhythm with LVH. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-04-04-3.p: Stroke + เจ็บอกร้าวหลัง + BP สองแขนต่าง → คิด dissection ห้าม rt-PA

CARDIO-04-04-4.s: A 50-year-old man with poorly controlled HT has severe progressive chest pain radiating to the back for 1 hour. BP 100/80 mmHg. Pulses are regular, 2+ in the upper limbs and 1+ in the lower limbs. Creatinine is 2.8 mg/dL and he is hemodynamically unstable. Which imaging is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?
CARDIO-04-04-4.p: Dissection + unstable หรือไตวาย → TEE

CARDIO-04-04-5.s: A middle-aged man has sudden chest pain. BP is 173/110 mmHg in the right arm and 153/100 mmHg in the left arm. CTA confirms aortic dissection. What is the most appropriate management?

CARDIO-05-01-1.s: A 55-year-old man has a 3-month history of intermittent pressure-like chest tightness that occurs with exertion and is relieved by rest. He has HT and DLP but no previous cardiac events. Examination is unremarkable and the resting EKG is normal. What is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?
CARDIO-05-01-1.p: Stable angina PTP ปานกลาง–สูง → CCTA/stress test ก่อน CAG

CARDIO-05-01-2.s: A 50-year-old man has chest tightness radiating to both sides of the mandible when climbing stairs, relieved by 10 minutes of rest. He has HT with poor adherence and smokes 3–4 cigarettes a day for 10 years. BP 160/90 mmHg, HR 80/min, RR 18/min. Besides aspirin and a statin, which antihypertensive drug is most appropriate?

CARDIO-05-01-3.s: A 50-year-old man has no history of heart disease, no symptoms and does not exercise. He asks which physical activity would best help prevent cardiovascular disease. What should you recommend?
CARDIO-05-01-3.a: Brisk walking 30 minutes, 5 days per week
CARDIO-05-01-3.p: ≥ 150 นาที/สัปดาห์ moderate aerobic

CARDIO-05-02-1.s: A 40-year-old man with high ASCVD risk has intermittent chest tightness and shortness of breath for 2 weeks. EKG shows ST depression in leads II, III and aVF. Troponin-T is 0.12 ng/mL (normal < 14 ng/L). What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-05-02-1.p: แปลงหน่วย troponin ก่อนเทียบ: 0.12 ng/mL = 120 ng/L

CARDIO-05-02-2.s: A 62-year-old man has 1 hour of crushing chest pain. EKG shows 3 mm ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with ST depression in I and aVL. BP is 82/50 mmHg, JVP is elevated and the lungs are clear. Which additional investigation should be done immediately?
CARDIO-05-02-2.p: Inferior STEMI + hypotension + ปอดใส → V4R หา RV infarct

CARDIO-05-02-3.s: A 58-year-old woman has 40 minutes of chest pressure. EKG shows ST elevation of 3 mm in leads V2–V4 with ST depression in II, III and aVF. Which coronary artery is most likely occluded?
CARDIO-05-02-3.p: V1–V4 = LAD · II, III, aVF = RCA · I, aVL, V5–6 = LCX

CARDIO-05-02-4.s: A 66-year-old man has had chest discomfort for 5 hours. EKG shows no ST elevation. High-sensitivity troponin T at 0 hours is above the 99th percentile URL. Using the 0/3-hour algorithm, which change at 3 hours confirms NSTEMI?
CARDIO-05-02-4.a: A change of more than 20% from the 0-hour value
CARDIO-05-02-4.p: 0/3 ชม.: เกิน ULN → > 20% · ต่ำกว่า ULN → > 50%

CARDIO-05-03-1.s: A 45-year-old Thai man develops chest tightness while watching TV. He is a heavy smoker with DM and DLP. BP 140/70 mmHg, HR 100/min, SpO2 98% on room air. EKG shows ST elevation in V1–V3. Among the following, what is the most appropriate initial management?
CARDIO-05-03-1.p: STEMI SpO2 ปกติ → aspirin ไม่ใช่ O2

CARDIO-05-03-2.s: A 45-year-old man with DM and heavy smoking has severe chest pain for 1 hour. BP 100/70 mmHg, PR 110/min. EKG shows ST elevation in V1–V4 with ST depression in II, III and aVF. The nearest PCI centre is 150 minutes away. After aspirin and clopidogrel, what is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-05-03-2.p: STEMI + PCI > 120 นาที = fibrinolysis

CARDIO-05-03-3.s: A 60-year-old man with inferior STEMI is in a hospital where primary PCI is available within 60 minutes. He has received aspirin. Which antithrombotic combination is most appropriate before PCI?
CARDIO-05-03-3.p: Primary PCI: ASA + P2Y12 (ตัวไหนก็ได้) + heparin

CARDIO-05-03-4.s: A 64-year-old man with inferior STEMI has BP 86/54 mmHg, JVP 12 cm, clear lungs and ST elevation in V4R. He is awaiting primary PCI. Which drug should be avoided?
CARDIO-05-03-4.p: RV infarct: ห้าม nitrate · ให้ IV fluid

CARDIO-05-04-1.s: A patient with chest pain is diagnosed with NSTEMI. He is clinically high risk with dynamic ST-T changes and a GRACE score of 160. He is hemodynamically stable and has received aspirin, ticagrelor and enoxaparin. What is the most appropriate management?
CARDIO-05-04-1.p: NSTEMI high risk → CAG เร็ว ไม่ใช่ fibrinolysis

CARDIO-05-04-2.s: A 65-year-old woman with DM and DLP has palpitation, sweating and left-sided chest tightness for 3 hours. PR 100/min, BP 110/70 mmHg. EKG shows 1.5 mm horizontal ST depression in V4–V6 without ST elevation, and hs-troponin is elevated. She has been given aspirin and clopidogrel. What is the most appropriate next step in treatment?

CARDIO-05-04-3.s: A 70-year-old man has 30 minutes of chest pain at rest that is now relieved. EKG shows T-wave inversion in V2–V4. hs-cTnT at 0 and 1 hour are both below the 99th percentile with no significant change. What is the most likely diagnosis?
CARDIO-05-04-3.p: ACS + troponin ปกติ = UA

CARDIO-05-05-1.s: A 65-year-old man is admitted to the CCU with a massive left ventricular myocardial infarction. On day 6 of admission he suddenly develops cardiac tamponade and dies. What is the most likely cause?
CARDIO-05-05-1.a: Rupture of the left ventricular free wall
CARDIO-05-05-1.p: Tamponade หลัง MI ใหญ่ ~1 สัปดาห์ = free wall rupture

CARDIO-05-05-2.s: A 68-year-old woman is on day 4 after an inferior STEMI treated with fibrinolysis. She suddenly develops severe dyspnea and hypotension. There are bilateral crackles and a new soft holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla. What is the most likely complication?
CARDIO-05-05-2.p: Acute MR + pulmonary edema หลัง inferior MI = papillary muscle rupture

CARDIO-06-01-1.s: A 50-year-old man has dyspnea on exertion and edema for 1 week. He has drunk beer every day for 25 years. BP 120/70 mmHg. There are fine crepitations at both lung bases, the PMI is at the 6th ICS 1 cm lateral to the MCL and an S3 gallop is present. In addition to an IV diuretic, what is the next management?
CARDIO-06-01-1.p: HF ในคนดื่มสุรา → ให้ thiamine

CARDIO-06-01-2.s: A 68-year-old woman with ischemic cardiomyopathy is comfortable at rest but becomes breathless walking across a room or dressing, which is less than ordinary activity. What is her NYHA functional class?
CARDIO-06-01-2.p: NYHA III = เหนื่อยเมื่อทำน้อยกว่าปกติ สบายตอนพัก

CARDIO-06-01-3.s: A 72-year-old man has progressive dyspnea. Which finding most specifically indicates elevated right-sided filling pressure?
CARDIO-06-01-3.a: JVP 5 cm above the sternal angle with a positive hepatojugular reflux
CARDIO-06-01-3.p: JVP + HJR = right side · crepitation/PND/orthopnea = left side
